2dhoYgHiC2.one_liner: Shows chunked KV-cache compression makes retrieval depend on token phase relative to compression windows, traced to phase-specialized attention components.
2dhoYgHiC2.problem: Average long-context retrieval scores can hide token positions relative to compression-window boundaries where retrieval fails under chunked KV-cache compression.
2dhoYgHiC2.method: Measures retrieval accuracy by token phase in the DeepSeek-V4 family, pretrains transformer families from scratch across multiple KV-compression designs to reproduce the effect, applies causal interventions to locate phase-specialized attention components, and analyzes idealized retrieval models for gradient-flow dynamics.
2dhoYgHiC2.key_idea: A token's position modulo the compression stride defines a phase; attention components specialize to phases, so retrieval is asymmetric across phases.
2dhoYgHiC2.evidence: DeepSeek-V4 family (also V4.1), controlled pretraining of 600M-scale Qwen3-derived models with several compression designs, causal interventions, and idealized retrieval models; evaluation relies mainly on synthetic needle-in-a-haystack retrieval per reviews.
2dhoYgHiC2.claimed_gains: Diagnostic paper with no method gains; it reports retrieval accuracy differing by up to 40 percentage points across phases in the DeepSeek-V4 family.
2dhoYgHiC2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the phase-sensitivity finding is interesting and timely, supported by extensive ablations and controlled pretraining where changing compression preferences moves the failures, showing average recall can hide repeating weak positions.
2dhoYgHiC2.main_concern: Evidence is mostly synthetic needle-in-a-haystack retrieval and a few code probes with no standard long-context benchmarks, and the controlled-model explanation is not shown to cause DeepSeek's failures.

fY0in3HE1E.one_liner: Training-free sampler for metric-path discrete flow models choosing the probability flux with minimal transport cost via row-Sinkhorn.
fY0in3HE1E.problem: Few-step sampling of pretrained discrete flow models is underexplored; a sampler can represent at most one jump per token per step, so how much probability moves per step limits quality at low NFE.
fY0in3HE1E.method: The travel-optimal (TO) sampler picks, among the infinitely many rates generating the same probability path, the flux minimizing expected distance traveled by probability mass. This reduces to optimal transport, solved with row-Sinkhorn for the entropic relaxation, plus temporal integration to cut scheduler error.
fY0in3HE1E.key_idea: Exploit non-uniqueness of the jump rate: choose the flux with minimal total travel cost (an entropic OT problem) so few-step samplers move less probability per step.
fY0in3HE1E.evidence: Error analysis bounding sampling error by a term proportional to total travel cost, plus image and video generation experiments against the default sampler (AVE, corrected samplers, and FUDOKI mentioned in reviews).
fY0in3HE1E.claimed_gains: Improves image generation quality over the default sampler by up to 37% in GenEval at low NFE and video generation quality by up to 3.7 (unit cut off in the abstract).
fY0in3HE1E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the sampler is clearly presented and well motivated, exploiting the non-uniqueness of jump rates with concise theory, with clear gains at small cost.
fY0in3HE1E.main_concern: Comparisons with higher-order discrete solvers are missing, applicability is narrow to metric-path discrete flows, and the error bounds are hard to interpret and do not guarantee optimality in the actual sampler.

CjVqkoY5YQ.one_liner: One policy trained across diverse sensor configurations amortizes policy learning so sensor suites can be searched cheaply.
CjVqkoY5YQ.problem: Sensor suites are designed by human intuition and trial and error, and evaluating each candidate by independently training a policy is prohibitively expensive over a combinatorial search space.
CjVqkoY5YQ.method: They train a single Sensor Generalist policy in simulation across diverse sensor configurations and sensing budgets, then use it for lightweight evaluation and search of sensor specifications. Reviewers describe the training as combining RL, privileged-state teacher-student distillation, and reconstruction objectives.
CjVqkoY5YQ.key_idea: Evaluate candidate sensor configurations with one generalist policy trained across sensor configurations instead of training a specialist per configuration.
CjVqkoY5YQ.evidence: Simulated dexterous manipulation with tactile and proprioception sensors, quadruped locomotion with LiDAR-based obstacle avoidance, and transfer of selected sensor configurations to a real-world dexterous manipulation task.
CjVqkoY5YQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree sensor selection is a practical problem and that amortizing policy training across sensor configurations is a compelling way to cut co-design cost, supported by evaluation across tasks, embodiments, and real-world transfer.
CjVqkoY5YQ.main_concern: The efficiency comparison is potentially confounded because specialists are trained from scratch with PPO while the generalist also uses privileged-state distillation and reconstruction, so the gains may not come from amortization or sensor selection alone.

PCE6xKHWVO.one_liner: Couples latent world prediction with VLA action generation through bounded residual feedback and hyperbolic regularization of future features
PCE6xKHWVO.problem: Existing world-model and vision-language-action approaches are structurally decoupled, lacking intrinsic interaction between world prediction and action generation.
PCE6xKHWVO.method: GeoWRA conditions future prediction on the VLA's latent actions and feeds predicted futures back into action generation through bounded world residual feedback. It embeds predicted future states in a Euclidean-hyperbolic product space and trains with a joint action and geometric world objective under hyperbolic regularization.
PCE6xKHWVO.key_idea: Couple future prediction and action generation bidirectionally through bounded, zero-initialized residual feedback, and embed predicted future states in hyperbolic space as a geometric bias.
PCE6xKHWVO.evidence: Multiple simulation benchmarks (SimplerEnv per reviewers) and real-world robotic manipulation tasks, with ablations on bidirectional coupling, geometric supervision and bounded residual feedback.
PCE6xKHWVO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find that feeding predicted futures into the action expert at each denoising step is a useful design, with consistent gains across simulation and real-robot tasks and supporting ablations.
PCE6xKHWVO.main_concern: The contribution of future prediction is not isolated from the extra V-JEPA features, and the motivation and validation of the hyperbolic geometry are weak.

KZGndNHcs6.one_liner: Overlapping Pruning lets neighboring 2:4 selector windows overlap, enlarging the mask space at 2:4 selector count and hardware cost.
KZGndNHcs6.problem: 2:4 semi-structured sparsity degrades LLM quality far more than unstructured 50% pruning because disjoint four-element windows make the mask space rigid.
KZGndNHcs6.method: OP overlaps neighboring selector windows while keeping 2:4's selector count, 50% sparsity, 2-bit index and datapath, and picks masks with a saliency-ordered greedy pass that is exact because feasible masks are independent sets of a transversal matroid.
KZGndNHcs6.key_idea: Rewire each 2:4 selector's unused input to a neighboring window; feasible masks form a transversal matroid, so greedy selection by saliency with a feasibility check is exact.
KZGndNHcs6.evidence: ASAP7 7nm synthesis of the selection hardware at 4-, 8- and 16-bit, and one-shot pruning with Wanda++ evaluated by perplexity on 13 models against 2:4, 4:8, 8:16 and unstructured 50%.
KZGndNHcs6.claimed_gains: OP-F2D increases perplexity by at most 10.4% over unstructured 50% versus up to 59.8% for 2:4, OP-1D beats 4:8 on all 13 models, OP-F2D is within 1.1% of 8:16, and OP-1D and OP-F2D have 0.94-1.04x the delay and 0.96-1.02x the power of 2:4 at matching core area.
KZGndNHcs6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is simple and well motivated, the transversal-matroid argument makes greedy mask selection provably exact, and quality gains are significant across many models.
KZGndNHcs6.main_concern: Hardware evidence covers only the selector network assuming all tile activations reach every selector, so operand supply, full sparse GEMM throughput and support on existing hardware are not shown.

mzf9obZdEx.one_liner: N-GLU combines gated linear units with pre-activation layer normalization to give compute-efficient, stable deep RL networks.
mzf9obZdEx.problem: Under wall-clock-limited RL with parallel simulators, larger networks cost more per step while small ones saturate, and naive GLUs are unstable because multiplicative interactions amplify activation variance and cause feature norm explosion.
mzf9obZdEx.method: N-GLU adds pre-activation layer normalization to a GLU block to stabilize feature magnitudes while keeping multiplicative gating, with theoretical motivation that it yields higher-rank features than standard ReLU blocks.
mzf9obZdEx.key_idea: Normalize before the GLU's multiplicative gating to prevent feature-norm explosion, producing higher-rank features that alleviate plasticity loss.
mzf9obZdEx.evidence: Theory and empirical evidence on feature rank, plus experiments with PQN and FastTD3 on Atari 57, HumanoidBench and MuJoCo Playground, where continuous-control experiments modify only the critic.
mzf9obZdEx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree N-GLU is a simple block that is easy to integrate, with a broad evaluation across discrete and continuous control and an interesting stability analysis.
mzf9obZdEx.main_concern: Novelty over closely related multiplicative architectures such as Hadamax is not established with a controlled comparison, and gains in aggregate continuous-control results are modest.

SbI8ap4e6o.one_liner: Diagnoses long-conversation collapse of full-duplex speech models and fixes it by pinning the first KV entry and penalizing echoing.
SbI8ap4e6o.problem: Full-duplex speech models generate a token every frame and exhaust their context within minutes, and existing benchmarks cover only single or few-turn conversations so long-horizon failures go unmeasured.
SbI8ap4e6o.method: Introduces FD-LHB, a long-horizon benchmark on five models with replayed and live conversations, identifies Initialization-Anchor Eviction and self-reinforced repetition in sliding-window models, and applies training-free Initialization-Anchor Pinning (IAP) and Duplex Repetition Penalty (DRP).
SbI8ap4e6o.key_idea: Keep the first KV entry in the sliding window (IAP) and penalize echoing of recent outputs while guarding against prolonged silence (DRP).
SbI8ap4e6o.evidence: FD-LHB tests five recent full-duplex models on long replayed conversations and in live conversation with an LLM partner, with the diagnosis and fixes evaluated mainly on Moshi and PersonaPlex.
SbI8ap4e6o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree long-horizon full-duplex failure is a practical, under-studied problem, the benchmark is valuable, and the training-free mitigation is simple and clearly presented.
SbI8ap4e6o.main_concern: The mechanism analysis and fixes cover only two sliding-window models from the same family (Moshi and PersonaPlex), leaving the collapse of growing-context models unexplained.

BzSjz4MgZ3.one_liner: CoCA derives criterion-level credits from group-relative outcomes and spreads them across tokens by criterion-induced distribution shifts.
BzSjz4MgZ3.problem: Rubric-based RL compresses criterion-level feedback into scalar rewards with uniform token advantages, and rubric self-distillation signals are not grounded in criterion outcomes and can degrade reward.
BzSjz4MgZ3.method: Treats rubrics as a relevance cue for credit allocation rather than imitation targets, computing criterion-level credits from group-relative outcomes and allocating them across tokens according to how each criterion shifts the token distribution.
BzSjz4MgZ3.key_idea: Token advantages are allocated by how much each rubric criterion shifts the token distribution (with relevance measures such as Jensen-Shannon divergence), weighting group-relative criterion credits.
BzSjz4MgZ3.evidence: Experiments on medicine and science benchmarks against recent baselines, with ablations on the credit allocation mechanism and relevance measures, plus a proposition bounding the hyperparameter beta.
BzSjz4MgZ3.claimed_gains: An average gain of +4.2% over standard rubric-based RL across medicine and science benchmarks.
BzSjz4MgZ3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is timely, allocating credit across tokens by criterion relevance is intuitive, and the ablated experiments show gains of about 4.2% over rubric-based RL.
BzSjz4MgZ3.main_concern: Most gains come from non-uniform credit allocation itself (criterion specificity adds only about a quarter), and beta is one global hyperparameter although the theoretical bounds differ by criterion.

HxsSFmrQ8g.one_liner: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning for MoE LLMs that adapts routing via candidate expert exploration and uncertainty-gated domain knowledge injection.
HxsSFmrQ8g.problem: Existing PEFT methods for MoE LLMs add parameters to experts and ignore the router, so adapted models largely inherit pretraining token-to-expert assignments.
HxsSFmrQ8g.method: RoCA explores potentially task-relevant experts beyond the top-k to shape task-adaptive routing and improve expert utilization, and uses routing uncertainty to adaptively inject domain knowledge. Standard top-k routing is restored at inference.
HxsSFmrQ8g.key_idea: Let candidate experts outside the top-k contribute during training to reshape routing preferences, and gate an added domain expert by routing uncertainty.
HxsSFmrQ8g.evidence: Three MoE backbones (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-V2-Lite, OLMoE-1B-7B) across five domains, with ablations, mixed-domain training and general-capability evaluation.
HxsSFmrQ8g.claimed_gains: Highest average downstream performance while using 5-10x fewer trainable parameters than the second-best method, and improved general capabilities after fine-tuning.
HxsSFmrQ8g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree routing is a practically important aspect of MoE fine-tuning and that candidate exploration is simple and supported by ablations and a reasonably comprehensive evaluation.
HxsSFmrQ8g.main_concern: The central claim that learned routing preferences drive the gains is not isolated, since ablations lack a control with router modulation fixed, and positioning against prior routing-adaptation work is incomplete.

Rj07kKWCZU.one_liner: HD-mapping memory operator whose signed query-memory score uses magnitude to select memories and polarity to route their integration.
Rj07kKWCZU.problem: Temporal HD mappers do not separate relation strength (whether a memory is selected) from relation polarity (how it enters the update), which hurts frame-to-frame stability.
Rj07kKWCZU.method: Triple Correlation Aggregation accumulates content, task-specific correspondence and geometric-temporal evidence into a signed query-memory score, whose magnitude drives sparse memory selection and whose polarity drives branch-specific residual updates. Trackwise Contrastive Regularization is a training-only contrastive regularizer on the shared query-memory embeddings.
Rj07kKWCZU.key_idea: Split one signed query-memory score into magnitude for sparse selection and sign for branch routing, with a training-only contrastive regularizer enforcing trackwise consistency.
Rj07kKWCZU.evidence: Experiments on nuScenes and Argoverse 2 with mapping accuracy and temporal stability metrics, ablations of each component, and comparison to MapTracker.
Rj07kKWCZU.claimed_gains: Gains in mapping accuracy and temporal stability with comparable inference efficiency; no numbers stated in the abstract.
Rj07kKWCZU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the magnitude-and-polarity separation is simple and well targeted, adds no measurable inference cost, and is supported by ablations and stability-oriented metrics.
Rj07kKWCZU.main_concern: Baseline and metric inconsistencies: MapTracker numbers differ across tables, the stability gain depends on a threshold chosen on the validation split with no variance reported, and one reported value exceeds a bound implied by the stated formula.

ZO2H1Fd3l7.one_liner: Serves process-reward verifiers for test-time scaling on edge GPUs by packing shared parent prefixes and relaying nonresident layers.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.problem: Existing TTS serving scores candidates independently and swaps generator and verifier at model granularity, repeating parent-prefix computation and model movement under limited device memory.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.method: RelayTTS treats the live search frontier as the unit of serving: parent-complete score packing evaluates shared prefixes once, a frontier-aware planner trades score-pack capacity against the resident verifier prefix, and layer relay supplies nonresident blocks only during scoring.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.key_idea: Exploit the reasoning-tree frontier to evaluate shared parent prefixes once and keep only part of the verifier resident, streaming the remaining layers only while scoring.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.evidence: Across search procedures and model scales on a single RTX 4090, with generator-verifier pairs up to 7B on mathematics benchmarks and component ablations per reviews.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.claimed_gains: 1.91x gain in effective-token throughput and 47.8% average end-to-end latency reduction, with a maximum reduction of 88.3%.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the system design is well motivated and intuitive, targets the concrete bottlenecks of repeated prefix computation and weight transfer, and shows substantial gains with a solid evaluation.
ZO2H1Fd3l7.main_concern: Limited novelty and coverage: prefix sharing and offloading are well studied with most gains from prefix reuse and residency, and evaluation covers one RTX 4090, models up to 7B and math benchmarks.

vGevyOeTXG.one_liner: Mean-Field Flow generates raw EEG in one step using mean-field token coupling and an average-velocity L1 objective.
vGevyOeTXG.problem: EEG datasets are small and diverse, and image or language generation recipes transfer poorly: latent compression can discard amplitude, phase and transients, attention lacks a shared-source prior, and multi-step samplers are costly.
vGevyOeTXG.method: MFF operates directly on raw EEG, using mean-field token coupling to model channel and temporal interactions through separate shared low-dimensional fields. It is trained with an average-velocity objective via L1 regression, so sampling needs a single forward pass.
vGevyOeTXG.key_idea: Couple tokens through shared low-dimensional channel and temporal fields and regress average velocity with an L1 loss, giving one-step latent-free sampling.
vGevyOeTXG.evidence: 14 public EEG benchmark datasets measured with TS-FID, downstream BCI classification, and signal statistics such as Hjorth parameters, skewness and scalp topographies.
vGevyOeTXG.claimed_gains: Lowest average TS-FID across 14 datasets, reduced by 27.8% relative to the strongest baseline, and 2.80 percentage points higher average BCI classification accuracy.
vGevyOeTXG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the evaluation broad and credible, with downstream augmentation controls, strong results across many datasets, and efficient one-step sampling.
vGevyOeTXG.main_concern: It is unclear the objective truly learns the mean velocity, since the network is not conditioned on the end time, so the one-step sampler may act as a plain regressor.

FjHqeZ4mEb.one_liner: Selects peers for LLM agents with LinUCB over relational features to promote exploration in multi-agent interaction.
FjHqeZ4mEb.problem: LLM agents interacting with one another show myopic, polarized interaction patterns and premature commitment instead of probing peers to infer their capabilities, which leads to suboptimal coordination and higher regret.
FjHqeZ4mEb.method: The paper formalizes Multi-Agent Exploration as a partially observable stochastic game and introduces Multi-Agent Contextual Exploration (MACE), which promotes exploration through structured peer selection. Reviewers describe MACE as LinUCB with a relational feature design applied to peer interaction, and the paper gives a sublinear expected-regret bound.
FjHqeZ4mEb.key_idea: Treat peer selection as a contextual bandit over relational features, so agents deliberately probe peers instead of committing early.
FjHqeZ4mEb.evidence: Contextual diversity (HotpotQA) and parametric diversity (Math500, GPQA) settings, a two-armed delegation study, transfer to 2WikiMultihopQA, and a sublinear expected-regret theorem.
FjHqeZ4mEb.claimed_gains: Exploration behavior and downstream task performance substantially improve with MACE, which has a sublinear expected-regret bound; no numbers stated in the abstract.
FjHqeZ4mEb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find premature commitment in peer selection a relevant failure mode diagnosed well by the controlled delegation study, and MACE straightforward with improvements in both main and transfer experiments.
FjHqeZ4mEb.main_concern: MACE largely builds on LinUCB, simple bandit baselines are missing from the main multi-agent tasks, and heterogeneity type is confounded with benchmark choice.

PEgr8IzJrR.one_liner: Best-arm identification at a target time in drifting bandits using multiresolution pairwise sign estimation within a successive-elimination structure.
PEgr8IzJrR.problem: Existing best-arm identification assumes stationary rewards or chases the largest average over a predefined timespan, whereas the learner must identify the best arm at a target time when rewards drift and the scale of non-stationarity is unknown.
PEgr8IzJrR.method: The paper introduces fixed-budget target-time BAI, studies the limits of identifiability, and proposes an algorithm combining multiresolution pairwise sign estimation with an elimination structure to balance bias and variance without prior knowledge of the drift.
PEgr8IzJrR.key_idea: Test each arm pair's gap sign over several window lengths around the target time, and eliminate arms only on certified rankings, trading bias against variance.
PEgr8IzJrR.evidence: Information-theoretic analysis showing near-optimality up to polylog factors, plus experiments on synthetic and real-world data.
PEgr8IzJrR.claimed_gains: The algorithm is information-theoretically near optimal up to polylog factors and does not require a priori knowledge of drift.
PEgr8IzJrR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the target-time setting well motivated and distinct from stationary BAI, and the algorithm with its minimax-optimality analysis and extensions rigorous.
PEgr8IzJrR.main_concern: The guarantee relies on finite resolving and ranking depths that hold only for instances with certain identifiability properties, and the synthetic experiment setup cannot be reconstructed from the stated stream lengths.

mBcwnxappX.one_liner: Test-time adaptation that couples a corrupted input and its diffusion-restored version through cross-view gating, JS coupling, and entropy-aware logit fusion.
mBcwnxappX.problem: Simply combining model adaptation with input restoration need not beat model adaptation alone, because corrupted inputs lose discriminative evidence while restoration can add biased or misleading cues.
mBcwnxappX.method: Inspired by data assimilation, CoDA treats the corrupted input as an observation and its diffusion-restored counterpart as a prior estimate. Cross-view gating filters updates, selective Jensen-Shannon coupling aligns consistent samples, and entropy-aware logit fusion forms predictions, leaving the underlying TTA objective unchanged.
mBcwnxappX.key_idea: Regulate interaction between the corrupted and restored views with gating, selective JS coupling, and entropy-weighted logit fusion on top of any TTA objective.
mBcwnxappX.evidence: ImageNet-C at severity 5 across five TTA methods and five backbones, plus label shift with batch size one, continual adaptation, ImageNet-R, and ImageNet-3DCC.
mBcwnxappX.claimed_gains: Improves independent data-model adaptation by 2.8 percentage points on average and up to 4.4 points, reaching 54.7% accuracy with ZeroSiam.
mBcwnxappX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is intuitive, works with existing TTA methods without offline training, and shows consistent average gains across TTA methods, backbones, and shift types.
mBcwnxappX.main_concern: Closely related diffusion-based adaptation methods (CMDA and Diffusion-calibrated CTTA) are not directly compared, and the framework mostly combines existing components with unclear per-corruption gains.

eTic76nLQW.one_liner: Post-training binarization for MoE LLMs combining routing-coupled binary factorization, conditional residual allocation, and margin-aware router calibration.
eTic76nLQW.problem: Applying dense-model binarization to MoE LLMs faces decomposition-binarization mismatch, interaction-dependent residual allocation, and quantization-induced expert shift.
eTic76nLQW.method: Routing-Coupled Binary Factorization alternately refines higher-precision shared factors and expert-specific binary factors; Conditional Expert Residual Allocation adds binary residual blocks by conditional reconstruction gain per added storage bit; Margin-Aware Optimal Brain Routing uses boundary-aware curvature to preserve selected-versus-unselected expert margins. All experts are retained and optimization is offline under a storage budget.
eTic76nLQW.key_idea: Optimize shared higher-precision and per-expert binary factors jointly with routing, allocate residual bits by marginal gain, and calibrate the router to keep expert-selection margins.
eTic76nLQW.evidence: Experiments on MoE LLMs (reviews mention Qwen3-30B-A3B and Qwen3-Next-80B) against binary baselines such as BiLLM and ARB-LLM and against GPTQ and AWQ.
eTic76nLQW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three MoE-specific components are well motivated and ablated, and that the method outperforms binary baselines at matched resident storage across MoE models.
eTic76nLQW.main_concern: Baseline fairness is questioned: GPTQ and AWQ results look unusually weak with unreported configurations, and headline gains are measured at matched resident bits rather than the higher active-path bits per token.

MFyJvvmUr8.one_liner: Benchmark comparing ten low-rank pretraining methods under matched-token and matched-FLOPs budgets with measured memory, throughput, and latency.
MFyJvvmUr8.problem: Low-rank pretraining studies use different hardware, scales, implementations, and budgets and report intermediate savings, so end-to-end memory and time efficiency are hard to compare.
MFyJvvmUr8.method: LR-EPB evaluates ten low-rank methods that place structure in weights, optimizer states, or weight updates on LLaMA-style models from 60M to 1B parameters under a shared training setup, measuring quality, training FLOPs, peak memory, throughput, and serving latency.
MFyJvvmUr8.key_idea: Compare methods under explicit matched-token and matched-FLOPs budgets with directly measured system costs, treating efficiency as a resource profile.
MFyJvvmUr8.evidence: 130 runs and approximately 13,000 equivalent A100-40 GPU-hours on LLaMA-style models from 60M to 1B parameters.
MFyJvvmUr8.claimed_gains: Under matched FLOPs, low-rank weight methods can trade lower per-token cost for more training data and close much of their quality gap to full-rank training; no specific figure is given.
MFyJvvmUr8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the explicit budget control and direct measurement of memory, throughput, and FLOPs make the comparison clear and practically useful.
MFyJvvmUr8.main_concern: Single-seed runs with differing tuning procedures cannot establish winners among methods separated by small perplexity gaps, and profiling is limited to a single GPU with short sequences.

HhRC3hBEgh.one_liner: Training-free one-step decoding for world action models by reusing the previous plan's unexecuted suffix as generative state.
HhRC3hBEgh.problem: World Action Models regenerate every action plan from noise even though much of the next plan was already predicted at the previous replan, wasting computation.
HhRC3hBEgh.method: InstantWAM carries the unexecuted suffix into the next planning window, perturbs it back onto the pretrained flow, and corrects it with a single observation-conditioned evaluation, while the WAM's own action attention decides how long the inherited future stays useful. The frozen model is not changed or retrained.
HhRC3hBEgh.key_idea: Treat the unexecuted part of the previous action plan as a persistent generative state, re-noise it onto the pretrained flow, and refine it with one network evaluation.
HhRC3hBEgh.evidence: Simulated manipulation on RoboTwin and LIBERO with a FastWAM backbone, compared against 10-step FastWAM, with latency measured per planner call and per episode.
HhRC3hBEgh.claimed_gains: Average NFEs drop from 10 to 1.62, planner calls are 3.19x faster and episode-level planning 2.47x faster; RoboTwin success is 91.27% versus 91.83% for 10-step FastWAM, and LIBERO reaches 95.75%.
HhRC3hBEgh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and training-free and gives a large planning speedup with success close to the FastWAM baseline.
HhRC3hBEgh.main_concern: Generality is unestablished (one backbone, simulation only), reviewers note uncited prior work such as Falcon and RTI-DP that looks highly similar, and it is unclear the constructed intermediate state matches the pretrained velocity field.

Aqg33sQyTN.one_liner: Synthetic benchmark separating distance extrapolation from count extrapolation of code-fence lengths across recurrent, SSM, attention and hybrid models.
Aqg33sQyTN.problem: LLMs often produce Markdown code fences with broken boundaries (38.0% of valid outputs in nine deployed Transformers), and inference alone cannot show whether a model lacks the needed computation.
Aqg33sQyTN.method: They build Minimal Boundary Transduction (MBT), three synthetic tasks, and train recurrent, SSM, Transformer and hybrid architectures from scratch, testing extrapolation along distance (twelvefold gaps) and count (unseen fence lengths) with controls on learning rate, depth and width.
Aqg33sQyTN.key_idea: Test two extrapolation axes separately, distance and count, on synthetic fence tasks to show recurrence and attention fail in opposite directions (a double dissociation).
Aqg33sQyTN.evidence: 1,216 from-scratch runs that pass an in-distribution gate, learning-rate scans, depth and width controls, ablations such as removing Mamba's selection, and a measurement of eight deployed SSM and hybrid LLMs.
Aqg33sQyTN.claimed_gains: Nonlinear or selective recurrence reaches closing accuracy 0.75 to 1.00 on Distance but at most 0.04 on Count, deep attention stacks reach up to 0.99 on Count, and the two linear time-invariant recurrences stay below 0.30 on Distance.
Aqg33sQyTN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study has thorough controls (per-family learning-rate scans, seeds, depth and width ablations) and cleanly separates two abilities that length-generalization work often conflates.
Aqg33sQyTN.main_concern: The synthetic setup (small models, one token per backtick) may not transfer to real tokenized LLM outputs, and the deployed-model analysis is confounded by scale and training data.

rYmiBu9q81.one_liner: DSG estimates few-shot point-cloud prototypes by EM-style likelihood estimation and adds unsupervised structural anchors as transductive geometric priors.
rYmiBu9q81.problem: In multimodal few-shot point cloud segmentation, support prototypes estimated from few examples may not represent the feature distribution of a new query scene.
rYmiBu9q81.method: Support prototype construction is reformulated as maximum likelihood estimation solved with Expectation Maximization, and unsupervised structural anchors capturing the latent Voronoi structure of the query manifold act as transductive geometric priors, separating semantic likelihood from geometry.
rYmiBu9q81.key_idea: Decouple semantic likelihood (EM-estimated prototypes instead of plain averaging) from geometric priors (unsupervised query anchors) in label prediction.
rYmiBu9q81.evidence: Experiments on S3DIS and ScanNet; reviews cite eight dataset, way and shot settings, a boundary evaluation, and adding the module to MM-FSS and DA-FSS.
rYmiBu9q81.claimed_gains: Reports new best performance on S3DIS and ScanNet for multimodal few-shot point cloud segmentation; the abstract gives no numbers.
rYmiBu9q81.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note consistent gains over all baselines in every reported dataset, way and shot setting, with clear implementation details and stability evidence.
rYmiBu9q81.main_concern: The probabilistic framing is not supported: the EM prototype and structural anchors reduce to single-step k-means after FPS initialization, and the label-independent geometric term cancels in the posterior normalization.

nLcAlGlnsN.one_liner: Release-time framework measuring dataset-property leakage from robot task conditions and protecting them with record-level differentially private release.
nLcAlGlnsN.problem: Released robot task conditions can expose dataset properties such as collection-domain composition even when the demonstration trajectories stay hidden.
nLcAlGlnsN.method: The framework measures dataset-property leakage against adaptive attackers and tests whether protected conditions still control robot behavior. The defense is a record-level differentially private release constrained by public task semantics.
nLcAlGlnsN.key_idea: Release a task condition built under record-level differential privacy anchored to public task semantics, so attackers cannot infer demonstration mixtures while closed-loop control is retained.
nLcAlGlnsN.evidence: Multiple manipulation tasks with adaptive, retrained attackers against perturbation and linear-erasure defenses, closed-loop rollouts in simulation, matched-state interventions, and offline analysis on BridgeData V2 per reviews.
nLcAlGlnsN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a meaningful privacy risk in robot task conditions and evaluates both adaptive attacks and closed-loop task utility with extensive experiments.
nLcAlGlnsN.main_concern: Record-level DP does not directly match the dataset-property threat, public-anchor-only success (Table 11) leaves unclear whether the private release adds information, and closed-loop tests are in simulation only.

y9sRfrKe7T.one_liner: Open mobile-agent stack with simulated commercial apps, SFT trajectories, verifiable RL tasks, and hybrid GUI plus app-native tools.
y9sRfrKe7T.problem: Training capable mobile agents needs open, controllable app environments with verifiable rewards, and interleaving GUI actions with app-native tool calls is largely unexplored.
y9sRfrKe7T.method: MobileGym++ provides 35 commercial-style apps with cross-app workflows and reset and verification control, combined with emulator apps for over 110 apps. The authors curate 12K SFT trajectories and over 2K executable RL tasks with automatic rewards, and add over 300 app-native tools across 50+ apps for a hybrid GUI-tool setting plus MobileGym++ Bench.
y9sRfrKe7T.key_idea: Make apps resettable and checkable on business state, and expose selected app functions as tools so agents interleave GUI actions with tool calls under verifiable RL.
y9sRfrKe7T.evidence: Established benchmarks, MobileGym++ Bench in GUI-only and hybrid settings, and physical devices per reviewers; the visible abstract is cut off before results.
y9sRfrKe7T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a substantial open infrastructure contribution with reusable environments, data, tools, and recipes, evaluated beyond the authors' own simulator.
y9sRfrKe7T.main_concern: Environment fidelity and novelty over existing data cannot be verified (the provided link did not work), hybrid-SFT gains are confounded with extra data, and train-eval overlap in app implementations is unclear.

JzjNi4rkcX.one_liner: GAIN is a backpropagation-free continual test-time adaptation method that scales history-based corrections by a source-relative gain estimate.
JzjNi4rkcX.problem: Confidence and entropy measure self-certainty, but in continual test-time adaptation accumulated target history can become misaligned as the distribution shifts, so it is unclear whether and how strongly to apply a correction.
JzjNi4rkcX.method: GAIN keeps compact target statistics to form a correction proposal, evaluates it with a posterior-predictive evaluator that accounts for estimation uncertainty, and sets a sample-specific intervention strength along a continuous path by one-dimensional optimization. Gain-controlled predictions update the target statistics online without backpropagation, sample storage, or replay.
JzjNi4rkcX.key_idea: History proposes a correction; a posterior-predictive, source-relative gain estimate decides its per-sample intervention strength along a continuous path via 1-D optimization.
JzjNi4rkcX.evidence: Five benchmarks assessing accuracy, calibration, and efficiency, with comparisons to optimization-based baselines such as REM per reviews.
JzjNi4rkcX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reframing test-time reliability as source-relative gain rather than self-confidence is a useful perspective and that the method is lightweight with a favorable accuracy-calibration-efficiency trade-off.
JzjNi4rkcX.main_concern: The evaluator captures finite-sample variance but not bias and implicitly assumes balanced class streams, with no evaluation under class imbalance, label shift, or small batches.

WyVkkjeYVr.one_liner: Lean Finder V2 improves Mathlib semantic search for short ambiguous queries via adversarial query generation for fine-tuning and query rewriting.
WyVkkjeYVr.problem: Existing Mathlib search engines assume context-rich queries, but mathematicians and coding agents issue short, ambiguous queries, and real short queries paired with ground-truth statements are scarce.
WyVkkjeYVr.method: Adversarial training scales up the generation of labeled short, ambiguous queries, which are used both to fine-tune the retriever (model level) and to train query rewriting (input level). Reviews describe the generator reward as gating query difficulty on alignment.
WyVkkjeYVr.key_idea: Adversarially generate hard short queries with an alignment gate and a difficulty window, then train both the retriever and a query rewriter on them.
WyVkkjeYVr.evidence: The human-curated MathlibQR benchmark, unlabeled human and coding-agent queries judged by LLM preference, and a downstream theorem-proving test with Claude Code.
WyVkkjeYVr.claimed_gains: At least 11% relative improvement over the previous best Mathlib semantic search engines on MathlibQR, ranked strongest on unlabeled queries, and improved proof success when integrated with Claude Code.
WyVkkjeYVr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a real data gap with short queries, shows clear gains over existing Mathlib search systems, and backs them with careful ablations.
WyVkkjeYVr.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited (adversarial synthetic-query training has precedent), and downstream evidence is thin: one 100-problem proving benchmark with a 3.3-point gap, no significance test, and LLM-only preference judging.

AK3pqh3T6S.one_liner: Proves that the low-frequency simplicity neural networks prefer differs irreducibly from symbolic description-length simplicity over Boolean functions.
AK3pqh3T6S.problem: It is unclear whether the simple functions neural networks favor are the ones humans find simple as short symbolic rules, so simplicity bias may not help symbolically simple targets.
AK3pqh3T6S.method: Theory over Boolean functions compares Fourier frequency with symbolic description length, showing almost every Boolean function has a longer description than parity yet lower frequency. Experiments train MLPs and a Transformer on targets of matched symbolic cost or spectral profile, including an exhaustive study of all four-bit functions under seven grammars.
AK3pqh3T6S.key_idea: Compare spectral (frequency) complexity with minimum symbolic description length across Boolean functions to show the two orderings diverge, then test learning order under matched fits.
AK3pqh3T6S.evidence: Proofs on Boolean functions, an exhaustive four-bit study, and training experiments where MLPs and a Transformer fit a compact parity rule and a random function equally well.
AK3pqh3T6S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is well framed and the investigation rigorous, with exact enumeration of four-bit functions and controlled comparisons that vary symbolic cost and spectral structure separately.
AK3pqh3T6S.main_concern: The conclusion is seen as largely consistent with known spectral bias and parity hardness, the matched training experiments use only four-variable targets, and the competition experiment may confirm a known bias rather than separate brevity from frequency.

ZnkSl1SEex.one_liner: NuRA adapts LLM hidden states at test time by minimizing angular dispersion over the numerical geometry of pretrained number representations.
ZnkSl1SEex.problem: Reliable numerical prediction remains difficult for LLMs despite advances in mathematical reasoning.
ZnkSl1SEex.method: The paper finds that pretrained numeric output representations have angular relationships tied to magnitude and digit patterns (the Numerical Manifold). NuRA adapts hidden representations by minimizing angular dispersion so probability concentrates on aligned numerical directions, without labeled test data or additional offline training.
ZnkSl1SEex.key_idea: Use the angular geometry of numeric token directions in the unembedding as a label-free loss, minimizing angular dispersion of the predicted number distribution.
ZnkSl1SEex.evidence: Numerical, mathematical-reasoning, and visual tasks across model families (including Llama-3.2-3B on GSM8K and Qwen2.5-VL-3B per reviews), with permutation controls and an error-detection AUROC analysis.
ZnkSl1SEex.claimed_gains: Broad accuracy gains with updates to approximately 0.01% of MLP parameters.
ZnkSl1SEex.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using pretrained numerical geometry as a label-free test-time adaptation signal is interesting, goes beyond plain entropy, and gives measurable gains across numerical, reasoning, and visual tasks.
ZnkSl1SEex.main_concern: Key controls are missing, notably an aggregate matched numeric-token entropy-minimization baseline, and reliance on fixed pretrained geometry may mislead on inputs where the relevant number relations differ, with possible overconfidence.

sALJJnJFFX.one_liner: Test-time method that resamples video frames in a second pass using a frozen MLLM's answer uncertainty and temporal attention.
sALJJnJFFX.problem: MLLMs see only a few frames of long videos; uniform sampling misses brief decisive events and separate frame selectors may be weaker than the base MLLM.
sALJJnJFFX.method: Starting from a uniform grid of F frames, STR builds a new sampling density from the MLLM's temporal attention and triggers a budget-matched second pass only when the answer is uncertain and attention is focused. STR-Refine gates repeated observations and accumulates relevance, and STR-Lite reduces visual-token cost.
sALJJnJFFX.key_idea: Gate a second pass on answer uncertainty plus focused temporal attention, then resample frames by inverse-CDF of the attention-derived density.
sALJJnJFFX.evidence: Per the reviews, experiments cover several MLLM backbones, medium and long videos, latency-accuracy trade-offs, and an evidence-localization control; benchmark names are not visible in the provided text.
sALJJnJFFX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree STR is simple, training-free, and plug-and-play, reusing the frozen answerer's uncertainty and attention without a separate selector, with gains on medium and long videos.
sALJJnJFFX.main_concern: Threshold and readout-layer settings may have been tuned on the evaluation benchmarks, the Table 1 frame budget is not matched to frame-selection baselines, and the conceptual advance over prior adaptive frame selection is limited.

3nIgOGSdxt.one_liner: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting that replaces learned 3D networks with fixed local grid averaging and a small pointwise MLP.
3nIgOGSdxt.problem: Feed-forward 3DGS methods aggregate multi-view evidence with heavy learned 3D networks, which cost runtime and memory.
3nIgOGSdxt.method: LoCoSplat splats a 16-d linear projection of point features into a fine and a coarse grid, then reads both back at each anchor with a 0.14M-parameter pointwise MLP that predicts scale, rotation, and opacity. It has no learned 3D network and no dynamic sparse computation, so the whole encoder runs as one fp16 CUDA graph.
3nIgOGSdxt.key_idea: A Gaussian is a local primitive, so a fixed local average of neighbouring point features at two grid scales supplies the 3D context needed for scale, rotation, and opacity.
3nIgOGSdxt.evidence: Evaluated on RealEstate10K at 6, 12, and 24 views against nine feed-forward methods including VolSplat, with zero-shot transfer to ACID, fine-tuning on ScanNet, and ablations using paired per-scene comparisons and repeated seeds.
3nIgOGSdxt.claimed_gains: Best SSIM and LPIPS at 6, 12, and 24 views and best PSNR at 6 and 12 views on RealEstate10K; +0.6 PSNR over VolSplat at 6 and 12 views, +3.3 at 24 views (+0.17 once VolSplat is retrained with the plane-sweep setting); 33 ms for a 6-view scene, 4.2x faster than the previous state of the art.
3nIgOGSdxt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of how much learned 3D capacity is needed well motivated, and credit the simple design for clear runtime and memory gains and strong image quality.
3nIgOGSdxt.main_concern: The 24-view margin over VolSplat is over-claimed because the gap traces to a plane-sweep candidate count, and a fair full-budget retrained VolSplat comparison is missing.

2bOu5RxCkD.one_liner: MeasureNet predicts K-point polylines along an object's principal axis to measure length directly, without dense segmentation.
2bOu5RxCkD.problem: Length measurement pipelines usually derive length from dense segmentation masks, which are expensive to annotate even though only length is needed.
2bOu5RxCkD.method: A polyline is a sequence of K points along an object's principal axis, and MeasureNet predicts it directly using specialized measurement-aware loss functions. The paper also introduces CeDeM, a newly curated duodenal biopsy dataset with application to celiac disease detection.
2bOu5RxCkD.key_idea: Replace dense mask supervision with sparse K-point polyline annotations, and train with measurement-aware losses so the predicted polyline length matches the true length.
2bOu5RxCkD.evidence: Evaluated on five datasets spanning brightfield and fluorescence microscopy, optical coherence microscopy, CT, and H&E histopathology (including CeDeM), against segmentation models trained on dense masks at a matched annotation budget.
2bOu5RxCkD.claimed_gains: Reduces length measurement MAE by up to 30 points versus segmentation models trained on dense masks when controlled for annotation budget.
2bOu5RxCkD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the measurement objective is practical, that predicting the line directly is sensible given annotation cost, and that the CeDeM dataset is a useful contribution.
2bOu5RxCkD.main_concern: The evaluation is inconsistent with the polyline definition and does not enforce one-to-one instance matching, and novelty over existing direct-measurement methods and loss combinations is unclear.

dF36jNvp1t.one_liner: A long-horizon benchmark of 50 transistor-level analog circuit design tasks scored by an isolated, specification-based verifier.
dF36jNvp1t.problem: It is unclear whether coding agents that sustain hours-long tool loops can carry analog and mixed-signal circuits to electrical specification.
dF36jNvp1t.method: Agents work with an open-source simulator on 50 tasks contributed by 17 chip designers, while an isolated verifier runs specification-based electrical tests on the submitted circuit. The authors then test time budget, reasoning effort, agent harness, and supplied design knowledge as interventions.
dF36jNvp1t.key_idea: Score agent-submitted circuits with a protected, specification-based electrical verifier over two-hour attempts, so success means meeting full electrical specs rather than producing a legal netlist.
dF36jNvp1t.evidence: 24 agent configurations across 3,600 two-hour attempts, with failure analysis and interventions on time, reasoning effort, harness, skill documents, and task-matched reference topologies.
dF36jNvp1t.claimed_gains: Full-specification pass rates range from 5.3% to 98.7%; supplying a task-matched reference topology raises DeepSeek V4 Pro by 18.0 percentage points.
dF36jNvp1t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the expert-built, practically relevant benchmark with isolated verification and a broad evaluation of many open and closed models.
dF36jNvp1t.main_concern: Evaluation scope is limited (no layout evaluation, few small or newer models), and the long-horizon framing is not separated from extra search and simulation time.

AQqnGTFday.one_liner: World-action model that closes the prediction-observation-action loop with observation-corrected belief states, writable memory, and port-Hamiltonian latent dynamics.
AQqnGTFday.problem: Refreshing an image context in world-action models does not explicitly correct a persistent predicted state when contact outcomes diverge from the rollout.
AQqnGTFday.method: At each policy call, the previous belief, memory, and executed action form a prior, and the new observation supplies an innovation that corrects the belief and memory before the next action chunk. A port-Hamiltonian-inspired latent field separates autonomous, action-conditioned, and predicted-contact terms, and scheduled rollout training feeds real and self-generated visual features through the same belief-update path.
AQqnGTFday.key_idea: Apply a prior-plus-innovation belief correction inside the world model so predicted state is repaired by each observation, and train on self-generated rollouts through that same update path.
AQqnGTFday.evidence: Four LIBERO suites, 24 RoboCasa-GR1 tasks, and seven real-world Unitree G1 tasks, with ablations of belief correction and scheduled rollout training.
AQqnGTFday.claimed_gains: 99.2% average success on four LIBERO suites versus 98.6% for the released DiT4DiT checkpoint; 67.50% (2430/3600) versus 56.7% (680/1200) on 24 RoboCasa-GR1 tasks, a 10.8-point difference; removing belief correction or scheduled rollout training lowers RoboCasa-GR1 success by 3.7 or 4.1 points.
AQqnGTFday.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is meaningful and the results are strong, with controlled comparisons and ablations in simulation and on a real humanoid.
AQqnGTFday.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited because the components (belief correction, memory, structured dynamics, closed-loop training) have close precedents, and it is unclear which components are essential.

uXMvBKVv3M.one_liner: Representation-invariant metric comparing the motions that one-DOF joints induce, via unordered pairs of Lie-algebra endpoint twists.
uXMvBKVv3M.problem: Existing protocols score joint type, axis direction, origin, and limits separately although they jointly describe one motion, so equivalent encodings of a joint can score maximally wrong and component errors become ill-conditioned where predictions are accurate.
uXMvBKVv3M.method: Represents each joint by the unordered pair of its Lie-algebra endpoint twists, proves the resulting quotient distance is a metric, unifies fixed, revolute, prismatic, and helical joints, and brings continuous joints in through a compactification. Weighted by mass distribution it reads as the RMS motion of the moving part in meters.
uXMvBKVv3M.key_idea: Compare the motion a joint induces (its endpoint twists in the Lie algebra) rather than the parameters that encode it, giving an encoding-invariant quotient metric.
uXMvBKVv3M.evidence: A proof that the quotient distance is a metric; per the reviews, controlled perturbation demonstrations and calibration of the single-joint metric (abstract is truncated).
uXMvBKVv3M.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract is truncated before any empirical results.
uXMvBKVv3M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the metric addresses an overlooked evaluation problem by treating equivalent joint encodings and edge cases in a principled, theoretically grounded way.
uXMvBKVv3M.main_concern: The metric is not identical to true SE(3) motion error (linearization error), and object-level behavior under coupled errors and joint-part binding is insufficiently validated.

A4D0Gz5VV2.one_liner: Benchmarks causal foundation models across observational views of one fixed SCM and estimand, each view implying a different identification regime.
A4D0Gz5VV2.problem: Differences in pretraining environments and evaluation protocols make it hard to assess how causal foundation models depend on the information available for causal identification.
A4D0Gz5VV2.method: CausalIDView holds the SCM realization and target estimand fixed while varying only the observational view, so each view matches a distinct identification regime. It adds stability diagnostics (Stay/Move tests and error decomposition per reviews) and a modular baseline pairing a predictive tabular foundation model with regime-specific identification procedures.
A4D0Gz5VV2.key_idea: Hold the SCM and estimand fixed while changing only which variables are observed, so performance differences isolate the identification regime.
A4D0Gz5VV2.evidence: Synthetic, semi-synthetic, and real-world datasets comparing several causal foundation models and classical estimators; the real-world tests cover only null effects (per reviews).
A4D0Gz5VV2.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that no CFM is consistently best across views and that the modular approach is competitive with CFMs and outperforms several of them.
A4D0Gz5VV2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired, controlled multi-view benchmark design is valuable and that CFMs failing to beat simpler identification approaches is an informative finding.
A4D0Gz5VV2.main_concern: Benchmark scope is narrow (binary confounder, complete mediation, null-effect real-world tests), and CFMs such as CausalPFN are applied to regimes they were not designed for, so some poor results are expected.

xmJrldZD2r.one_liner: Shows RL post-training of flow-based VLAs makes low-rank parameter updates concentrated in the action expert's Timestep Modules.
xmJrldZD2r.problem: How RL post-training reshapes vision-language-action policies is poorly understood.
xmJrldZD2r.method: Analyzes parameter updates from RL across pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.5/N1.6 on four benchmarks, uses module-replacement experiments that keep only selected RL updates, and probes the Timestep Modules' shift vectors for task success and cross-task relationships.
xmJrldZD2r.key_idea: RL specializes the action expert's Timestep Modules to the discrete denoising timesteps used in rollouts, and this discrete-timestep training underlies the low-rank updates.
xmJrldZD2r.evidence: pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.5/N1.6 on LIBERO, ManiSkill, MetaWorld and CALVIN with module-replacement and probing experiments.
xmJrldZD2r.claimed_gains: In pi_0.5, keeping only Timestep Module RL updates gives performance within 1.6% of the full RL policy with 27.6% of the action expert's parameters, and shift update directions predict task success with ROC-AUC up to 99.6%.
xmJrldZD2r.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the parameter-space perspective interesting, with experiments across several architectures and benchmarks and module-replacement evidence.
xmJrldZD2r.main_concern: The findings may be overgeneralized and not RL-specific: the low-rank structure is tied to fixed discrete denoising timesteps (behavior cloning gives similar updates), and in GR00T N1.5 keeping only timestep-module updates drops success from 90.3% to 61.3%.

4hFaP95dmY.one_liner: Server-side graph hypernetwork generates parameters for heterogeneous client architectures represented as computational graphs, with type-aware decoding.
4hFaP95dmY.problem: Multimodal federated learning struggles with highly heterogeneous client tasks and architectures, often relies on public data for distillation, and has high communication overhead.
4hFaP95dmY.method: Client models built from a predefined operator vocabulary are represented as computational graphs, and a server-side hypernetwork generates architecture-specific parameters, giving implicit parameter sharing without a shared parameter space. Type-aware Decoding conditions parameter generation on operator-specific information.
4hFaP95dmY.key_idea: A graph hypernetwork over operator-typed computational graphs generates each client's parameters, with the shared decoder conditioned on operator type.
4hFaP95dmY.evidence: Three multimodal tasks (image-text retrieval, sentiment recognition, scene recognition) against a broad range of federated baselines, plus an ablation of Type-aware Decoding.
4hFaP95dmY.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy by an average of 3.8% over the strongest baseline and substantially reduces communication time versus existing multimodal federated methods.
4hFaP95dmY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find graph hypernetworks for architecture-heterogeneous clients a promising alternative to parameter aggregation, with consistent gains across three tasks.
4hFaP95dmY.main_concern: The closest hypernetwork baselines (FedMBridge, HAFL-GHN) are not evaluated, and gains from Type-aware Decoding may come from added decoder capacity.

QQwP2rYViT.one_liner: Three LLM agents plan, build and refine region-specific traffic signal controllers using a versioned skill library and decoupled multi-agent RL.
QQwP2rYViT.problem: Traffic demand varies across regions and over time, so a single control algorithm cannot stay stable, and existing approaches rely on predefined principles, specialized architectures or task-specific training.
QQwP2rYViT.method: A planning agent partitions the network into spatiotemporally coupled regions and assigns strategies, a modeling agent builds region-specific control policies, and a skill agent develops reusable analysis and control-development skills kept in a persistent versioned library and scored by downstream traffic improvement. DCMA-RL trains the three agents, starting from supervised cold-start training (abstract truncated).
QQwP2rYViT.key_idea: Close a loop of traffic diagnosis, controller construction, feedback and skill development, with skills retrieved and refined according to their measured downstream traffic improvement.
QQwP2rYViT.evidence: Reviews mention average travel time, throughput, queue length and waiting time metrics and a missing-initial-skills robustness test; datasets are not stated in the abstract.
QQwP2rYViT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is realistic and that integrating planning, modeling and skill agents with a versioned skill library is a coherent, practical design, since LLM reasoning is used during controller development rather than at every control step.
QQwP2rYViT.main_concern: Reviewers say the experiments do not isolate the contributions of LLM reasoning, skill evolution, controller selection or DCMA-RL design choices, and lack related LLM-based baselines and a non-LLM selector over the same controller portfolio.

BBYYq7b8IV.one_liner: Generates text-driven 3D human-object interaction by planning variable-duration action prototypes and modeling their evolution before dense motion synthesis.
BBYYq7b8IV.problem: Text-conditioned HOI generators often omit required actions or execute them with wrong timing or ordering, so motions do not faithfully follow instructions.
BBYYq7b8IV.method: AW3D learns a data-driven vocabulary of interaction stages (Joint-Embedding Action Prototype Learning), decomposes intent into an ordered sequence of action prototypes with durations (Distribution-Guided Action Sequence Decomposition), and generates dense motion with role-guided interaction world modelling for body, hand and object.
BBYYq7b8IV.key_idea: Organize intent into an ordered sequence of learned, variable-duration action prototypes first, then condition role-specific dense motion generation on that plan.
BBYYq7b8IV.evidence: Experiments (InterAct per reviews) with ablations, and integration of the prototype module into several HOI generation methods.
BBYYq7b8IV.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract, which claims state-of-the-art semantic alignment and motion quality; reviewers cite R@3 rising from 0.748 to 0.826 and FID falling from 0.171 to 0.101 against guided LIGHT in Table 1.
BBYYq7b8IV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the stage-based action-prototype formulation is well motivated, targets skipped or reordered actions, and gives strong text-alignment results that carry over to other HOI generators.
BBYYq7b8IV.main_concern: Reviewers say there is no direct test that generated motions follow the planned order, since shuffling prototypes gives slightly higher R@3 than the full model (0.833 vs 0.826), and the semantic coverage of 64 prototypes is unclear.

sgGxNSI0Qj.one_liner: Multi-turn agent for cross-video question answering trained with SFT then RL using information-gain credit on evidence notes.
sgGxNSI0Qj.problem: Cross-video understanding needs evidence located and compared across videos, but fixed frame sampling has no way to supplement or verify evidence as reasoning unfolds.
sgGxNSI0Qj.method: VideoSeeker runs a closed loop of targeted segment replay, temporally interleaved comparison and persistent evidence notes. It is fine-tuned on 4,000 distilled multi-turn trajectories, then trained with RL where note-level information-gain rewards are gated by a visual grounding check.
sgGxNSI0Qj.key_idea: Reward each evidence note by the change in ground-truth log-likelihood it produces, granting positive credit only when the note cites previously observed frames.
sgGxNSI0Qj.evidence: Multiple cross-video benchmarks, model sizes and tool ablations; Table 3 compares against outcome-only GRPO.
sgGxNSI0Qj.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract; a review reports VideoSeeker-9B raising the average score from 50.33 to 63.71 over the base model.
sgGxNSI0Qj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree active evidence seeking is well motivated for cross-video tasks, the framework and trajectory construction are careful, and overall gains over base models are substantial.
sgGxNSI0Qj.main_concern: Note-level credit assignment adds only 0.5-1.0 points over outcome-only GRPO, and the grounding gate checks only that cited frames were observed, not that they support the note.

w6gaVpbL1f.one_liner: Unified framework comparing nine world representations for driving world-action models, with training-time world supervision and action-only inference.
w6gaVpbL1f.problem: How world representations affect planning in world-action models for autonomous driving remains unclear.
w6gaVpbL1f.method: Under a common architecture, ReWAM instantiates inverse dynamics, world and world-action models across nine representations (VAE latents, visual foundation features, driving-specific BEV features) and evaluates them through action recovery, world-action consistency and planning. It also introduces a method that directs world-prediction supervision to action generation during training while keeping action-only inference.
w6gaVpbL1f.key_idea: Compare nine frozen encoders under one architecture, and route world-prediction supervision into action generation during training so inference needs no future generation.
w6gaVpbL1f.evidence: Nine representations evaluated on NAVSIM v1, v2 and navhard through action recovery, world-action consistency and planning, with decoded-video FID and FVD.
w6gaVpbL1f.claimed_gains: Reaches 91.6 PDMS on navtest and 39.3 EPDMS on navhard; the efficient variant retains 91.6 PDMS on navtest at 59 ms, 3.6x faster than inference with future-world generation.
w6gaVpbL1f.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled comparison of nine representations gives practical guidance, shows an advantage for visual foundation features, and that the cache mechanism gives a good latency-accuracy trade-off.
w6gaVpbL1f.main_concern: The world-model metric is confounded by the representation-specific frozen inverse dynamics model, so encoder differences cannot be attributed purely to representation quality, and the world model may recall nuPlan locations.

uAwsyUczIL.one_liner: Training-free activation steering using offset vectors from parallel claim-evidence pairs to restore small VLMs on low-resource multimodal fact verification.
uAwsyUczIL.problem: Small vision-language models suffer a severe, disproportionate accuracy collapse on low-resource languages in multimodal fact verification, and closing the gap normally needs scale or language-specific fine-tuning.
uAwsyUczIL.method: ORBIT estimates span-specific offset vectors from parallel claim-evidence instances and applies them to claim and evidence representations at inference time, targeting degradation induced by low-resource evidence. No gradient updates are used.
uAwsyUczIL.key_idea: Estimate language-offset vectors per span from parallel instances and add them to claim and evidence hidden representations at inference to undo low-resource degradation.
uAwsyUczIL.evidence: 81 claim-evidence language configurations on MOCHEG-XL across three model architectures with separate calibration, validation and test sets, compared with translation-based and steering baselines.
uAwsyUczIL.claimed_gains: Substantially recovers accuracy and F1-score in low-resource settings across 81 configurations and outperforms translation-based and steering baselines, with no further numbers stated.
uAwsyUczIL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled 81-configuration diagnostic, which holds images fixed, cleanly shows an evidence-language-driven collapse across three models, and that ORBIT is a cheap training-free fix.
uAwsyUczIL.main_concern: Evidence that the gains come from cross-lingual realignment is weak: the effect may be a label-bias shift without random-vector or text-only controls, the equations are inconsistent for English claims, and translation baselines use weaker translators than ORBIT's calibration.

yJipgniOxV.one_liner: Geometry-aware setwise ranker that selects facial surgery visualizations from fixed diffusion candidate pools without postoperative ground truth.
yJipgniOxV.problem: Stochastic image editing yields several plausible facial surgery visualizations, but selecting one without postoperative ground truth is hard, and identity preservation and realism do not show that the intended anatomical change occurred.
yJipgniOxV.method: A fixed FLUX.1-Fill backbone generates candidate pools across seeds and edit intensities. The ranker combines procedure-normalized morphometric changes, geometric information pooled across candidates and learned appearance features with a procedure-conditioned direction predictor, trained with paired postoperative images as teacher supervision.
yJipgniOxV.key_idea: Rank candidates as a set using normalized landmark morphometry pooled across candidates and a predicted case-level change direction, trained to regress a teacher score from postoperative images.
yJipgniOxV.evidence: A locked 160-case multi-procedure test set, a 211-case ASPS/PCA rhinoplasty cohort and a 57-case HDA cross-procedure cohort, with seed analyses.
yJipgniOxV.claimed_gains: Improves mean teacher SurgicalScore over a handcrafted selector by 0.036 with 15 candidates (p=0.0022) and 0.039 with 25 candidates (p=0.0016), plus 0.032 on the 211-case cohort and 0.033 on the 57-case cohort at K=15.
yJipgniOxV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem framing, which separates selector quality from generator quality using identical nested candidate pools, is clear and practically relevant.
yJipgniOxV.main_concern: The ranker is trained on and evaluated with the same teacher score without clinician validation, and the reported significance largely comes from merging validation data, with small non-significant gains on the pure held-out test set.

NSvIJnAORy.one_liner: Regularizer aligning latent states and local dynamics across rollout origins so autoregressive neural PDE solvers agree at shared target times.
NSvIJnAORy.problem: In autoregressive neural PDE rollouts, approximation errors propagate so predictions at a shared target time depend on their temporal origin and rollout depth, although exact evolution of a deterministic flow would agree.
NSvIJnAORy.method: Align Latent Rollout (ALR) regularizes internal solver representations with two objectives motivated by a second-order Taylor analysis: zeroth-order latent state consistency at a shared target time and first-order latent dynamics consistency of local responses to shared perturbations. It plugs into different neural PDE solvers without changing their backbones.
NSvIJnAORy.key_idea: Penalize latent-state and Jacobian-response differences between rollouts from different origins that reach the same target time, using the semigroup property of deterministic flows.
NSvIJnAORy.evidence: Experiments on multiple PDE benchmarks and neural-operator backbones, compared with unrolled training and the base surrogates; reviews note 2D single-channel regular-grid benchmarks.
NSvIJnAORy.claimed_gains: Improves prediction accuracy and reduces shared-target discrepancies across rollout origins; no numbers stated.
NSvIJnAORy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-origin consistency principle is physically grounded and intuitive, and that ALR is a lightweight, backbone-agnostic training regularizer with no inference cost that improves base surrogates.
NSvIJnAORy.main_concern: Comparisons are limited to naive unrolled training, with no comparison against PDE-Refiner, scheduled sampling or other rollout-stability methods, and it is unclear why Jacobian alignment beats simpler consistency objectives.

Ab09hyLHqR.one_liner: Score-only VLM adaptation that standardizes class scores and corrects them with prompt-conditioned residual interactions via target prototypes.
Ab09hyLHqR.problem: Deployment interfaces may expose only a fixed tensor of prompt-level class scores, and existing score-only methods mainly aggregate or reweight scores rather than exploit relational structure.
Ab09hyLHqR.method: Prompt-Class Residual Interaction (PCRI) class-standardizes the score tensor to build a Score-space Core, extracts Core-conditioned prompt innovation, and uses the joint representation only to correct the frozen semantic score field through target prototypes. One configuration selected on CIFAR-100 is frozen across all evaluation domains.
Ab09hyLHqR.key_idea: Standardize scores across classes to remove sample-wise offsets and scales, then add Core-conditioned prompt residuals to correct the frozen score field via target prototypes.
Ab09hyLHqR.evidence: Eleven classification datasets and three VLM backbones using cached scores under matched controls and stress tests, across 33 fixed-pool settings.
Ab09hyLHqR.claimed_gains: Improves matched CARPRT by +2.378 percentage points on average across 11 datasets and three VLM backbones, with gains in 32/33 settings; Core conditioning adds +0.306 percentage points.
Ab09hyLHqR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the strictly score-only setting is precisely defined, matched comparisons on cached scores are convincing, and limitations and failure cases are reported honestly.
Ab09hyLHqR.main_concern: Most of the gain comes from the simple cross-class standardization step, the extra benefit of core conditioning is modest, and the scope is narrow (classification, transductive target pools, three prompt-weighting aggregators).

GztLE09afn.one_liner: Spectral RLVR optimizer that anchors the update on the positive-advantage gradient subspace and separately transforms the remaining negative gradient.
GztLE09afn.problem: Muon and Pion transform gradients after combining positive- and negative-advantage terms into momentum, although positive-advantage gradients have lower effective rank than negative ones.
GztLE09afn.method: PASP uses the current positive gradient to define an anchor subspace, jointly transforms the full positive gradient and the part of the negative gradient inside that subspace, separately transforms a low-rank approximation of the remaining negative gradient, and adds the two outputs to form the update.
GztLE09afn.key_idea: Split the RLVR gradient by advantage sign and orthogonalize the positive gradient plus its in-subspace negative component jointly, handling the residual negative part separately.
GztLE09afn.evidence: Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B (plus other model families per reviews) against AdamW, Muon and Pion on four reasoning benchmarks, with three training seeds, GRPO and DAPO, and ablations.
GztLE09afn.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B PASP reaches 0.489 +/- 0.006 versus 0.470 +/- 0.015 for Pion; on Qwen3-1.7B it averages 0.463 versus 0.398 for Muon and 0.184 for Pion; under DAPO it reaches 0.485 versus 0.466 for Muon.
GztLE09afn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the optimizer is grounded in a measurable spectral asymmetry between positive and negative advantage gradients and that ablations favor the positive-gradient anchor.
GztLE09afn.main_concern: Statistical and mechanism evidence is thin: paired confidence intervals include zero in four of five main settings, the asymmetry may reflect token counts, the sign-split ablation confounds branch count, and the main version needs three backward passes.

nG8mpFKXo5.one_liner: RL framework for document-level translation combining alignment-based coverage and discourse fluency rewards with stage- and length-adaptive weights.
nG8mpFKXo5.problem: LLM document-level translation struggles to preserve source information while staying coherent, and word-alignment coverage declines on longer documents while fluency improves.
nG8mpFKXo5.method: DocGRPO combines an alignment-based coverage reward for source preservation with a discourse-aware fluency reward, adapts reward weights to training progress and source-document length, and combines group-relative and reference-relative advantages for policy updates.
nG8mpFKXo5.key_idea: Shift reward weights between coverage and fluency according to training progress and document length inside GRPO, using group-relative plus reference-relative advantages.
nG8mpFKXo5.evidence: Five translation directions and two model scales with automatic metrics, human evaluation including omission and addition errors, and ablations.
nG8mpFKXo5.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports improvements over strong document-level baselines without numbers)
nG8mpFKXo5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balancing adequacy and fluency with stage- and length-aware weights is well motivated, with gains across five directions, two model scales and human evaluation.
nG8mpFKXo5.main_concern: The contribution is seen as incremental (GRPO plus reward engineering and adaptive weighting) without justification of the schedule, and evaluation lacks a whole-document prompting baseline and covers only X-to-English translation on a single news domain.

om6j217LX6.one_liner: Reference-free reward model for action-conditioned world models, trained on complementary action-mismatch and video-mismatch preference pairs.
om6j217LX6.problem: Existing rewards for action-conditioned world models capture only one dimension: metric rewards assess visual quality but need ground-truth videos, and IDM rewards assess action following but not quality and may be unreliable on generated videos.
om6j217LX6.method: AVM-Eval (67.2k pairs) tests how reliably IDMs assess action following, and AVM-Pref (506.3k pairs) combines action-mismatch pairs supervising action following with video-mismatch pairs supervising both. ACWM-RM pretrains an action-conditioned predictor on real videos to learn forward dynamics, then scores videos without ground-truth references.
om6j217LX6.key_idea: Train a reward from action-mismatch and video-mismatch preference pairs on top of a forward-dynamics predictor pretrained on real videos, so scoring needs no reference video.
om6j217LX6.evidence: AVM-Eval and AVM-Pref benchmarks, ablations (fresh/frozen predictor, JEPA-IDM, preference removal, score head), and Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning on DreamDojo-2B.
om6j217LX6.claimed_gains: The visible abstract states no performance numbers (only dataset sizes of 67.2k and 506.3k pairs); a review reports nDTW rising from 14.84 to 16.41 under Flow-GRPO.
om6j217LX6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the complementary action-mismatch and video-mismatch supervision is well motivated and that ablations show both preference types and dynamics pretraining improve generated-video ranking.
om6j217LX6.main_concern: Generalization is untested: the same four world models generate both training and evaluation videos, RL is shown on one model, and evaluation relies on PSNR and LPIPS that also built the training pairs plus 2D trajectories only.

1bDSpqiyNc.one_liner: Lightweight probe for frozen cross-modal biomolecular models: projector-guided token readout plus input-conditioned fusion of encoder and projector embeddings.
1bDSpqiyNc.problem: Frozen cross-modal biomolecular models are probed on a single pooled or projected embedding, yet the better one changes across tasks, fixed pooling is task-independent, and concatenation gives limited gains.
1bDSpqiyNc.method: Allosteric Readout uses the projected embedding to guide token selection over encoder tokens, replacing fixed pooling. Homeostatic Fusion assigns complementary, input-conditioned per-dimension weights to the aggregated token representation and the projected embedding.
1bDSpqiyNc.key_idea: Use the projector's embedding as a query to attend over encoder tokens, then gate-fuse that readout with the projected embedding per dimension.
1bDSpqiyNc.evidence: Three platforms and five groups of biomolecular tasks (molecular property and protein function), compared with encoder-only, projector-only and other foundation-model probing, plus an effective-rank analysis.
1bDSpqiyNc.claimed_gains: Best average performance across three platforms and five groups of biomolecular tasks, and recovery of the effective rank lost by projection, with no numbers beyond counts.
1bDSpqiyNc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is important, the finding that the better representation varies by task is useful, and the readout is effective across a wide variety of experiments.
1bDSpqiyNc.main_concern: Novelty is limited because projector-queried cross-attention is standard attentive probing, and there are no component ablations isolating it from a learnable query, a pooled query, concatenation or a scalar gate.

KeOQ4l14XN.one_liner: Unified inference runtime for VLA and world-action robot models, with adaptive parallelism, CUDA graph replay and kernel fusion.
KeOQ4l14XN.problem: Robot Learning Model inference infrastructure is fragmented across deployment scales, unlike the mature serving ecosystems for LLMs.
