KeOQ4l14XN.method: PhyAI decouples model semantics from execution and adapts parallelism (unbatched, DP, TP) and kernel dispatch to the target hardware, using CUDA graph replay, kernel fusion and state reuse. A Control Rate Roofline model relates inference speedups to physical control frequency.
KeOQ4l14XN.key_idea: Separate model semantics from execution so one runtime selects parallelism and kernels per hardware target, with CUDA graphs, kernel fusion and state reuse.
KeOQ4l14XN.evidence: Latency benchmarks over 11 configurations against official implementations across five model families, task-success matching for pi0.5 and GR00T, and a replica-scaling RL rollout workflow (per reviews).
KeOQ4l14XN.claimed_gains: 1.40x to 4.65x latency speedups over official implementations across 11 benchmark configurations.
KeOQ4l14XN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the runtime covers a useful breadth of VLA and WAM models and deployment modes and addresses real fragmentation in robot deployment software.
KeOQ4l14XN.main_concern: Headline speedups are measured against weaker official implementations rather than optimized runtimes (with no consistent advantage over FlashRT), and the work reads as engineering integration of standard techniques with limited evaluation.

DfeZKCs4Ga.one_liner: Frozen-LM residual-stream steering probe plus a label-free reconstruction map that repairs interference with a mean-difference abstention direction.
DfeZKCs4Ga.problem: A frozen language model under-uses evidence in its hidden states and answers confidently when the context contains no answer, and combining steering with abstention scoring in one pass degrades the abstention signal.
DfeZKCs4Ga.method: A small trained probe adds an input-dependent vector to the residual at several middle layers to raise accuracy, while a fixed mean-difference direction scores hidden states for abstention. A map trained without labels to reconstruct the unedited hidden state from the edited one removes the probe's interference.
DfeZKCs4Ga.key_idea: Train a label-free map to reconstruct the unedited hidden state from the steered one, so the abstention direction can read a clean state in the same forward pass.
DfeZKCs4Ga.evidence: Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B on alpha-NLI and four QA datasets with human answerability labels, compared with LoRA, hidden-state classifiers, LoFiT and LoReFT.
DfeZKCs4Ga.claimed_gains: The probe raises Qwen2.5-1.5B on alpha-NLI from 51% to 73% accuracy; the direction loses under 3 percentage points of decision accuracy (from 0.83 in domain) when moved to another dataset; the map removes 63% of interference on 1.5B.
DfeZKCs4Ga.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of improving accuracy and abstention in one pass interesting, the label-free map promising across steering methods, and the experimental procedure clear.
DfeZKCs4Ga.main_concern: Novelty and positioning are weak because linear abstention probes and MLP steering probes already exist and related probing literature is not cited, and the map's benefit shrinks or vanishes at 7B.

1Zx80T4SRH.one_liner: Benchmark for streaming audio-video generation with progressive and interactive tracks across 32 dimensions and 13 systems.
1Zx80T4SRH.problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate completed sequences and fail to capture the properties of unbounded streaming audio-video generation.
1Zx80T4SRH.method: StreamAV-Bench has a progressive track for instruction adherence and long-horizon stability and an interactive track for interactive response and state retention and reuse, using expert-verified cases scored over 32 fine-grained dimensions. It evaluates 13 representative systems.
1Zx80T4SRH.key_idea: Split evaluation into progressive generation (drift over long horizons) and interactive runtime updates (response and state retention) with expert-verified cases and a shared judge.
1Zx80T4SRH.evidence: Evaluation of 13 systems (native joint models and cascaded pipelines) on 320 expert-verified scenarios at up to 180 seconds, with a human study of 120 output pairs per metric.
1Zx80T4SRH.claimed_gains: not stated (benchmark paper; the abstract reports that current models show temporal drift in progressive generation and responsiveness bottlenecks in interactive control)
1Zx80T4SRH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark asks the right questions for streaming audio-video generation, with broad coverage and a clean progressive versus interactive decomposition.
1Zx80T4SRH.main_concern: Evaluation reliability is under-validated, since most semantic metrics rely on one Gemini judge and all ten cascaded systems share one video-to-audio model (HunyuanVideo-Foley), which confounds the audio comparison.

5Pm3o3quFp.one_liner: Task-specific layer folding for unified multimodal models: DAG shortest-path search chooses layers to skip, with Stitch LoRA repair.
5Pm3o3quFp.problem: In unified multimodal models, understanding has redundancy in deeper layers while generation is sensitive to depth reduction, so static layer pruning degrades one task.
5Pm3o3quFp.method: FoldUMM formulates layer folding as a constrained shortest-path problem on a directed acyclic graph, with dynamic programming finding task-specific folding paths under a pruning budget. Lightweight Stitch LoRA modules at fold points repair representation mismatch.
5Pm3o3quFp.key_idea: Pick different skipped-layer paths per task by dynamic programming over a layer DAG using representation-similarity costs, and heal each fold point with a small LoRA.
5Pm3o3quFp.evidence: Janus-Pro and OmniGen2, with layer-wise redundancy profiling, selection-rule ablations (uniform, random, greedy mutual information, DAG-DP) and understanding and generation benchmarks (MM-Vet-V2, GenEval).
5Pm3o3quFp.claimed_gains: not stated numerically (the abstract says higher understanding and generation performance is preserved under structured pruning, with practical inference speedup)
5Pm3o3quFp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that task-dependent layer redundancy is a sound motivation and that local Stitch LoRA recovery is well motivated, with the DP search shown to carry much of the benefit.
5Pm3o3quFp.main_concern: The efficiency claim is weak on the decoupled OmniGen2 architecture, where end-to-end generation time stays at 30.10 s despite a 1.22x backbone throughput gain, and multiple paths need extra GPU memory.

7l7yCCeSYj.one_liner: 3D affordance grounding using large models only for a coarse region, then three lightweight point-cloud heads pick the instance.
7l7yCCeSYj.problem: Leading language-guided 3D affordance methods run an 8B-72B VLM inside the grounding loop on captured RGB-D frames, where the target may be occluded or absent, and leave 3D relations between same-type candidates largely unused.
7l7yCCeSYj.method: A frozen VLM parses the instruction and selects a rendered view, and a frozen grounder delimits a candidate region, after which no large model is used. Three heads (5.05M parameters) on frozen point-cloud features propose candidate instances, select the referred same-category instance, and refine the final mask.
7l7yCCeSYj.key_idea: Resolve which same-type instance is meant from candidate-to-candidate 3D structure with a set-selector, rather than from rendered images or large-model reasoning.
7l7yCCeSYj.evidence: SceneFun3D experiments against the reproduced AffordBot-72B and RGB-based pipelines, with ablations, failure-stage analysis and isolated selection experiments.
7l7yCCeSYj.claimed_gains: On SceneFun3D it leads the strongest (baseline; sentence cut off in the abstract) using 5.05M trainable parameters.
7l7yCCeSYj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the decomposition into localization, candidate generation, instance selection and refinement is well motivated, improves over the reproduced AffordBot-72B, and trains cheaply on frozen features.
7l7yCCeSYj.main_concern: The ablations do not isolate candidate-to-candidate relational modeling from language access and model capacity, and the end-to-end contribution of the Set-Selector is unclear since most failures occur in upstream candidate and ROI stages.

aNZULdwzqX.one_liner: Reward fine-tuning for guided diffusion that learns DiffusionNFT's regression center online by flow matching on guided samples.
aNZULdwzqX.problem: Applying classifier-free guidance after DiffusionNFT can reduce the optimized reward, and guiding during NFT fine-tuning can collapse, because a mismatched regression center biases the reward-driven update.
aNZULdwzqX.method: GuidanceNFT learns the regression center online by flow matching on guided samples and corrects both NFT regression terms while preserving the policy's reward-driven displacement, supporting explicit and intrinsic guidance without extra inference passes.
aNZULdwzqX.key_idea: Replace NFT's mismatched regression center with an online-learned conditional mean velocity from guided samples, applying the same correction to both regression branches.
aNZULdwzqX.evidence: SD3.5-M on GenEval and OCR specialization across three training objectives and seven metrics, plus ImageNet generation, OpenWebText and GSM8K under intrinsic guidance.
aNZULdwzqX.claimed_gains: OCR reward rises from 0.971 to 0.975 while held-out GenEval success rises from 0.035 to 0.488, and it outperforms NFT on all seven GenEval and OCR evaluation metrics.
aNZULdwzqX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the regression-center mismatch diagnosis is clear and theoretically explained, and that the proposed fix is simple and effective across several guidance mechanisms and tasks.
aNZULdwzqX.main_concern: The auxiliary center estimator adds about 1.73-1.77 times NFT training time per iteration, and a simpler baseline (condition dropout during NFT followed by CFG at inference) is not compared.

HWi9uA3nEe.one_liner: Multi-bitwidth post-training quantization of LLMs by training additive codebook prefixes with Matryoshka supervision, so dropping codebooks lowers precision.
HWi9uA3nEe.problem: Deploying LLMs on heterogeneous hardware needs adjustable precision from one model without retraining, whereas static per-bitwidth quantized models multiply storage and quantization cost.
HWi9uA3nEe.method: Drop-by-Drop adds Matryoshka-style supervision to additive codebook training so codebook prefixes give accurate partial reconstructions at each precision level, and a block-Hadamard rotation brings weights closer to a Gaussian source. A proof of Gaussian successive refinability under weighted MSE motivates the design.
HWi9uA3nEe.key_idea: Order additive codebooks by Matryoshka-style prefix supervision so that dropping later codebooks yields coarser but accurate weights, after Hadamard rotation toward Gaussian.
HWi9uA3nEe.evidence: Qwen, LLaMA, Gemma and Mistral models, perplexity and zero-shot accuracy against multi-bitwidth methods and AQLM, with a proof of Gaussian successive refinability and specialized inference kernels.
HWi9uA3nEe.claimed_gains: Lower perplexity than state-of-the-art multi-bitwidth methods with competitive zero-shot accuracy across Qwen, LLaMA, Gemma and Mistral; no numbers stated in the visible abstract.
HWi9uA3nEe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree prefix supervision makes AQLM codebook dropping usable across a broad model sweep, with a sound theoretical motivation and practical storage and kernel benefits.
HWi9uA3nEe.main_concern: Comparisons are not fully reliable or fair: the evaluation protocol is unspecified, a rotated AQLM baseline is missing, recent models and generation benchmarks are absent, and the method is seen as an incremental extension of AQLM.

hp43WMCdKT.one_liner: End-to-end driving planner that distills multiple trajectory targets from a future-privileged teacher, with safety-aware score correction.
hp43WMCdKT.problem: Driving logs record only the executed trajectory, giving limited supervision for alternative valid behaviors, and broader multi-target coverage makes safe candidate selection harder.
hp43WMCdKT.method: Future-Privileged Multi-Target Distillation transfers diverse, high-quality trajectory targets from a teacher with access to recorded future observations into a visual student. Safety-Aware Score Correction fixes ranking errors between nearby safe and unsafe candidates and raises underestimated safety scores of safe candidates; the student needs no future input at deployment.
hp43WMCdKT.key_idea: Let a teacher see recorded future observations to generate varied trajectory targets for the student, and correct candidate scoring so nearby safe and unsafe options rank correctly.
hp43WMCdKT.evidence: NAVSIM v1 navtest and NAVSIM v2 navhard benchmarks plus zero-shot closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM, with ablations on target budget and future-privileged versus self-distillation.
hp43WMCdKT.claimed_gains: The base model reaches 94.9 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 navtest and 55.9 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 navhard; FPD-Drive-Pro reaches 95.5 PDMS and 58.1 EPDMS; HUGSIM HD-Score is 45.1.
hp43WMCdKT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending supervision beyond the single recorded trajectory with future-privileged multi-target distillation is well motivated, and that the empirical results, including closed-loop HUGSIM, are strong.
hp43WMCdKT.main_concern: Novelty overlaps with prior work (EvoDriveVLA's future-informed teachers, CLOVER's multi-target selection, Hydra-MDP's multi-target distillation), and the effects of future privilege and multi-target supervision are not fully disentangled.

RLrlBOyjMk.one_liner: Diffusion for combinatorial optimization in a learned VAE latent space with rectified flow, decoding to feasible solutions with repair.
RLrlBOyjMk.problem: Diffusion-based combinatorial optimization needs a corruption process: generic variable-wise noise ignores solution geometry, and search-style perturbations are task-specific and hard to define for some problems.
RLrlBOyjMk.method: An instance-conditioned VAE maps discrete solutions to a latent regularized toward Gaussian geometry, and an instance-conditioned rectified-flow model with canonical Gaussian interpolation is trained there. Denoised latents decode to solution scores and become feasible solutions through constraint-aware decoding and repair, and the latent geometry supports test-time search.
RLrlBOyjMk.key_idea: Learn a Gaussian-regularized latent space for solutions so standard continuous flow matching applies to any problem class, moving constraint handling to the decoding step.
RLrlBOyjMk.evidence: Experiments on TSP (including TSP-500), RB-graph MIS, CVRP and TSPTW (per reviews), with ablations against diffusion in the raw solution space.
RLrlBOyjMk.claimed_gains: The visible abstract states no numbers; a review reports the optimality gap lowered more than eightfold on TSP-500 and RB graphs versus raw-space diffusion.
RLrlBOyjMk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving diffusion into a learned latent space is a relatively novel and sound approach, evaluated on a wide variety of combinatorial problems with strong results versus raw-space diffusion.
RLrlBOyjMk.main_concern: The latent-space ablation is confounded because LCO-Diff adds a 12-layer VAE and the raw-space baseline uses Gaussian rather than discrete noise with no parameter-matched control, and reviewers also cite unclear notation and problem-specific repair and retraining.

t5xTNmR1Dd.one_liner: Circuit-complexity proof that diffusion language models with token revision need fewer decoding rounds than those without.
t5xTNmR1Dd.problem: It is unclear whether revision's advantage in sequential computation persists as diffusion language models evolve and what mechanisms drive it.
t5xTNmR1Dd.method: In a model where each Transformer decoding round uses AC^0 computation, the paper compares the minimum rounds needed to sample (X, f_L(X)) for uniform X and a binary regular language L, with and without revision, proving upper and lower bounds.
t5xTNmR1Dd.key_idea: Overwriting tokens during revision lets a DLM sample a word with its regular-language label in two rounds, where no-revision models need Theta(log n / log log n).
t5xTNmR1Dd.evidence: Theoretical results only: round-complexity upper and lower bounds for sampling binary regular languages, a Transformer realization with polynomial width and constant precision, and a round separation under further settings (cut off).
t5xTNmR1Dd.claimed_gains: A DLM with revision samples this distribution in at most two rounds without CoT positions, while without revision the round complexity is Theta(log n / log log n) for every L outside AC^0, and O(n^(1-theta)) CoT positions do not suffice for constant rounds.
t5xTNmR1Dd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a rigorous, comprehensive round-complexity characterization with matching bounds that strengthens a prior separation result, using a nontrivial hidden aperiodic DFA construction.
t5xTNmR1Dd.main_concern: Novelty over the preceding separation result (Jiang et al.) is limited, and the assumptions (binary regular languages, AC^0 rounds, constant precision) are artificial and may not transfer to practical diffusion language models.

B2ZWlbFSxg.one_liner: Conformal prediction under covariate shift: repeated doubly-robust regeneration across splits, coverage balancing, and union of candidate sets.
B2ZWlbFSxg.problem: Weighted conformal prediction can give excessively wide or infinite sets under severe covariate shift, while doubly robust prediction can undercover because errors in a single pair of component estimates reinforce one another.
B2ZWlbFSxg.method: Doubly propagated calibration (DPC) repeatedly regenerates the DRP component-model estimates across data splits and propagates their finite-sample uncertainty through calibration. Within each run it balances source and target samples on estimated coverage probabilities, then takes the union of candidate sets across runs.
B2ZWlbFSxg.key_idea: Propagate nuisance-estimation uncertainty by regenerating component models across splits, balancing coverage-probability tilts per run, and taking the union so one reliable candidate protects coverage.
B2ZWlbFSxg.evidence: Severe-shift simulations and California Housing experiments, plus theory (Theorem 3.1 on asymptotic coverage) under stated conditions.
B2ZWlbFSxg.claimed_gains: DPC attains near-nominal 90% coverage in settings where DRP substantially undercovers (the interval-width comparison is cut off in the abstract).
B2ZWlbFSxg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multiple-regeneration plus union strategy is easy to implement, well formulated with deep theoretical analysis, and addresses the finite-sample sensitivity of doubly robust calibration.
B2ZWlbFSxg.main_concern: The theory depends on strong conditions (such as a positive probability of a successful candidate and bounded weights) not shown for the actual procedure, and the union can be overly conservative with unclear efficiency gains over DRP.

jn2ZqqccCF.one_liner: Approximation algorithms for alpha-partial p-Wasserstein barycenters, with fixed-support and free-support variants running in quadratic time or less.
jn2ZqqccCF.problem: Wasserstein barycenters are sensitive to outliers, and the alpha-partial formulation that addresses this lacked provably efficient algorithms.
jn2ZqqccCF.method: The first algorithm computes an approximate fixed-support alpha-partial barycenter in roughly m*n*delta^-2 time (m the support size, delta a mass error), and the second improves free-support runtime in metric spaces by a factor of m at the cost of extra epsilon error in OT-plan cost. Reviews describe synchronized multiplicative-weights-style updates on a packing LP.
jn2ZqqccCF.key_idea: Solve the partial-barycenter packing LP with synchronized updates that keep equal incoming mass from every input distribution at each barycenter point, avoiding the multimarginal tensor.
jn2ZqqccCF.evidence: Theoretical analysis only: running-time and approximation guarantees for fixed and free supports in Euclidean and general metric spaces, plus an exact algorithm when the p-centroid is computable in polynomial time.
jn2ZqqccCF.claimed_gains: The fixed-support algorithm runs in roughly m*n*delta^-2 time, the free-support algorithm saves a factor of m at an extra epsilon cost error, and an exact algorithm exists when p-centroids are polynomial-time computable (details cut off).
jn2ZqqccCF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree these are the first provably efficient approximation algorithms for the alpha-partial barycenter problem, covering fixed and free supports and avoiding the full transport tensor.
jn2ZqqccCF.main_concern: Reviewers raise soundness and clarity concerns, including a possibly invalid feasibility argument in Lemma 10, an exact algorithm with m^O(k) time, unquantified cost degradation in the faster free-support algorithm, and hard-to-parse LP-solving sections.

u6gVELv8sv.one_liner: Hierarchical branch-level and segment-level preference optimization teaching MLLMs object identification, defect knowledge reference and judgment for anomaly inspection.
u6gVELv8sv.problem: MLLM-based industrial anomaly detection mostly decides whether a defect exists, neglecting diagnostic details such as which object is involved, why a defect is suspected and what judgment is made.
u6gVELv8sv.method: Hierarchical Knowledge Preference Optimization (HKPO) abstracts object and defect morphologies into structured knowledge and applies branch-level and segment-level preference optimization, so the model identifies objects, references structured knowledge and judges defects.
u6gVELv8sv.key_idea: Weight preference errors by reasoning stage (object identity, defect knowledge, final judgment) at branch and segment level instead of treating every response error equally.
u6gVELv8sv.evidence: Public industrial anomaly benchmarks (MMAD and SSGD per reviews) with ablations on SFT, DPO and HKPO components, using an 8B backbone compared with a 32B model and a proprietary model.
u6gVELv8sv.claimed_gains: Lifts a lightweight 8B model 7.15% above its own backbone and 2.71% above a 4x larger 32B counterpart, and surpasses the strong proprietary model by 5.46% in average accuracy (margin over dedicated anomaly-detection MLLMs cut off).
u6gVELv8sv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the object, defect-knowledge and judgment decomposition mirrors human inspection and that same-backbone gains are substantial across several tasks.
u6gVELv8sv.main_concern: Most of the gain comes from answer-only SFT (5.35 of 7.15 points), the preference-weighting increment over DPO is narrow, and hierarchical reasoning is not directly validated or compared with related work such as JUDO.

NXGAVuPO9o.one_liner: Diagnoses causal abstraction by partitioning inputs into well-interpreted and under-interpreted buckets from pairwise interchange-intervention behavior.
NXGAVuPO9o.problem: Interchange intervention accuracy is a single global summary that does not show where an interpretation works or fails.
NXGAVuPO9o.method: The method partitions the input space by pairwise interchange-intervention behavior (reviewers describe finding cliques in an interchange-consistent graph) and analyzes the regions to find missing distinctions, unmodeled intermediate variables, and complementary partial interpretations to combine. It is packaged as a four-step recipe.
NXGAVuPO9o.key_idea: Group inputs into buckets whose pairwise interchange interventions succeed, so high-level hypotheses are evaluated and refined per region rather than by one global IIA score.
NXGAVuPO9o.evidence: Three settings (a logic inference task, entity binding and entangled factual recall), with error analyses and recursive application of the recipe.
NXGAVuPO9o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that moving beyond a single global IIA score to a region-wise diagnostic is a clever, useful idea, clearly presented and evaluated on three tasks.
NXGAVuPO9o.main_concern: The evidence for improving causal abstraction is thin, since results mostly rediscover known interpretations, and high within-bucket IIA can arise when an intervention changes nothing (as in RAVEL language buckets), so it may not test local faithfulness.

H2AE8pLouI.one_liner: Benchmark for line-level student answer reconstruction from full exam pages, plus ExamInk-Evo, a failure-driven skill self-evolution method.
H2AE8pLouI.problem: Existing benchmarks evaluate handwriting recognition, document parsing and answer grounding separately, so coupled failures in reconstructing a student's full response from a whole page are hard to measure.
H2AE8pLouI.method: A gold-standard corpus of 4,017 annotated samples from about 31,769 real mathematics exam papers (141 public as ExamInkBench) represents responses as ordered answer lines grouped by question item, with a two-level protocol for line extraction and ordering and for intra-line transcription. ExamInk-Evo mines recurrent errors, induces reconstruction and verification skills, and keeps updates only when held-out validation improves.
H2AE8pLouI.key_idea: Mine recurrent page-level failures, induce targeted reconstruction and verification skills for tool-using agents, and accept skill updates only if held-out validation improves.
H2AE8pLouI.evidence: Evaluation of mainstream multimodal models on 141 public samples and experiments with tool-using agents applying ExamInk-Evo.
H2AE8pLouI.claimed_gains: not stated numerically (the abstract says ExamInk-Evo consistently improves extraction and a second metric, with the sentence cut off)
H2AE8pLouI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the full-page reconstruction task is a meaningful problem for educational AI, supported by substantial annotation effort and an explicit two-level evaluation protocol.
H2AE8pLouI.main_concern: Evidence that skill self-evolution is necessary is limited (it uses a predefined skill catalog with no fixed-pipeline or all-skills baseline), and the public set is small with unclear data provenance and split construction.

ZymMfXyt8z.one_liner: Compact query-aware retriever, distilled from cloud VLM attention, that selects visual tokens on the edge before transmission.
ZymMfXyt8z.problem: Uploading dense visual tokens from edge to cloud VLMs is costly, vision-only selectors ignore the query, and query-aware methods need heavy language or multimodal models on the edge device.
ZymMfXyt8z.method: READ trains a compact cross-modal retriever offline using prompt-to-visual attention from the frozen cloud model as supervision, jointly with prefix-ranking and score-calibration objectives, so edge devices pick query-relevant visual tokens without running large models locally.
ZymMfXyt8z.key_idea: Distill the cloud VLM's prompt-to-visual attention into a small cross-modal retriever with ranking and calibration losses, treating token selection as evidence retrieval.
ZymMfXyt8z.evidence: Experiments across diverse VLM architectures and transmission budgets, with ablations of ranking, calibration, visual prior and coverage, and a comparison with SGP (per reviews).
ZymMfXyt8z.claimed_gains: Competitive efficiency-accuracy trade-off across architectures and transmission budgets (rest of abstract cut off); a review notes the retriever is 32x smaller than SGP.
ZymMfXyt8z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the edge-cloud token-transmission problem is practical and that distilling cloud attention into a lightweight query-aware retriever is well motivated, with ablations supporting each component.
ZymMfXyt8z.main_concern: The ablations are insufficient (no removal of the ranking objective and no query-free retriever control), attention as an evidence signal is only qualitatively validated, and communication is measured in token counts rather than bytes.

Ay9vudYeQK.one_liner: Zero-initialized convolutional residual adapter in the visual token space that targets counting bottlenecks in MLLMs.
Ay9vudYeQK.problem: MLLMs struggle with fine-grained counting because patchification fragments objects across patch boundaries (individuation) and attention compression collapses count separation as numerosity grows (aggregation).
Ay9vudYeQK.method: ConvStack is a lightweight architecture acting on visual tokens that aggregates and injects local spatial structure via zero-initialized residual connections, fine-tuned only on counting tasks.
Ay9vudYeQK.key_idea: Mix neighboring visual tokens with local 3x3 convolutions and add the result through zero-initialized residuals, giving explicit geometric evidence to the downstream counting aggregation.
Ay9vudYeQK.evidence: Mechanistic analysis with synthetic disk experiments, attention theory, count-class separation measurements, ablations versus 1x1, LoRA and single-route variants, and counting plus spatial benchmarks on Qwen3 (per reviews).
Ay9vudYeQK.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements in dense object counting and broader spatial understanding benchmarks without compromising general visual (sentence cut off); no numbers in the visible abstract.
Ay9vudYeQK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled synthetic experiments and ablations make a clear case for local spatial mixing at patch boundaries, with parameter-efficient gains on counting and several spatial benchmarks.
Ay9vudYeQK.main_concern: Evidence that ConvStack resolves the two identified bottlenecks is indirect and the theory relies on strong assumptions (homogeneous tokens, additive counting features), novelty is limited, and results cover one backbone family (Qwen3) with small real-image counting sets.

0AdawuC1tj.one_liner: Jointly trains a VLM policy and a rubricator that generates environment-validated rubrics as turn-level process rewards.
0AdawuC1tj.problem: Outcome rewards give little supervision on why intermediate visual reasoning steps and actions succeed or fail, and existing dense process rewards are manually specified or fixed, so they do not adapt to the trajectory distribution that RL induces.
0AdawuC1tj.method: GEAR co-evolves a VLM policy and a rubricator that self-generates grounded rubrics for spatial grounding, action legality, temporal consistency, and transition progress. A rubric is kept only if its satisfaction is statistically aligned with grounded environment feedback, and kept rubrics are evaluated on local visual transitions to give turn-level process rewards.
0AdawuC1tj.key_idea: Keep a self-generated rubric only when its satisfaction statistically correlates with environment outcomes, then use it as a turn-level reward on local visual transitions.
0AdawuC1tj.evidence: Experiments on multi-turn VLM agent benchmarks with ablations on rubric evolution; reviews mention Sokoban, FrozenLake, embodied 3D navigation and PrimitiveSkill, SVG reconstruction, and a 3B backbone.
0AdawuC1tj.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says only that GEAR improves over SFT and outcome-centric RL baselines, with no numbers).
0AdawuC1tj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that rubrics are validated against environment feedback instead of being fixed, and that the shared solver and rubricator backbone makes the pipeline efficient with a small 3B model.
0AdawuC1tj.main_concern: Rubric filtering may leak the outcome label (an accepted Sokoban rubric has correlation 1.00 with success), so the process reward could be hindsight relabeling rather than an independent signal.

aMs3T9Kgbl.one_liner: Tests how driving benchmark scores respond to behavior changes, showing optimization gains can reverse when the execution interface changes.
aMs3T9Kgbl.problem: When a driving benchmark score is itself optimized, it is unclear whether score gains still reflect real driving improvement.
aMs3T9Kgbl.method: The authors decompose the scoring process into execution, measurement, subscore mapping, and aggregation, then run controlled interventions on driving behavior and matched closed-loop comparisons under different execution interfaces.
aMs3T9Kgbl.key_idea: Decompose scoring into execution, measurement, subscore mapping and aggregation, then compare optimization gains under controlled interventions and swapped execution interfaces.
aMs3T9Kgbl.evidence: Controlled interventions and closed-loop comparisons across multiple planners, including a matched comparison of two execution interfaces; reviews mention PDMS, LQR, Qwen-Drive and ReCogDrive-2B.
aMs3T9Kgbl.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative findings only, with no numbers).
aMs3T9Kgbl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the matched closed-loop execution-interface comparison, which holds planner checkpoints, scenes, scoring and inference fixed and shows gain reversals.
aMs3T9Kgbl.main_concern: Reviewers say the novelty over already-known PDMS limitations is unclear, and that waypoint jitter measured on intermediate planner outputs does not by itself show worse driving.

EEg8z09LdM.one_liner: Differentiable latent-tree causal discovery using triplet branch-point objectives for skeleton and three-terminal independence for root orientation.
EEg8z09LdM.problem: Recovering directed causal structure with latent variables is hard, especially when identifiability principles must be turned into practical learning objectives.
EEg8z09LdM.method: For skeleton learning, a differentiable triplet branch-point (TBP) formulation uses simplex-valued triplet-center assignments to jointly learn branch-point identities and latent-related distances. For orientation, a tree-conditioned three-terminal independence (TTI) criterion identifies the latent root under linear non-Gaussian assumptions, and edges are oriented away from it.
EEg8z09LdM.key_idea: Learn latent-tree branch points via simplex-valued triplet-center assignments under the median property, then identify the root by three-terminal independence and orient edges away from it.
EEg8z09LdM.evidence: Synthetic experiments across diverse latent-tree structures (reviews mention 190 topologies), plus the White Wine Quality dataset and a VAE-based generative model.
EEg8z09LdM.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports strong structure recovery without numbers).
EEg8z09LdM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the TTI root characterization and the separation of skeleton recovery from orientation as a useful theoretical contribution, with synthetic evaluation covering varied tree topologies.
EEg8z09LdM.main_concern: The recovery guarantee assumes the learned distances form a tree metric, but the optimization does not enforce this, leaving a gap between the theory and the algorithm.

fGez0hx1gX.one_liner: Orthogonal fine-tuning with a tangent update that restores exact orthogonality only when measured drift reaches a tolerance.
fGez0hx1gX.problem: Existing OFT methods build an exact or approximate orthogonal transform at every step, and the construction parameter does not reliably control realized orthogonality (OFTv2 checkpoints show defects spanning five orders of magnitude).
fGez0hx1gX.method: Restarted Tangent Orthogonal Finetuning (RTOFT) updates weights as W(I+S) with S skew-symmetric, monitors the norm of S, and restores exact orthogonality before the next forward pass when drift reaches tolerance tau. Since the defect equals the squared spectral norm of S exactly, this bounds the defect by tau squared independently of loss, data, model, or optimizer.
fGez0hx1gX.key_idea: Use the exact identity that the defect of I+S equals the squared spectral norm of S as a loss-independent drift monitor that triggers restoration of exact orthogonality.
fGez0hx1gX.evidence: Block-diagonal, subspace, and butterfly parameterizations, with GLUE results over five shared seeds; reviews mention ablations separating tangent adaptation, fixed-period restoration, drift-triggered restoration, and per-step restoration, and PEFT-Arena.
fGez0hx1gX.claimed_gains: Training time drops from 1.10-1.58x LoRA's wall-clock to 0.97-1.12x, and the block variant runs at 0.97x LoRA's wall-clock while exceeding LoRA by 1.98 +/- 0.39 points on the six-task GLUE average over five shared seeds.
fGez0hx1gX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the drift-triggered restoration idea clean and well motivated, supported by controlled ablations, and aimed at a real overhead of maintaining orthogonality in OFT.
fGez0hx1gX.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the evidence supports the drift trigger itself: efficiency results rely mostly on fixed-period restoration, drift is checked only every twenty steps on PEFT-Arena, and the tau sensitivity study covers only CoLA and RTE.

mjp4kXucmp.one_liner: Parallel draft model trained with prefix-confidence-weighted token loss and stochastic gating of target features for dual-mode speculative decoding.
mjp4kXucmp.problem: Draft-model training objectives are not aligned with the inference-time goal of maximizing consecutive token acceptance.
mjp4kXucmp.method: PARD-2 builds on PARD with Confidence-Adaptive Token (CAT) optimization, which reweights each token by the cumulative target-model confidence over its prefix. Stochastic gating of target hidden features lets one draft model run in target-dependent or target-independent mode, serving a model family without retraining.
mjp4kXucmp.key_idea: Weight each draft-token loss by cumulative target confidence over its prefix, and randomly gate target hidden features during training so one drafter serves both modes.
mjp4kXucmp.evidence: Experiments on Llama3 and Qwen3 models; reviews mention ablations on CAT and gating, greedy decoding, and single-chain comparisons.
mjp4kXucmp.claimed_gains: Up to 6.94x lossless acceleration in target-dependent mode and up to 5.71x in target-independent mode.
mjp4kXucmp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the dual-mode design, where one checkpoint supports both modes with little cost from gating, and the motivation of aligning training weights with expected acceptance length.
mjp4kXucmp.main_concern: CAT's isolated gain is modest and its principled interpretation is overstated (average speedup rises from 4.23x to 4.36x over the best fixed decay), and target-independent mode is tested only across Qwen3 sizes.

PIj90T0pCO.one_liner: Post-trains all-atom protein generators with endpoint-based reinforcement plus temporary supervision on high-reward endpoints found by reward-guided search.
PIj90T0pCO.problem: Reinforcement post-training of protein generators is expensive over long denoising trajectories, while inference-time search improves candidates without updating the model.
PIj90T0pCO.method: SARP (Search-Augmented Reinforcement Post-Training) combines trajectory-free endpoint-based reinforcement with temporary supervision on high-reward endpoints discovered through reward-guided search, so design quality improves under standard sampling.
PIj90T0pCO.key_idea: Distill reward-guided search into the generator by supervising on high-reward endpoints found by search, alongside trajectory-free endpoint-based reinforcement.
PIj90T0pCO.evidence: Small-molecule binder, enzyme-design (five targets), and DNA-binder design (three held-out targets) tasks, compared with the pretrained model and DGPO, plus independent AlphaFold3 cross-evaluation.
PIj90T0pCO.claimed_gains: Binding energy falls by up to 14.6 REU and RF3 min-iPAE by up to 2.2 A versus the pretrained model; enzymes reach 42.2 unique successes per 100 designs versus 11.2 (pretrained) and 35.6 (DGPO); DNA binders reach an 8.33% unique pass rate versus 3.33% (pretrained) and 6% (DGPO).
PIj90T0pCO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see distilling expensive search into the generator as well motivated, with gains over the pretrained model and the RL-only baseline and useful ablations comparing search-derived and rollout-derived supervision.
PIj90T0pCO.main_concern: Reviewers say the benefit of search over cheaper rollout supervision is not shown under a matched compute budget, and the method largely combines existing DGPO, beam search, and reward-selected supervision.

UsY1AKR8JG.one_liner: Learns a diagnostic speech judge, using about 300 human labels to calibrate acoustic hints for a frontier audio model.
UsY1AKR8JG.problem: Most automatic speech judges reduce quality to one naturalness score, and prompting a frontier audio-language model for dimension-level labels is error-prone and unstable.
UsY1AKR8JG.method: For each perceptual dimension, SpeechCritic selects acoustic measurements that agree with human judgments, maps them to A/Tie/B probabilities, and passes these to the audio-language model as non-binding hints alongside the audio. A 7B judge is then trained on this supervision with different training signals.
UsY1AKR8JG.key_idea: Use a few hundred human labels to choose, per dimension, the acoustic measurements that agree with humans, and feed them to the frontier model as non-binding hints.
UsY1AKR8JG.evidence: A reference-conditioned cross-lingual setting built from about 300 human-labeled comparisons; reviews mention a 290-comparison English-Japanese test set and a paired bootstrap on the calibration result.
UsY1AKR8JG.claimed_gains: Compared with the same model labeling without hints, dimension-level agreement with humans rises by 6.3 points and mismatch with human Tie rates falls by 10.4 points.
UsY1AKR8JG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find using a few hundred human labels to calibrate a machine labeler sensible and cost-efficient, supported by a paired bootstrap on the calibration gain and candid reporting of trade-offs.
UsY1AKR8JG.main_concern: There is no student baseline trained on uncalibrated direct Gemini labels, so the final judge's gain from human-calibrated supervision is not isolated.

EX1ZShBEom.one_liner: Treats extreme VLM KV-cache eviction as query-conditioned budget allocation to layout-aware 2D regions rather than global token ranking.
EX1ZShBEom.problem: At 1-3% KV budgets, global top-k token ranking spreads the cache over many locations and leaves each visual region with too few tokens to stay usable.
EX1ZShBEom.method: CARVE partitions visual tokens into layout-aware cells, commits most of the budget to a few query-ranked regions, and selects tokens within them. When selection-time diagnostics find this unsuitable it falls back to attention-based selection, and the gated mode CARVE-G falls back to conservative token-level eviction.
EX1ZShBEom.key_idea: Commit most of the KV budget to a few query-ranked 2D cells so chosen regions keep enough tokens, with diagnostic-triggered fallback to attention-based selection.
EX1ZShBEom.evidence: Four models and four benchmarks at equal KV budget; reviews mention ablations against one-dimensional selection and uniform or random region allocation.
EX1ZShBEom.claimed_gains: On DocVQA at a 1% budget, CARVE retains 77.4% of the full-cache score on InternVL3-8B versus 40% for the strongest text-guided baseline (up to +31.3 on DocVQA at 1%), and CARVE-G stays within 1.6 points of its text-guided fallback in all sixteen model-budget settings.
EX1ZShBEom.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gains at extreme budgets are substantial across models, that ablations support spatial allocation, and that the method is deployment-friendly.
EX1ZShBEom.main_concern: The full method relies on many insufficiently isolated heuristics and hyperparameters (signal switching, fallback thresholds, hybrid scoring), and the need for 1-3% budgets is not motivated.

RjEx6MSVtM.one_liner: Detects AI-generated images using frozen VQ-VAE reconstruction trajectories in CLIP space, weighted per stage by VAR token negative log-likelihoods.
RjEx6MSVtM.problem: Detectors based on static image representations or endpoint reconstruction discrepancies miss forensic evidence in intermediate coarse-to-fine reconstruction stages, which limits generalization to new generators.
RjEx6MSVtM.method: RED represents the reconstruction trajectory from a frozen multiscale VQ-VAE in the feature space of a frozen CLIP encoder and learns image-adaptive stage weights from scale-wise token negative log-likelihoods of a frozen VAR model. A cross-stage evidence aggregation module then models the original-image representation together with the weighted reconstruction features.
RjEx6MSVtM.key_idea: Weight each coarse-to-fine reconstruction stage by VAR token negative log-likelihood, because real versus generated token predictability reverses across scales, then aggregate across stages.
RjEx6MSVtM.evidence: Six evaluation collections with ablations, robustness evaluations, source-only model selection, and an alternative real-image source test, as described in reviews.
RjEx6MSVtM.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract text provided; reviews report 92.5% average accuracy and 97.5% AP across six collections.
RjEx6MSVtM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the scale-dependent reversal in token predictability a well-motivated observation, with ablations supporting both intermediate states and NLL guidance and strong generalization across six collections.
RjEx6MSVtM.main_concern: Reviewers say the mechanism of NLL-guided weighting is not directly tested (no analysis of learned stage weights or shuffled-NLL control), and inference cost and memory are not reported.

GoPHJpAQE7.one_liner: Repairs a misspecified dense proxy reward using sparse trajectory outcomes queried on trajectory prefixes and exploration data.
GoPHJpAQE7.problem: Dense proxy rewards are often misspecified and lead to reward hacking, while sparse outcomes are reliable but weakly guiding, and since an outcome measures only total trajectory reward, a correction can fit every outcome yet favor the wrong policy.
GoPHJpAQE7.method: AIR2 queries outcomes on trajectory prefixes to catch errors that cancel within a trajectory, and collects outcomes from an exploration policy to cover behavior the data missed. It also estimates a potential function alongside the correction so harmless shaping is not mistaken for error, then freezes the correction and passes it to a standard RL learner.
GoPHJpAQE7.key_idea: Query outcomes on trajectory prefixes and exploration rollouts to identify policy-relevant reward errors, while a jointly estimated potential separates harmless shaping from error.
GoPHJpAQE7.evidence: A regret bound via an ambiguity modulus, plus experiments on 22 continuous control tasks with constructed reward misspecifications, ablations, and a comparison with HERON.
GoPHJpAQE7.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off before reporting results).
GoPHJpAQE7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the framing of asking which policy comparisons outcomes can identify and the theoretical analysis, with ablations supporting the design and large recoveries on tasks such as Door-open and Peg-unplug.
GoPHJpAQE7.main_concern: AIR2 receives richer feedback (cardinal returns at multiple horizons plus exploration) than preference-based baselines, and total feedback and interaction cost is not accounted for, so the source of the gain is unclear.

xtMGsGokzG.one_liner: Post-training quantization for geometry transformers adding special-token bias correction beyond rotation, predicted by a leverage statistic Gamma.
xtMGsGokzG.problem: Rotation and smoothing PTQ methods apply the same transform to every token, so they cannot remove the differentiated quantization degradation of special tokens with high output leverage in feed-forward geometry transformers.
xtMGsGokzG.method: QMapAnything treats floating-point-preserving rotation and smoothing as a token-blind reparameterization group, proved to give common-mode gains while leaving relative token SNR unchanged, and adds differentiated bias correction for special tokens. A statistic Gamma, combining a special token's quantization disadvantage and output leverage, predicts when that correction is needed.
xtMGsGokzG.key_idea: Rotation and smoothing leave relative token SNR unchanged, so a special-token bias correction is added where statistic Gamma, combining quantization disadvantage and output leverage, predicts it is needed.
xtMGsGokzG.evidence: Geometric benchmarks at W4A8 and W8A8 with measured memory and speed; reviews mention MapAnything, VGGT, DA3, and W4A4 comparisons against standard PTQ baselines.
xtMGsGokzG.claimed_gains: W4A8 closely matches full-precision performance; under W8A8, peak memory falls by 2.2-3.1x versus FP32, with up to 3.1x speedup.
xtMGsGokzG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a well-motivated, simple method with near-lossless W4A8 accuracy, gains over standard PTQ baselines, and a useful unified view of rotation and smoothing under special tokens.
xtMGsGokzG.main_concern: The structural properties and results are tied to the MapAnything architecture, and apart from the special-token bias every component is an existing technique (rotation, bias correction, gradient refinement).

ludS0SUwJC.one_liner: Trains watermark robustness against a sequential differentiable adversary that selects attack families via straight-through Gumbel-Softmax with entropy regularization.
ludS0SUwJC.problem: Random post-processing augmentation under-covers the combinatorial space of realistic attack pipelines and rarely hits the rare compositions that break detection, which makes training unstable and sample-inefficient.
ludS0SUwJC.method: CAT casts watermark robustness as a min-max problem over compositional transformations. A plug-in sequential adversary observes the current intermediate image and selects an attack family at each step to maximally disrupt message recovery, using straight-through Gumbel-Softmax selection with entropy regularization.
ludS0SUwJC.key_idea: A sequential adversary conditioned on the intermediate image picks attack families through straight-through Gumbel-Softmax, with entropy regularization preventing collapse to a single attack.
ludS0SUwJC.evidence: Post-generation watermarks VideoSeal 0.0, VideoSeal 1.0, and PixelSeal and in-generation WMAR, under single-step and two-step attack suites, on in-distribution and out-of-distribution image and video benchmarks.
ludS0SUwJC.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says CAT outperforms random-augmentation baselines at the same number of gradient updates and augmentation budget, with the largest gains on hard attacks, but gives no numbers).
ludS0SUwJC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CAT gives consistent improvements over random augmentation across watermarking models and datasets, addressing rare compositional attacks with broad image, video, and autoregressive evaluation.
ludS0SUwJC.main_concern: The adversary only composes a predefined library of attack primitives, so robustness to unseen attacks is unclear (the appendix shows near-chance accuracy against diffusion-based regeneration), and comparisons with related adversarial-training methods are mostly cost analyses.

OnQCb08Xe9.one_liner: Removes backdoors from vision-language models by projecting out hijacked weight-update directions identified against a pseudo-benign reference model.
OnQCb08Xe9.problem: Existing LVLM backdoor defenses need extensive clean-data retraining or per-query inference-time intervention, and finding hijacked directions requires a benign reference model that defenders usually lack.
OnQCb08Xe9.method: OrthoPurify fine-tunes the pretrained weights on a small clean set to obtain a pseudo-benign reference, uses it to isolate the hijacked weight-update directions, and removes them with a single orthogonal projection on the weight update.
OnQCb08Xe9.key_idea: Backdoors divert a few weight-update directions from task adaptation to shortcut encoding (direction hijacking), so one orthogonal projection against a pseudo-benign reference removes them.
OnQCb08Xe9.evidence: Experiments across diverse benchmarks; reviews mention multiple LVLM architectures, backdoor attacks, downstream tasks, adaptive attacks, clean-model evaluations, and direction-selection controls.
OnQCb08Xe9.claimed_gains: Reduces the attack success rate to near zero while preserving original performance across diverse benchmarks, with no further numbers stated.
OnQCb08Xe9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like that the method needs few clean samples and no inference-time overhead, is computationally simple, and reaches near-zero attack success rate across attacks and LVLM architectures with clean utility largely preserved.
OnQCb08Xe9.main_concern: Adaptive-attack robustness depends on a threshold that is hard to choose in practice (residual ASR of 91.4-96.1% at the default 50 degrees versus 0% at 20 degrees), and comparisons omit recent post-training purification methods.

eoeXgTDQvj.one_liner: RGB-only semantic Gaussian SLAM that keeps open-vocabulary semantics in a separate sparse voxel map with revisable observation provenance.
eoeXgTDQvj.problem: Gaussian-based semantic SLAM attaches semantics to evolving Gaussians, which makes fusion hard to maintain and costly, while hybrid Gaussian-voxel methods often need RGB-D or known poses and do not revise historical semantic evidence after geometry updates.
eoeXgTDQvj.method: UniGS-SLAM uses foundation priors to enhance monocular depth and pose estimation and fuses semantic observations into an independent sparse voxel map with observation provenance, so past contributions can be revised as reconstruction evolves. The fused semantics then guide Gaussian filtering and local surface refinement.
eoeXgTDQvj.key_idea: Keep open-vocabulary semantics in a sparse voxel map that records observation provenance, so semantic evidence can be retracted and re-fused after geometry updates and can guide Gaussian filtering.
eoeXgTDQvj.evidence: Experiments on Replica, ScanNet, and KITTI-360 for tracking, rendering, and geometric reconstruction, plus open-set semantic mapping on Replica and ScanNet.
eoeXgTDQvj.claimed_gains: Leading tracking, rendering, and geometric reconstruction performance among representative RGB-only methods, and a 2.37x reconstruction speedup over the fastest compared semantic SLAM baseline.
eoeXgTDQvj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the semantic-to-geometry feedback loop and observation-level semantic revision a reasonable, well-structured contribution with strong results across tracking, rendering, and mapping.
eoeXgTDQvj.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing comparisons (Hier-SLAM, MonoGS, OpenMonoGS-SLAM) and limited novelty beyond stacking DROID-SLAM, Splat-SLAM, and a Depth-Anything-3 prior without isolating each component's cost and benefit.

RyzSMVgXVB.one_liner: Cost-aware selector choosing the cheapest sufficient representation (caption, text, or image) of each retrieved page under a token budget.
RyzSMVgXVB.problem: Reading retrieved multimodal evidence is costly, with representation costs differing by more than an order of magnitude; rich representations waste budget while uniformly cheap ones can discard answer-critical evidence.
RyzSMVgXVB.method: GATOR adds query-dependent granularity selection to relevance ranking, using a greedy selector that balances relevance, redundancy, and cost under a token budget and keeps at most one representation per page. A lightweight scorer learns representation preferences from automatically derived weak supervision and on-policy distillation without LLM calls, and the selector can take host retrieval scores.
RyzSMVgXVB.key_idea: A greedy budgeted selector scores each page representation by relevance, redundancy, and cost, keeping at most one granularity per page, with a lightweight scorer trained on weak supervision.
RyzSMVgXVB.evidence: UniDoc and MMDocRAG, run standalone and mounted on the Mem0 and A-Mem memory systems.
RyzSMVgXVB.claimed_gains: Standalone GATOR reduces token-equivalent evidence cost by 41.3% and 59.4% relative to Vanilla RAG while improving answer F1; mounted on Mem0 and A-Mem it reduces evidence cost by up to 88.5%, with F1 changes from -0.011 to +0.042.
RyzSMVgXVB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a simple, easy-to-plug approach to an important and underexplored efficiency problem, with strong results and integration into memory systems without retraining or re-indexing.
RyzSMVgXVB.main_concern: It is unclear whether the gains come from granularity choice or from better page selection, since GATOR changes both and the vanilla RAG baseline does neither (BM25 page selection alone lifts a score from 0.194 to 0.274).

69ScEMmTG7.one_liner: Distills a dense teacher into a diffusion LM that uses sparse attention and reused KV caches, via selective replay.
69ScEMmTG7.problem: Bidirectional diffusion language models recompute KV states for long prompts during generation at substantial cost, and sparse attention or cache reuse yields approximate states the model was not trained on.
69ScEMmTG7.method: REPRISE distills a frozen dense teacher into a student using sparse attention and reused caches. Selective replay exploits generation refreshes that overwrite historical generation KV, rebuilding only the cache computations needed by selected predictions so later losses train prompt-cache construction; inference pairs sparse prompt attention with separate prompt and generation refresh schedules.
69ScEMmTG7.key_idea: Rebuild only the cache computations needed by selected predictions during training, so losses on reused-cache predictions back-propagate into prompt-cache construction.
69ScEMmTG7.evidence: UltraLLaDA-8B on RULER and LongBench V1/V2 under shared parallel decoding, plus matched later-block tests comparing selective replay with activation-checkpointed full-history reconstruction.
69ScEMmTG7.claimed_gains: 5.05x and 1.55x complete-generation speedups over Dual Cache on RULER 32K and LongBench V1 subsets, with an 8.59-point RULER score gain; selective replay matches full-history gradients using 8.7-17.6% of its update time and 22.4-46.6% of its peak GPU memory.
69ScEMmTG7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training design addresses a concrete mismatch between fresh-state training and reused-cache inference, with controlled evidence of gains mainly on RULER and substantial speedups.
69ScEMmTG7.main_concern: Evidence that cache-aware training improves natural-task quality is narrow: LongBench V1 paired confidence intervals include zero, and LongBench V2 gains come mostly from examples where baselines produce unparseable outputs.

FJ5FCggkhG.one_liner: Particle-based test-time scaling that advances each distinct complete state once, storing repeated states with multiplicity while drawing independent continuations.
FJ5FCggkhG.problem: After resampling many particles share the same complete state, yet sequence runtimes decode each separately, and prefix-aware KV sharing still repeats the Transformer pass and vocabulary projection, so execution cost scales with particle count.
FJ5FCggkhG.method: PluralGen keeps particles as the unit of search but stores each repeated state once with its multiplicity, draws an independent continuation for every particle, and carries the grouping through model execution, resampling, and KV ownership.
FJ5FCggkhG.key_idea: Group particles that share a complete state into one execution row with a multiplicity count while sampling independent continuations per particle, leaving search semantics unchanged.
FJ5FCggkhG.evidence: Evaluated workloads include ASMC and Power-SMC on benchmarks such as AIME 2026 and MATH500 (per reviews), with ablations and an SGLang-based implementation.
FJ5FCggkhG.claimed_gains: 3.2x end-to-end speedup, 88.1% lower KV allocation, 4x larger populations, and 2.9x higher serving throughput on the evaluated workloads.
FJ5FCggkhG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the execution-search decoupling a clean, well-defined idea with convincing systems evidence and exact equivalence to standard sequence-wise SMC.
FJ5FCggkhG.main_concern: Evaluation covers only ASMC and Power-SMC (no lookahead, backtracking, or tree search), and speedups shrink under low state concentration, small populations, or long prompt prefill.

sr7MI7H9gA.one_liner: On-policy distillation for temporal video grounding that combines pointwise teacher imitation with IoU-derived listwise ranking of teacher proposals.
sr7MI7H9gA.problem: Token-level on-policy distillation does not require the student's preferences over complete answers to reflect their localization quality, so answers with the right action but wrong temporal extent are not distinguished.
sr7MI7H9gA.method: Geo-OPD uses teacher proposals both as answers to imitate and as alternatives to rank, combining pointwise imitation of a teacher answer with listwise supervision that aligns the student's sequence scores with an annotation-IoU-derived preference distribution. Adaptive token guidance balances soft and sharp teacher views by temporal discrepancy, and reliability filtering selects teacher supervision.
sr7MI7H9gA.key_idea: Align the student's relative sequence scores over teacher proposals with a preference distribution derived from IoU against the annotation, in addition to imitating one teacher answer.
sr7MI7H9gA.evidence: Charades-TimeLens, ActivityNet-TimeLens, and QVHighlights-TimeLens against reported distillation baselines, with ablations over the loss components.
sr7MI7H9gA.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports improvements over distillation baselines without numbers and notes the listwise benefit varies across datasets).
sr7MI7H9gA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gap between the primary and the best teacher proposal motivates using multiple teacher answers, and that guiding answer preferences by interval localization quality is reasonable and clearly presented.
sr7MI7H9gA.main_concern: Novelty is seen as incremental, and the listwise term, the main idea, adds little over adaptive guidance plus pointwise imitation (nothing on Charades), with no matched comparison against existing ranking or preference objectives.

3NBIIpYenn.one_liner: Fuses DINOv3 and SigLIP features into 196 visual tokens via Sinkhorn-weighted patch-wise residuals mapped through a shared orthogonal transform.
3NBIIpYenn.problem: Language-aligned and self-supervised visual encoders have complementary semantic and spatial strengths, but using both requires injecting language-aligned semantics into local visual representations without lengthening the visual token sequence.
3NBIIpYenn.method: PAIQ uses DINOv3 features as the base and projects both streams into the language-model dimension; learned content similarities and a finite-step Sinkhorn procedure set how SigLIP features are aggregated per patch. A shared orthogonal transformation maps the difference between aggregated and base features, and the residual is added back with a fixed scale while both encoders and the language model stay frozen.
3NBIIpYenn.key_idea: Add a SigLIP-derived residual, aggregated per patch by Sinkhorn and rotated by a shared orthogonal map, to DINOv3 features, preserving residual norms and pairwise angles.
3NBIIpYenn.evidence: Five language backbones and four evaluated datasets, compared with single-encoder, multi-encoder, and token-compression baselines.
3NBIIpYenn.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports higher correctness and lower hallucination severity than single-encoder baselines in most settings, with no numbers; the fused sequence keeps 196 visual tokens).
3NBIIpYenn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometric constraint from orthogonal residuals clearly specified and the validation across multiple language backbones reasonable, with the full method beating single encoders in most settings.
3NBIIpYenn.main_concern: Simple fusion baselines such as channel concatenation are missing, and the ablations do not separate the contributions of Sinkhorn aggregation and the orthogonal constraint.

SwGtiMX805.one_liner: Compares data-selection pipelines for natural long documents in 128K context extension, finding LongPPL key-token density selection scores highest.
SwGtiMX805.problem: Document length alone does not reveal whether natural long documents provide useful long-range supervision for extending language models to longer contexts.
SwGtiMX805.method: Under a controlled 128K protocol with 256K validation, using Qwen2.5-3B and matched 6B-token budgets, the study compares repacking shorter documents, random sampling of natural long documents, and generic-quality, LLM-judge, and likelihood-based selection. It then selects documents by their density of LongPPL key tokens.
SwGtiMX805.key_idea: Rank natural long documents by the density of LongPPL key tokens, whose predictions improve markedly when the long context is available.
SwGtiMX805.evidence: Qwen2.5-3B with 128K-token continued training and matched 6B-token budgets, using HELMET tasks for model selection and RULER for held-out evaluation, plus 256K validation.
SwGtiMX805.claimed_gains: Random sampling leads repacking by approximately 2.5 HELMET points and 3.3 RULER points at 128K, and selection by LongPPL key-token density achieves the highest observed scores among the evaluated pipelines.
SwGtiMX805.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clean, controlled comparison of complete selection pipelines under matched budgets, with HELMET used for tuning, RULER held out, and informative analysis showing gains concentrated in retrieval-oriented tasks.
SwGtiMX805.main_concern: The paper is mainly an empirical comparison of existing selectors, its truncLongPPL variant is a simple truncation of LongPPL, and selection rates are not controlled across pipelines.

QIUGvz1Dsb.one_liner: Second-order neural ODE for single-cell temporal prediction that adds an explicit velocity state and an optimal-transport-initialized initial velocity.
QIUGvz1Dsb.problem: First-order neural ODE methods let position and time alone set velocity, but hidden kinetic variables such as unspliced RNA and dimensionality reduction can make latent dynamics depend on history that position does not record.
QIUGvz1Dsb.method: scMomenta augments latent position with an explicit velocity state and learns a damped acceleration field. An initial-velocity module estimates each cell's velocity by optimal transport.
QIUGvz1Dsb.key_idea: Make latent cell dynamics second-order by adding a velocity state with a learned damped acceleration field, initialized with per-cell velocities from optimal transport.
QIUGvz1Dsb.evidence: Five time-course datasets against six competing methods, plus experiments on latent dynamical order, trajectory crossing, and velocity-space perturbation.
QIUGvz1Dsb.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports strong overall performance against six competing methods without numbers).
QIUGvz1Dsb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that asking whether position alone is a sufficient state is meaningful, and that the biophysical, mathematical, and empirical motivation for second-order dynamics is supported, with the best results in most settings.
QIUGvz1Dsb.main_concern: Reviewers argue the objective and OT-derived initial velocities do not explicitly favor momentum-preserving couplings, and that the initialization assumes early snapshots are observed, which competing methods do not.

RhVLl37uHA.one_liner: Training-free visual token pruning combining pixel-level spectral saliency anchors with adaptively fused query-relevance selection.
RhVLl37uHA.problem: Token importance estimated after patchification or spatial aggregation may weaken fine-grained structure, and existing query-guided pruning often relies on a single relevance signal that may not capture visual token and query correspondence.
RhVLl37uHA.method: SQ-Pruner has two stages: Spectral Saliency Anchoring (SSA) estimates pixel-level spectral saliency before visual encoding to keep structurally informative tokens as anchors, and Query-Guided Relevance Selection (QRS) adaptively fuses query-related signals to select tokens from the remaining candidates.
RhVLl37uHA.key_idea: Anchor tokens by spectral saliency computed on raw pixels before the visual encoder, then fill the remaining budget with adaptively fused query-relevance scores.
RhVLl37uHA.evidence: Diverse LVLMs and tasks in image and video modalities, with Qwen2.5-VL results, prefill speedup, and ablations of the two stages.
RhVLl37uHA.claimed_gains: On Qwen2.5-VL, SQ-Pruner retains 81.6% of the original performance while pruning 95.1% of visual tokens, outperforming the strongest prior method by 4.3%, with a 1.42x prefilling speedup.
RhVLl37uHA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the simple, training-free design combining image structure with query relevance, with ablations showing both stages help and reduced FLOPs and prefill latency.
RhVLl37uHA.main_concern: Reviewers say the components are existing techniques (spectral residual saliency, attention- or similarity-based token scoring), so methodological novelty is limited.

GzFM1pJ3PN.one_liner: Defines Figurative Vehicle Intrusion in text-to-image generation and introduces the VISTA benchmark, V-Score metric, and VISTA-Guard mitigation.
GzFM1pJ3PN.problem: For figurative prompts, a vehicle that should guide the depiction of a tenor may instead be rendered as a visible object, an error that presence-oriented evaluation can miss.
GzFM1pJ3PN.method: VISTA is a multilingual benchmark of figurative prompts organized by Figurative Form and Mapping Mechanism, V-Score is a diagnostic question-answering metric for role-aware figurative faithfulness, and VISTA-Guard is a lightweight mitigation.
GzFM1pJ3PN.key_idea: Score images with diagnostic questions built on a tenor-vehicle framework to check whether figurative content is assigned the right visual role, not merely whether it is present.
GzFM1pJ3PN.evidence: Evaluations of recent high-performing text-to-image models across languages and figurative categories; reviews mention 1,930 benchmark prompts in four languages, 193 main-experiment samples, and a 30-image human study.
GzFM1pJ3PN.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says VISTA-Guard partially reduces vehicle intrusion, with no numbers).
GzFM1pJ3PN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between visual presence and visual role is clear, useful, and underexplored, supported by a four-language benchmark and a human study of V-Score.
GzFM1pJ3PN.main_concern: V-Score's reliability is not established: the intrusion boundary is subjective, the metric and mitigation are evaluated in a closed loop with an MLLM evaluator, and validation subsets are small (193 samples, 40 prompts, 30 images).

bYWDkFjA4k.one_liner: Distills a reflection-conditioned self-teacher's velocity predictions into a text-to-image student on student-generated states, with reference-centered residual distillation.
bYWDkFjA4k.problem: Using a unified multimodal model's textual feedback on its own images as sparse rewards makes it hard to assign credit to individual generation states across timesteps.
bYWDkFjA4k.method: T2I-OPSD makes the current model both student and self-teacher, with the teacher also conditioned on the student's generated image and textual reflection; matching velocity predictions at shared student-induced states gives dense directional supervision. Reference-centered residual distillation interpolates self-teacher predictions with a frozen prompt-only reference to stabilize supervision.
bYWDkFjA4k.key_idea: Match the student's velocity predictions to those of a self-teacher conditioned on the generated image and its textual reflection, at student-induced states, stabilized by a frozen prompt-only reference.
bYWDkFjA4k.evidence: Multiple text-to-image benchmarks; reviews mention BAGEL initialized from an AlphaGRPO checkpoint, GenEval, DPG-Bench, and TIIF-Bench.
bYWDkFjA4k.claimed_gains: Leading performance in compositional generation without additional sampling steps or inference memory; reviews cite GenEval rising from 77.17 to 85.04 and DPG-Bench from 86.05 to 88.77 over the AlphaGRPO model.
bYWDkFjA4k.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see turning textual reflection into dense state-level targets as a plausible way to internalize correction, with improved compositional results and no inference-time refinement cost.
bYWDkFjA4k.main_concern: The independent contribution of reflection is not isolated, since the teacher also sees the generated image and uses stronger guidance (CFG 1.0 to 2.0), with no ablation that removes or shuffles the reflection.

YUUQwuqvD6.one_liner: Differentially private prototype classifier that projects noisy class means and corrects distance scores, with optional public-feature regularization.
YUUQwuqvD6.problem: Adding noise at the same scale to every class sum makes rare-class means less accurate and inflates squared distances to them, which hurts long-tailed private classification.
YUUQwuqvD6.method: PDC projects noisy class means onto the feature ball and corrects their distance scores for the added noise. When a public feature bank is available, PRDC retrieves features aligned with each released class sum and uses their mean to regularize each private prototype before correcting its score; both are post-processing of a single release with no additional privacy cost.
YUUQwuqvD6.key_idea: Correct the noise-inflated squared distances to rare-class prototypes after projecting them onto the feature ball, optionally shrinking toward a retrieved public-feature mean.
YUUQwuqvD6.evidence: Three image datasets and two imbalance ratios across several privacy settings, with an analysis bounding deviations from non-private class scores and ablations isolating projection, correction, and public-mean retrieval.
YUUQwuqvD6.claimed_gains: Under the three strongest privacy settings, PDC improves balanced accuracy by an average of 20.0 percentage points over direct nearest-prototype classification, and PRDC adds 3.0 points over PDC, with positive average gains in five of six dataset-imbalance settings.
YUUQwuqvD6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the failure mode of noise-inflated distances to small classes is clearly identified and that PDC and PRDC are simple, no-extra-privacy-cost fixes with strong gains and careful ablations at small budgets.
YUUQwuqvD6.main_concern: PRDC helps reliably only when the public bank matches the target domain (it underperforms PDC with a mismatched source in five settings), and no rule is given to detect mismatch or fall back safely.

kbMlZBRXVn.one_liner: Measures per-fact recall probability across post-training checkpoints using repeated rollouts, showing most apparent forgetting is sampling variability.
kbMlZBRXVn.problem: Prior studies of factual forgetting during post-training use aggregate measures that mask individual facts or compare only two checkpoints, so they can mistake sampling noise for knowledge loss.
kbMlZBRXVn.method: The authors estimate each fact's recall probability from repeated rollouts at intermediate checkpoints across the whole post-training trajectory, and formalize a lower bound that certifies knowledge loss in bits and can account for recall fluctuations.
kbMlZBRXVn.key_idea: Treat factual knowledge as a per-fact recall probability estimated from repeated rollouts at each checkpoint, and certify knowledge loss with a lower bound measured in bits.
kbMlZBRXVn.evidence: Repeated rollouts at intermediate checkpoints of open-weight models; reviews mention 100 facts across 55 checkpoints, about 100M rollouts in total, and a stationary-binomial null.
kbMlZBRXVn.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative findings that recall probabilities fluctuate and that prior methods can substantially overestimate persistent knowledge loss).
kbMlZBRXVn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the message useful and well supported: apparent forgotten and reappearing facts arise frequently from finite sampling alone, shown with large-scale rollouts and a stationary-binomial null.
kbMlZBRXVn.main_concern: The certified-loss bound relies on i.i.d. Bernoulli assumptions that the rollout protocol (one greedy response among 128) does not strictly meet, and the findings come from small open-weight models, leaving frontier post-training pipelines untested.

tJ2ONFedVz.one_liner: Compares direct tool exposure with wrapping a service's tools behind an inner agent, measured from the service provider's perspective.
tJ2ONFedVz.problem: Existing studies take the client's perspective with a fixed tool set, and none quantify what a client agent gains when a provider offers a capable agent wrapper as one tool instead of exposing all low-level tools.
tJ2ONFedVz.method: A dedicated controlled experiment compares Direct Tool Exposure (DTE) with Agent-as-a-Tool (AaT) across models, task complexities, and tool configurations, including cross-model and same-model pairings.
tJ2ONFedVz.key_idea: Hold the tools fixed and vary only whether they are exposed directly or wrapped behind a service agent, separating capability transfer from token overhead.
tJ2ONFedVz.evidence: Controlled experiments across multiple models, task complexities, and tool-catalog sizes, with stronger-inner and weaker-inner cross-model pairings.
tJ2ONFedVz.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports qualitative findings: AaT's benefits are mainly capability transfer, and DTE's token cost grows more sharply as the tool surface scales).
tJ2ONFedVz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the provider-side question useful and the controlled cross-model experiments clear, separating capability transfer from stronger-model effects and showing token savings as tool catalogs grow.
tJ2ONFedVz.main_concern: Reviewers say the findings are largely intuitive with limited novelty, and the token comparison gives DTE the full tool catalog every turn without retrieval or filtering baselines.

nLREuW3zrL.one_liner: Dataset and benchmark pairing good and degraded camera views with known 6-DoF motions for aesthetic-guided viewpoint editing.
nLREuW3zrL.problem: Improving image composition requires small viewpoint changes involving full 3D translation and rotation, but no dataset couples fine-grained 6-DoF camera changes with substantial composition improvement.
nLREuW3zrL.method: Aes6D covers nine composition patterns and provides complete 6-DoF supervision with Single and Multi samples, using aesthetic guidance so small viewpoint changes consistently improve composition. Per reviews, it starts from good views, degrades composition to make bad views, uses the reverse motion as ground truth, and trains an MLLM with GRPO to predict camera motion.
nLREuW3zrL.key_idea: Build training pairs by degrading good views along composition-specific camera motions and using the reverse motion as the 6-DoF ground truth.
nLREuW3zrL.evidence: A benchmark with nine composition patterns and Single and Multi samples; reviews cite human evaluation on about 100 benchmark samples and a 50-image out-of-distribution test.
nLREuW3zrL.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off before results; reviews cite an 83% human win rate over Bad Views on approximately 100 benchmark samples).
nLREuW3zrL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the task real and interesting and the data construction well aligned with it, linking composition principles to explicit camera adjustments with known motion parameters.
nLREuW3zrL.main_concern: Evidence for precise 6-DoF control and generalization is thin: there are no per-DoF errors, composition is judged by an aesthetic model, and the 50-image out-of-distribution human win rate is 56% versus 54% for the strongest baseline without uncertainty estimates.

3uuuDJFo5I.one_liner: Latent reasoning for speech language models that models multiple continuations and predicts chunks of future states, with RL-adapted effort.
3uuuDJFo5I.problem: Explicit chain-of-thought improves speech-model reasoning but delays responses, while existing latent reasoning trails CoT and is limited by single-path supervision and reasoning budgets that do not adapt to problem difficulty.
3uuuDJFo5I.method: AURAL models a distribution over multiple plausible reasoning continuations in latent space and jointly predicts chunks of future states to reduce sequential forward passes.
