It is initialized with AuralReason-683K (683K bilingual speech utterances, about 1,000 hours, with concise CoT), and AURAL-RL rewards concise reasoning that yields high-quality answers and adapts effort to each problem.
3uuuDJFo5I.key_idea: Predict chunks of future latent reasoning states from a mixture over plausible continuations, then use RL that rewards concise correct reasoning to adapt the number of latent steps per problem.
3uuuDJFo5I.evidence: Two backbones, with AuralReason-683K supervision, comparison to CoT-RL, and analysis showing harder questions elicit more latent steps; reviews mention mixture-component analysis and latency profiling on 256 paired examples.
3uuuDJFo5I.claimed_gains: AURAL-RL achieves performance comparable to CoT-RL across two backbones with larger gains over supervised checkpoints on most metrics; reviews cite mean time to first visible answer token falling from 1.218 s to 0.103 s (11.8x).
3uuuDJFo5I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree low-latency latent reasoning for speech models is of interest and that the experiments, latency profiling, and AuralReason dataset are well executed, with performance largely comparable to text CoT.
3uuuDJFo5I.main_concern: Gains cannot be attributed to latent reasoning because direct SFT and direct RL baselines on AuralReason and speech-based latent reasoning baselines are missing, and results use a single seed.

4Mg0HWnNSL.one_liner: Shows that teaching a model about inoculation prompting before RL raises natural emergent misalignment and weakens the inoculation effect.
4Mg0HWnNSL.problem: Inoculation prompting (IP) neutralizes emergent misalignment from reward hacking in coding RL but rests on a lie, and future models that know more about IP may be harder to inoculate.
4Mg0HWnNSL.method: After lightweight synthetic document finetuning that teaches IP, the authors RL-train a hack-knowledgeable Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct with and without IP and compare natural emergent misalignment against an IP-unaware counterpart, using reasoning trace analysis and concept ablations.
4Mg0HWnNSL.key_idea: Give the model synthetic-document knowledge of IP and its deceptive nature before coding RL, then measure how much emergent misalignment IP leaves behind.
4Mg0HWnNSL.evidence: Coding RL on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct with and without IP, large-scale reasoning trace analysis and concept ablations; reviews mention six evaluations, repeated runs, and an open-source testbed.
4Mg0HWnNSL.claimed_gains: A hack-knowledgeable, IP-aware Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct trained with IP shows about 2.6x the natural EM of its IP-unaware counterpart; reviews cite EM rising from 8.06% to about 19.5%.
4Mg0HWnNSL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the open-weight testbed that elicits natural EM, with ablations, repeated runs, and six evaluations, is a substantial contribution, and the increase in residual misalignment is large enough to matter.
4Mg0HWnNSL.main_concern: Attribution to IP awareness is confounded: an EM-only document group nearly reproduces the full effect, and the absolute benefit of inoculation rises while only the normalized ratio falls.

SsbmYE3tI6.one_liner: Learns humanoid whole-body manipulation from robot-free human demonstrations recorded with wearable contact patches, using contact goals as the transferable signal.
SsbmYE3tI6.problem: Most humanoid loco-manipulation restricts manipulation to the hands and avoids other body contacts, so manipulation with any suitable body surface is not learned from demonstrations.
SsbmYE3tI6.method: PanTact combines a wearable robot-free interface that adds whole-body contact patches to egocentric vision and bimanual UMI grippers, a visuomotor policy that predicts whole-body contact goals while mitigating the egocentric observation gap, and contact-aware whole-body control that realizes active contact goals with suitable robot surfaces.
SsbmYE3tI6.key_idea: Use contact locations and timing as embodiment-transferable task information, and let the robot's controller choose which body surface realizes each contact.
SsbmYE3tI6.evidence: Deployment on a Unitree G1 humanoid without additional body contact sensors, demonstrating body support, pushing, sweeping, and load-sharing; reviews note 10-20 real-robot trials per task.
SsbmYE3tI6.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports real-robot demonstrations of body support, pushing, sweeping, and load-sharing, with no numbers).
SsbmYE3tI6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree contact goals are a useful task-level interface linking wearable sensing, policy learning, and control, with real-robot demonstrations and no extra robot contact sensors.
SsbmYE3tI6.main_concern: Contact realization is under-specified and not shown to be smooth or stable (force from open-loop position offsets, binarized contact goals, jittery videos), and baselines do not isolate the benefit of controller-chosen body surfaces.

EVWvMfhHt5.one_liner: Reinforcement-learning reward that penalizes fragmented and cyclic reflection, modulated by answer entropy and problem difficulty, to shorten reasoning chains.
EVWvMfhHt5.problem: Large reasoning models overthink, and methods that penalize reasoning length or reflection-word counts ignore problem difficulty and reflective structure, which may cause frequent path switching and fragmented reflection.
EVWvMfhHt5.method: The reflection reward (EARR, per reviews) integrates answer entropy and difficulty awareness, based on analyses of reflection-word counts, continuous reasoning spans, and answer distributions. It constrains inefficient reflection in two scenarios (high accuracy with low entropy, low accuracy with high entropy), penalizing fragmented and cyclic reflection and favoring low-frequency reflection and long continuous spans.
EVWvMfhHt5.key_idea: Modulate a reflection-penalty reward by answer entropy and accuracy so fragmented, cyclic reflection is penalized while long continuous reasoning spans are favored.
EVWvMfhHt5.evidence: Experiments on two backbones (reviews mention a 1.5B R1-Distill model and Qwen3-8B) on MATH-500 and MMLU against baselines including ARLCP, with ablations of reward components and reflection lexicons.
EVWvMfhHt5.claimed_gains: Reduces token consumption in chain-of-thought reasoning without reducing performance; reviews cite average length reductions of 53.4% and 57.3% with accuracy gains of 4.0 and 1.4 points over Vanilla.
EVWvMfhHt5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the empirical results strong and broad, with the largest length reduction against recent baselines on both backbones while accuracy is kept or improved, using a simple reward that is cheap to add to GRPO.
EVWvMfhHt5.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited relative to ARLCP and DAST, and ablations suggest the entropy factor trades accuracy for length rather than improving both.

M40vxoReQo.one_liner: Reformulates multi-view compositional 3D generation as scene-level pose reasoning through a Guide-Route-Reconcile paradigm using reconstruction-derived geometry.
M40vxoReQo.problem: Existing approaches either entangle scene layout with object generation or estimate placement separately from view-specific observations, so pose hypotheses stay ambiguous and inconsistent across views, producing an incoherent object-camera soup.
M40vxoReQo.method: SPOON coordinates view-specific object pose hypotheses using reconstruction-derived multi-view geometry through Guide, Route, and Reconcile stages, progressively organizing object poses and camera configurations into a coherent scene-level arrangement. Per reviews, Guide uses point-cloud alignment with flow guidance, Route is a scoring heuristic with truncation filtering, and Reconcile is analogous to bundle adjustment.
M40vxoReQo.key_idea: Coordinate per-view object pose hypotheses jointly with multi-view reconstruction geometry through Guide, Route, and Reconcile stages instead of estimating each view's poses independently.
M40vxoReQo.evidence: Experiments on ARSG-110K and MIDI-3D-Front across varying numbers of input views.
M40vxoReQo.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off before the numbers; it says SPOON gives consistent improvements in object placement and scene composition across input-view counts).
M40vxoReQo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the object-camera soup problem precisely defined and the Guide-Route-Reconcile workflow reasonable, with better layouts and placements than baselines on two benchmarks that stay stable as views increase.
M40vxoReQo.main_concern: Reviewers see mostly a system integration of existing modules (point-cloud alignment, flow guidance, bundle-adjustment-like reconciliation) with limited mechanistic novelty and no analysis of error propagation across stages.

8pcv7KZH4L.one_liner: Runtime guard that repairs injected tool arguments from protected records or one scoped question, using deterministic checks.
8pcv7KZH4L.problem: An execution guard can refuse a hijacked call but cannot recover its intended value, such as the payee, so a person must finish the task and the handoff cost keeps agents from running unattended.
8pcv7KZH4L.method: Before deployment an agent reads each tool's schema and writes a contract naming consequential arguments and the trusted sources that hold their copies, with a linter admitting or rejecting each entry. At runtime a deterministic check compares each guarded argument with those sources, restores the value from an independent protected record, asks one scoped question to an authorized source when no record exists, and refuses when neither is available.
8pcv7KZH4L.key_idea: Treat an injected value as corrupted data and recover it by comparing guarded arguments against contract-named protected sources with a deterministic, model-free check.
8pcv7KZH4L.evidence: AgentDojo rent tasks (reviews mention four tasks with five replicates), plus tau2 retail and AppWorld Gmail results, with conditions stated for when each response is sound.
8pcv7KZH4L.claimed_gains: On AgentDojo rent tasks with the same amount-scoped question channel, AgentECC keeps 13 of 20 runs under injection versus 5 for refusal on GPT-4o and 14 versus 7 on GPT-5.5, and 10 versus 1 on a third model whose name is cut off in the text provided.
8pcv7KZH4L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recovering correct behavior instead of refusing is a useful and novel direction, and that binding fields to protected sources with a deterministic check is a clear systems contribution that improves utility over refusal.
8pcv7KZH4L.main_concern: The trust boundary is weakly justified (an offline agent writes the contracts) and witness applicability is ambiguous, and the evidence rests on constructed cohorts where a qualified witness is deliberately present.

jl7PfWbfeG.one_liner: Benchmark for decoupled retrieval and generation evaluation in long-video RAG, plus a training-free chunk-wise reranker choosing modality-granularity per chunk.
jl7PfWbfeG.problem: Existing long-video RAG benchmarks allow queries to be answered without the video, hiding retrieval errors, and prior methods apply one modality-granularity configuration per query, ignoring chunk-level variability.
jl7PfWbfeG.method: V-RAGBench provides query, evidence chunk, and answer triplets over hour-scale videos in which each answer depends on a unique evidence chunk. CARVE runs parallel retrievers across configurations and uses chunk-adaptive reranking to select a winning configuration for each chunk, which is carried into generation.
jl7PfWbfeG.key_idea: Run retrievers in parallel over several modality-granularity configurations and rerank to pick one configuration per chunk rather than one per query.
jl7PfWbfeG.evidence: V-RAGBench (2,100 queries per the TL;DR) against eight recent VideoRAG baselines, across egocentric and third-person long videos and an expanded configuration space.
jl7PfWbfeG.claimed_gains: CARVE outperforms eight recent VideoRAG baselines on both retrieval and generation on V-RAGBench; no numeric margins are stated in the abstract.
jl7PfWbfeG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark, with careful filtering and human audit, enables stage-wise evaluation of VideoRAG, and that training-free chunk-level configuration selection is relevant, easy to integrate, and gives consistent gains.
jl7PfWbfeG.main_concern: The retrieval comparison does not separate the effect of pooling a larger candidate set from chunk-level selection, and retrieval gains do not consistently translate into QA gains.

YV8OplyuqL.one_liner: Benchmark pairing GUI task trajectories across software versions with Reuse, Reground, Replan labels, plus VAEA to selectively adapt prior experience.
YV8OplyuqL.problem: GUI interfaces change with software updates, so prior experience can stay useful or become outdated and misleading, and existing benchmarks give limited support for controlled evaluation of cross-version experience transfer.
YV8OplyuqL.method: VersionShift fixes task intent while pairing executions across chronological software versions, then semantically aligns paired trajectories to label each target step Reuse (directly executable source action), Reground (applicable semantics needing new grounding), or Replan (no applicable source action). VAEA selectively adapts prior experience to reduce negative transfer.
YV8OplyuqL.key_idea: Annotate each target step's source-experience validity as Reuse, Reground, or Replan so agents can selectively adapt prior experience instead of copying it.
YV8OplyuqL.evidence: 312 tasks and 1,248 trajectories across 53 applications and websites on Mobile, Desktop, and Web; reviews mention 13 evaluated agents and supervised-selection controls.
YV8OplyuqL.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided says historical trajectories can improve action prediction but also introduce substantial negative transfer; reviews cite VAEA beating Supervised Selection + Actor by only 1.12 and 1.03 points in step accuracy).
YV8OplyuqL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree cross-version experience validity is a real problem and that the paired-trajectory benchmark across Mobile, Desktop, and Web is a systematic setting that exposes positive and negative transfer separately.
YV8OplyuqL.main_concern: The benchmark is small (53 apps, 312 tasks, one trajectory per task per version, author-annotated), evaluation uses recorded observations rather than live interaction, and VAEA's margin over supervised selection is about one point without uncertainty estimates.

4fy7N1aVYn.one_liner: Benchmark of 77 Unity game-development tasks scored by 1,178 deterministic in-engine milestone tests, evaluating 21 models across 9 harnesses.
4fy7N1aVYn.problem: Game development depends on how engine APIs, serialized scene state, and runtime behavior interact, and existing benchmarks mainly target Godot and rely heavily on LLM judges or coarse task-level outcomes.
4fy7N1aVYn.method: Each of the 77 tasks, organized around seven expert-defined skill categories and three difficulty tiers, pairs a complete Unity project with natural-language requirements and is scored by held-out, human-authored milestone tests covering scene structure, component configuration, and runtime behavior.
4fy7N1aVYn.key_idea: Score projects with held-out in-engine milestone tests that give deterministic partial credit and localize failures, without relying on LLM judges.
4fy7N1aVYn.evidence: 21 models across 9 coding harnesses (32 model-harness configurations per reviews), each run once per task.
4fy7N1aVYn.claimed_gains: Average pass rate is 80.9% on easy tasks, 35.2% on hard tasks, and 57.7% overall across 21 models and 9 coding harnesses.
4fy7N1aVYn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the benchmark fills a clear evaluation gap for Unity, with deterministic milestone-level partial credit and a broad comparison across models and harnesses.
4fy7N1aVYn.main_concern: Reviewers raise limited novelty beyond extending existing game-development benchmark setups to Unity, unreported run-to-run variance (one run per configuration), and unclear benchmark validation.

k9hRsLVqDf.one_liner: Distills AR models into diffusion LMs by scoring candidate tokens against subsequent text with the teacher's sequence-level scores, on-policy.
k9hRsLVqDf.problem: Causal-prefix supervision ignores the mismatch between an AR teacher that predicts from a left prefix and a diffusion student that reconstructs missing text from context on both sides.
k9hRsLVqDf.method: CrossDLM uses the teacher's sequence-level scores to evaluate candidate tokens in the context of subsequent text, giving supervision for bidirectional reconstruction that uses visible evidence while accounting for uncertainty in unresolved content. Shared teacher computation across token alternatives and aggregation over a few student-generated completions make it practical, within on-policy self-distillation.
k9hRsLVqDf.key_idea: Score each candidate token with the AR teacher in the context of the following student-completed text, accounting for uncertainty of unresolved content, to supervise bidirectional reconstruction.
k9hRsLVqDf.evidence: Converts pretrained AR checkpoints into DLMs and compares with causal-prefix distillation across benchmarks and model families; reviews mention five backbones, GSM8K, MATH-500, and four-token blocks.
k9hRsLVqDf.claimed_gains: Converts pretrained AR checkpoints into DLMs using approximately 0.10B training tokens per model and outperforms causal-prefix distillation across benchmarks and model families; reviews cite Qwen3.5-4B rising from 85.8% to 92.5% on GSM8K and from 68.2% to 78.8% on MATH-500 over OPDLM.
k9hRsLVqDf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the supervision mismatch is concrete and well motivated, with theory tied to implementation and consistent gains over the matched OPDLM baseline across backbones.
k9hRsLVqDf.main_concern: Evaluation lacks comparison with the original AR teachers and decoding efficiency, uses only four-token blocks, and does not isolate importance weighting from uniform aggregation.

Jjc1cLl7WO.one_liner: Zero-shot cross-embodiment manipulation using embodiment-agnostic imagined futures from a world-action model plus an imagination-observation refiner.
Jjc1cLl7WO.problem: Generalist robot policies are fine-tuned for one robot, camera, and control interface, so they are hard to reuse when morphology or camera configuration changes even though the task and object dynamics are unchanged.
Jjc1cLl7WO.method: CrossWAM removes the source arm from the world-action model's imagined future by video inpainting and re-expresses its motion as an abstract gripper trace, then closes the loop with an imagination-observation refiner that compares the imagined future with what the target camera sees and corrects not-yet-executed actions. The abstract lists three components but is cut off before the third.
Jjc1cLl7WO.key_idea: Make the imagined future embodiment-agnostic by inpainting out the arm and keeping a gripper trace, then correct unexecuted actions from the gap between imagined and observed scenes.
Jjc1cLl7WO.evidence: Simulation with camera shifts (reviews mention ARX and a Table 3 ablation) and real-robot studies with 10 trials per condition.
Jjc1cLl7WO.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off before results; reviews cite the refiner adding up to 16.9 points under camera shifts on ARX).
Jjc1cLl7WO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see the imagination-observation refiner as the strongest idea, backed by an ablation, and find the use of the imagined future for cross-embodiment transfer a new perspective with well-constructed simulation and real-world setups.
Jjc1cLl7WO.main_concern: Evidence is thin and baselines are missing or unfair (LAP is not compared, Mirage appears only in an appendix, one simulated ablation embodiment, 10 real trials per condition), and gripper-only assumptions are untested.

rvjI95E3hR.one_liner: Treats block size in diffusion LLMs as a learnable action chosen per input by a high-level GRPO policy.
rvjI95E3hR.problem: Fixed-size block decoding does not extend to multi-domain settings because different domains favor different block sizes, and existing adaptive methods rely on heuristic rules and prompt-specific cues rather than learned selection.
rvjI95E3hR.method: HiBlock is a hierarchical policy framework trained with GRPO: a high-level policy selects a block-size action and a low-level policy generates the response under that block size. During post-training it explores diverse block-size actions across rollouts, and at inference the learned policy picks a block size for each input before generation.
rvjI95E3hR.key_idea: Turn block size from a fixed hyperparameter into a learned action by splitting the policy into a high-level block-size selector and a low-level generator trained jointly with GRPO.
rvjI95E3hR.evidence: Experiments on 13 benchmarks; reviews mention multiple backbones, RL algorithms, and a multi-seed experiment.
rvjI95E3hR.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text provided cuts off before the results on 13 benchmarks).
rvjI95E3hR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated and the idea of input-dependent learned block size simple and useful, with consistent improvements over fixed-size multi-domain RL baselines across benchmarks, backbones, and RL algorithms.
rvjI95E3hR.main_concern: The gains are not cleanly attributed to the learned selector, since the ablation changes both training exploration and inference selection, and the checkpoint selection protocol and block-action implementation are unclear.

ka5dWKsjwi.one_liner: A small detector decides when a capable agent model hands a long-horizon task off to a cheaper model, cutting cost.
ka5dWKsjwi.problem: Capable agent models are expensive, and it is under-explored whether capable and efficient models can collaborate within one long-horizon task, beyond query-level routing, to cut cost while preserving accuracy.
ka5dWKsjwi.method: Studies model handoffs by direction and context transfer, finding that capable-to-efficient handoffs at suitable stages largely preserve or improve accuracy at lower cost while efficient-to-capable handoffs underperform. AgentBaton is a lightweight detector that learns when to hand off from recurring patterns in task progress.
ka5dWKsjwi.key_idea: Make one well-timed capable-to-efficient handoff per task, with a lightweight detector predicting the handoff point from patterns in task progress.
ka5dWKsjwi.evidence: Systematic handoff studies across model pairs, with reviewers noting software-engineering tasks and comparisons against query routing and the cost-effective frontier.
ka5dWKsjwi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the handoff analysis interesting and well motivated, the detector lightweight, and the cost reductions at similar accuracy convincing.
ka5dWKsjwi.main_concern: Generalizability and rigor: only software-engineering tasks and one open-weight family are tested, accuracy holds in only 12 of 22 settings, and Tables 3 and 6 disagree on apparently matching configurations.

NxX49DNW2C.one_liner: Traces LLM refusal through three SAE feature sets (risk encoding, safety integration, refusal execution) validated by ablation and mediation.
NxX49DNW2C.problem: Safety evaluation of LLMs is mostly behavioral, recording what a model outputs but not where refusal is computed or why it can be bypassed.
NxX49DNW2C.method: RefusalTrace uses layer-wise probing to split model depth into three regions, then localizes a Sparse Autoencoder feature set in each by activation-based ranking and set-level ablation under a shared refusal/compliance objective, with a general-capability control bounding set size. The account is tested with three-condition activation comparisons, graded suppression against activation-matched controls, and bidirectional mediation.
NxX49DNW2C.key_idea: Define three probe-based depth regions and localize a causal SAE feature set in each by activation ranking and set-level ablation with a capability-bounded set size.
NxX49DNW2C.evidence: Experiments on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-IT with activation comparisons, matched-control ablations, mediation interventions, jailbreak analysis, and a harmfulness-detection use case.
NxX49DNW2C.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract gives qualitative findings only, with no numbers)
NxX49DNW2C.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the set-level interventions with activation-matched controls and two-model replication give stronger causal evidence than correlational work in this area.
NxX49DNW2C.main_concern: The middle safety-integration region is not shown to be distinct from refusal execution, and the mediation evidence is uneven (for example, ablating the risk-encoding set increases the refusal margin).

X7vtATvMpt.one_liner: Benchmark of 300 stories comparing image-reference conditions (assets, storyboards) for multi-shot narrative video generation across seven dimensions.
X7vtATvMpt.problem: Existing benchmarks assess final video quality or rank models, giving little insight into how different forms of image conditioning affect multi-shot narrative generation.
X7vtATvMpt.method: ReelBench provides 300 story-style pairs with asset and storyboard images in three visual styles, supports controlled comparisons of reference conditions within the same story, and scores generated videos on seven dimensions and 40 subdimensions.
X7vtATvMpt.key_idea: Hold each story fixed while varying the image-reference condition, and score outputs with a seven-dimension, 40-subdimension rubric checked against human preferences.
X7vtATvMpt.evidence: 300 stories in Pixar-style animation, live-action realism and 2D anime, paired tests across reference conditions, and agreement with human pairwise preferences.
X7vtATvMpt.claimed_gains: Stronger visual anchoring through first-frame conditioning does not consistently improve overall quality, and ReelBench agrees with human overall preferences in over 90% of pairwise comparisons.
X7vtATvMpt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the parallel-condition dataset and the question of which references to feed a shot-by-shot pipeline are practically useful, with rich evaluation dimensions.
X7vtATvMpt.main_concern: The reference-condition comparison is not cleanly controlled (no text-only baseline, and I2V differs in interface and information), and some effects sit near the judge's run-to-run noise.

khtzaAyfJX.one_liner: Non-Markovian simplex diffusion for DNA design that routes cached noisier denoising states into the denoiser via a Gumbel-Softmax router.
khtzaAyfJX.problem: Masked diffusion, Dirichlet flow matching, and SLM use Markov reverse processes, so each denoising step ignores the rest of the sampling trajectory even though the noisier states are already computed.
khtzaAyfJX.method: TC-SLM represents corrupted DNA as simplex-valued nucleotide distributions and, at each reverse step, augments the denoiser with a learned summary of cached noisier states. A Gumbel-Softmax router scores those states by compatibility with the current state and forms a routed history context used to predict the clean sequence.
khtzaAyfJX.key_idea: Condition each reverse step on a Gumbel-Softmax-routed summary of earlier noisier states, keeping per-level marginals while changing the joint distribution over the trajectory.
khtzaAyfJX.evidence: Conditional enhancer and promoter design and unconditional protein generation, with matched SLM and MDLM backbones mainly at 5 sampling steps, plus history and routing ablations and motif-profile analysis.
khtzaAyfJX.claimed_gains: not stated (the visible abstract gives no figures; reviewers report consistent gains over matched SLM and MDLM baselines at five sampling steps).
khtzaAyfJX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the history-routing mechanism gives consistent few-step gains over matched SLM and MDLM baselines, with ablations isolating the history component.
khtzaAyfJX.main_concern: Evaluation is mostly at 5 NFE with no multi-step (around 100 NFE) comparison, relies on proxy classifiers and FBD, and needs per-dataset tuning of the bias and guidance scale.

F17AH2BmQh.one_liner: Low-rank LLM compression via greedy, student-input-aware block-level regression that models residual connections and normalization.
F17AH2BmQh.problem: Matrix-wise low-rank compression ignores residual connections and normalization layers, so compression errors cascade through blocks.
F17AH2BmQh.method: STRIM starts from a block-level reconstruction view and derives a greedy, student-input-aware compression procedure that explicitly accounts for residual connections and normalization layers. Reviewers describe the procedure as a closed-form regression that provides an initialization for later optimization.
F17AH2BmQh.key_idea: Fit low-rank factors by closed-form regression on already-compressed (student) inputs, adding residual-path and normalization corrections to curb cascading compression error.
F17AH2BmQh.evidence: Six classification datasets (for example OpenbookQA, WinoGrande, HellaSwag) across Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen families and several compression ratios, with ablations of structural correction and regularization.
F17AH2BmQh.claimed_gains: STRIM consistently improves task accuracy by over 5% on six classification datasets across model families and compression ratios.
F17AH2BmQh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is sound, the closed-form formulation is simple and efficient, and results are good across model families and compression ratios, especially under aggressive compression.
F17AH2BmQh.main_concern: The contribution of the structural terms is not isolated (after post-compression optimization they add only 0.05 and 0.16 points) and the difference from AA-SVD, which also uses student-aware regression, is unclear.

AMEgzIfo1c.one_liner: Offline RL regularizer that models action support and conditional transition support separately and propagates value-guided future support costs.
AMEgzIfo1c.problem: Local action support and marginal successor-state support do not show whether a specific state-action-successor relation is supported or whether later decisions stay supported, and low support does not necessarily imply low return.
AMEgzIfo1c.method: SFPR separately models action support given the state and transition support given the state-action pair, with two branch-specific cost estimators that recursively connect local assessments to later decisions. Support and behavior-relative value assessments set batch-level cost strengths, support-dependent continuation reduces propagation at weakly supported transitions, and the costs are combined with behavior-distribution fitting and selective value regularization.
AMEgzIfo1c.key_idea: Factorize future support cost into action and conditional-transition branches, propagate them recursively with support-dependent continuation, and scale them by behavior-relative value.
AMEgzIfo1c.evidence: D4RL locomotion and a second benchmark (cut off in the abstract; reviewers mention Maze2D and AntMaze), with branch ablations including a NoPath control.
AMEgzIfo1c.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says SFPR achieves the highest average performance among compared methods on the D4RL locomotion benchmark and a second one, without figures).
AMEgzIfo1c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating action support from conditional transition support is well motivated and that ablations indicate benefit, with strong results particularly on AntMaze.
AMEgzIfo1c.main_concern: Evidence is incomplete: few seeds, an evaluation protocol that differs from published baselines, no direct replacement of conditional with marginal successor support, a modest gain over DOSER, and many hyperparameters.

4BrtB0L8Ow.one_liner: Predicts per-query attention thresholds and gates logits through a shifted SiLU so long-context decoding can prune KV blocks near-losslessly.
4BrtB0L8Ow.problem: Massive KV caches cause memory-bandwidth bottlenecks in long-context decoding, and sparse attention methods often drop necessary context and degrade quality.
4BrtB0L8Ow.method: ETA predicts dynamic contextual thresholds directly from query representations and, during training, filters attention logits through a shifted SiLU gate that creates a smooth near-uniform attention floor, neutralizing sub-threshold value contributions and removing localized attention sinks on initial tokens. A fused Triton kernel screens KV blocks in O(1) time using cached geometric-probabilistic bounds.
4BrtB0L8Ow.key_idea: Learn query-dependent thresholds end-to-end with a shifted-SiLU gate so sub-threshold attention contributes nothing, making block-level KV pruning at inference near-lossless.
4BrtB0L8Ow.evidence: Language modeling, reasoning, and RULER benchmarks with a 1.45B ETA model against Quest, H2O, and NSA, plus a fused Triton kernel benchmark (abstract truncated).
4BrtB0L8Ow.claimed_gains: The 1.45B ETA model matches or exceeds dense quality, outperforms Quest, H2O, and NSA at higher sparsity, and its kernel reaches up to 2.15x end-to-end speedup over FlashAttention-2 (abstract truncated).
4BrtB0L8Ow.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multiplicative SiLU gate is a simple, well-motivated design that aligns training and inference behavior, backed by a full-stack implementation with a fused kernel and measured speedups.
4BrtB0L8Ow.main_concern: Quality is evaluated only at short contexts (2K-8K) while headline speedups are at 64K-512K, and novelty relative to SeerAttention-R and Twilight and baseline coverage are insufficiently established.

1TP2oMunsA.one_liner: Pessimistic offline contextual-bandit learning under factored optimal-transport ambiguity sets for context and reward shift, with a matching minimax lower bound.
1TP2oMunsA.problem: Offline contextual-bandit policies may face simultaneous shifts in the context distribution and reward laws, and prior factored-DRO analyses required uniform coverage.
1TP2oMunsA.method: A pessimistic OT-DRO learner built on sharp confidence bounds for robust rewards, with a distribution-dependent concentration bound for context estimation; it needs neither the behavior policy nor the context distribution.
1TP2oMunsA.key_idea: Use pessimism over separate OT ambiguity sets for context and reward, with regret governed by coverage along a robust optimal policy rather than uniform coverage.
1TP2oMunsA.evidence: Regret upper bound and matching lower bound; reviews note a synthetic coverage experiment and an Open Bandit Dataset experiment in the appendix.
1TP2oMunsA.claimed_gains: Regret of order D C*_rob sqrt(log(|X||A|/delta)/n), matched by a lower bound showing minimax optimality up to constants.
1TP2oMunsA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper clear and the coverage-dependent guarantee, requiring coverage only along an optimal robust policy, an improvement over uniform coverage, with a new lower bound.
1TP2oMunsA.main_concern: The finite-context tabular setting shares no information across similar contexts, and the experiments do not exercise the context-shift or coverage claims.

XfpS4kdT48.one_liner: CausalFusionFormer aggregates causal discovery graphs with a transformer and routes to a raw-data expert when candidates err together.
XfpS4kdT48.problem: Causal discovery algorithms return different graphs under different assumptions, and candidate-only ensembles are limited to information retained in the submitted graphs.
XfpS4kdT48.method: It builds progressively richer variants: global candidate weighting, edge-adaptive transformer aggregation, an independent data-driven expert, and a full hybrid that routes between aggregated candidates and observational evidence. The candidate pool is PC, GES-BIC, ICA-LiNGAM, NOTEARS and DAGMA, each contributing a full-data estimate and two bootstrap perturbations (15 graphs).
XfpS4kdT48.key_idea: Route adaptively between transformer-aggregated candidate graphs and an independent expert that reads observational data statistics, so errors shared by the candidates can be corrected.
XfpS4kdT48.evidence: Evaluation on 90 locked held-out tasks against a shared-budget adaptation of Causal-Bayes-Ensemble (CBE), uniform voting and the base algorithms, with separate training, validation, calibration and test partitions and paired comparisons.
XfpS4kdT48.claimed_gains: The full hybrid reaches directed F1 0.661 versus 0.612 for the CBE adaptation and 0.608 for global candidate weighting, improving directed F1 by 0.050 (p=0.0091) and AUPRC by 0.094 (p<10^-4) over CBE.
XfpS4kdT48.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find combining candidate algorithms with observational evidence well motivated and the evaluation procedure transparent, with separated data partitions and paired comparisons.
XfpS4kdT48.main_concern: Gains over simpler variants are not significant (hybrid vs uniform vote directed F1 0.661 vs 0.651, p=0.5351), so the added complexity is not clearly justified, and many design choices are unexplained.

CcQZiItXgs.one_liner: Training-free diffusion sampler using chance-constrained control that switches off per sample once a calibrated safety threshold is met.
CcQZiItXgs.problem: Training-free safety methods for text-to-image diffusion do not state how often returned outputs remain unsafe, and they apply guidance over a fixed window that stops some samples too early and controls others longer than needed.
CcQZiItXgs.method: SLCF formulates safe generation as a chance-constrained stochastic optimal control problem that limits the probability of unsafe outputs while staying close to the pretrained sampler. The control is derived from the denoiser's posterior mean, and the same prediction decides when to stop against a threshold calibrated once per task.
CcQZiItXgs.key_idea: Derive the control from the denoiser's predicted posterior mean and use the same prediction to stop control per sample when a calibrated unsafe-probability threshold is met.
CcQZiItXgs.evidence: Three safe-generation benchmarks (including MMA-Diffusion) against training-free baselines, with certification of the stopping rule on held-out prompts, a second-detector check and COCO CLIPScore for benign quality.
CcQZiItXgs.claimed_gains: Achieves the lowest unsafe rate among training-free baselines on three safe generation benchmarks and preserves benign generations better; no numbers in the abstract.
CcQZiItXgs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical safety gains are substantial, notably on MMA-Diffusion, and that the stochastic-optimal-control derivation to a practical sampler is well motivated.
CcQZiItXgs.main_concern: The safety certification is weakly supported: it assumes a risk bound at every admitted stopping state, but calibration estimates an average over uncontrolled states.

kJFS6ITWuW.one_liner: MAC-v2 trains a reconstruction-free latent world model with action chunking for long-horizon value expansion from pixels in offline RL.
kJFS6ITWuW.problem: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels is hard because the agent must learn both representation and dynamics, and errors compound over imagined trajectories.
kJFS6ITWuW.method: Trains a reconstruction-free latent world model with prediction and control objectives so control-irrelevant visual details are not encoded, and uses action chunking to cut the number of recursive model predictions needed for value expansion.
kJFS6ITWuW.key_idea: Reconstruction-free latent dynamics learned from prediction and control objectives, rolled out in action chunks to shorten the recursion in value expansion.
kJFS6ITWuW.evidence: Visual OGBench, MMBench2, Robomimic, and LIBERO-10 against model-free and model-based offline RL baselines, with analyses of action chunking and the latent learning objectives.
kJFS6ITWuW.claimed_gains: Reports strong performance against model-free and model-based offline RL baselines on four visual benchmarks, with no numbers stated.
kJFS6ITWuW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses an important visual offline RL problem with a coherent method and clear gains on challenging OGBench tasks across multiple benchmarks.
kJFS6ITWuW.main_concern: The comparison is confounded and attribution is unclear: baselines use discount 0.99 while MAC-v2 uses 0.999, differences from the original MAC are not described, and no error or calibration analysis supports the compounding-error explanation.

mw63qSHu1t.one_liner: Self-distillation teaches a small model a low-resource programming language by training it, without documentation, on its own documentation-conditioned programs.
mw63qSHu1t.problem: Small models fail to write programs in languages poorly represented in pretraining, and SFT plus GRPO break because no quality corpus exists and GRPO gets no signal when no sampled program passes its tests.
mw63qSHu1t.method: Self-distilled SFT (SD-SFT) fine-tunes the model on its own test-passing programs generated with the language documentation in context. Self-distillation policy optimisation (SDPO) then trains every token of the model's own attempts toward a teacher that also sees the documentation and the compiler's feedback.
mw63qSHu1t.key_idea: The same model with documentation in context acts as teacher for itself without it, replacing corpus-based SFT and sparse-reward GRPO.
mw63qSHu1t.evidence: Ballerina, where base Qwen3-8B solves 28 of 30 elementary problems with a syntax sheet and none without, plus other models and languages (OCaml per reviews) and a compiler-error breakdown.
mw63qSHu1t.claimed_gains: On Ballerina, Gemma 4 E4B goes from 0% pass@1 to 55.4% with SD-SFT and 60.8% with SDPO.
mw63qSHu1t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setting is realistic and the gains on Ballerina and OCaml are large, with error analysis showing fewer invented function names and less grammar borrowed from other languages.
mw63qSHu1t.main_concern: Support for the general claim is thin: Ballerina is the only language at zero for both base models, a GRPO-only comparison and the general-coding check lack results, no gold-program upper bound is given, and the appendix is missing.

9yFvS60i0H.one_liner: Training-free, geometry-aware soft-token construction for diffusion language models, with analysis of why soft feedback helps parallel decoding.
9yFvS60i0H.problem: Parallel diffusion LM decoding yields individually plausible but mutually inconsistent tokens, and how soft-token feedback mitigates this has not been systematically examined.
9yFvS60i0H.method: In frozen pretrained DLMs, identifies a geometric mismatch between conventional soft-token construction and the pretrained embedding space and proposes a geometry-aware normalization-and-interpolation construction. Analysis suggests soft feedback favors coherent token sequences rather than only preserving uncertainty.
9yFvS60i0H.key_idea: Build soft tokens with geometry-aware normalization and interpolation toward the [MASK] embedding, since linear mixing distorts norms and directions.
9yFvS60i0H.evidence: Four pretrained DLMs and four math and code benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH500, HumanEval, MBPP per reviews) at three parallel decoding rates, plus analysis on 70 constructed toy prompts.
9yFvS60i0H.claimed_gains: The abstract says the method outperforms standard parallel decoding across four DLMs and four benchmarks (text cut off); a review cites gains over Euclidean soft tokens in 46 of 48 settings.
9yFvS60i0H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric diagnosis of linear soft-token mixing is informative, the fix is simple to implement, and the empirical gains under frozen-model decoding are consistent.
9yFvS60i0H.main_concern: The explanatory claim is not tied to the benchmarks: the agreement-seeking evidence comes from 70 synthetic prompts, causality between lower reverse-KL and higher accuracy is unestablished, and the probabilistic analysis is not mathematically identified.

Iu4khDXeyy.one_liner: EmbodiedHarness revises one harness component at a time, chosen by anchored counterfactual replay, with model weights frozen.
Iu4khDXeyy.problem: Improving an embodied agent's external harness from sparse feedback requires deciding which component to revise, not only how to revise it.
Iu4khDXeyy.method: A frozen VLM acts as planner and optimizer in a diagnose-revise-validate loop over four harness components. Anchored counterfactual replay restores simulator state at an observable deviation anchor, applies a bounded single-component revision, and compares candidate and parent via paired suffix rollouts; revisions are accepted only if success improves without losing parent-solved validation episodes, subject to cost and catastrophic-event constraints.
Iu4khDXeyy.key_idea: Pick the component to revise by replaying paired suffix rollouts from a restored simulator state and history, then gate updates by paired validation.
Iu4khDXeyy.evidence: Three simulated embodied benchmarks including VLABench, with held-out evaluation and a comparison against SHAPER on its backbone.
Iu4khDXeyy.claimed_gains: On VLABench average success rises from 34.8% to 48.9%, and with SHAPER's backbone it exceeds SHAPER by 10.2 percentage points over the four jointly reported capability (text cut off).
Iu4khDXeyy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the harness-component selection problem is practical, the method is clear and intuitive, and evaluation on recent embodied benchmarks supports it.
Iu4khDXeyy.main_concern: Cost and generality are underreported: results hold only in recoverable simulation, total optimization cost, tokens, and machine details are missing, backbones are mostly Qwen and the closed models dated, and baselines such as Zetta and Evo-Harness are not compared.

VpgGkAfZHQ.one_liner: Hindsight goal supervision and action-transition consistency train inverse and forward latent models for search-free visual planning.
VpgGkAfZHQ.problem: Latent world-model planning requires expensive online search, while action prediction alone may neglect goal-relevant representations and forward-model consistency.
VpgGkAfZHQ.method: HIJP relabels future trajectory observations as goals and backpropagates action supervision through goal representations. It aligns forward predictions under inferred actions with successor encodings and alternates inverse and forward models at inference.
VpgGkAfZHQ.key_idea: Train goal-conditioned actions and latent transitions jointly, enforcing consistency between predicted actions and encoded successor states.
VpgGkAfZHQ.evidence: Four visual-control tasks, including PushT and OGCube, evaluate success and efficiency with hindsight, goal-gradient, and consistency ablations.
VpgGkAfZHQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the coherent inverse-forward coupling and component ablations, with promising manipulation results.
VpgGkAfZHQ.main_concern: Unclear separation between training trajectories and evaluation episodes leaves generalization to independent state-goal pairs uncertain.

hWV7TkZ7dW.one_liner: Hierarchical Bayesian pilot estimates allocate stochastic LLM rollouts by task variance, with speculative execution reducing synchronization overhead.
hWV7TkZ7dW.problem: Uniform rollout repetition wastes evaluation budget when benchmark tasks have different outcome variances.
hWV7TkZ7dW.method: HBN pools pilot success counts to estimate task variances and assigns exact positive-integer Neyman allocations, combining stages with a precommitted weight. HBN-async starts continuations from partial feedback and retains those selected by the final allocation.
hWV7TkZ7dW.key_idea: Pool pilot outcomes across tasks to allocate fresh rollouts by posterior variance while preserving an unbiased benchmark estimate.
hWV7TkZ7dW.evidence: Evaluation covers 107 nondegenerate profiles across six checkpoints and 18 benchmark groups, alongside real-generation tests of asynchronous execution.
hWV7TkZ7dW.claimed_gains: For rollout budgets of 8-64 per task, Speculative Evaluation reduces variance relative to Uniform by 12.8%-33.6% on average across profiles.
hWV7TkZ7dW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value budget-aware evaluation and the careful preservation of unbiasedness under adaptive allocation.
hWV7TkZ7dW.main_concern: The incremental benefit of hierarchical pooling over simpler Bayesian or two-stage Neyman baselines is small and insufficiently established.

tx7jVsCnCb.one_liner: Three-valued rule audits and deterministic evidence qualification decide whether agents should reuse, adapt, reject, or defer retrieved procedures.
tx7jVsCnCb.problem: A relevant retrieved procedure may be inapplicable, and missing evidence must remain distinct from evidence of failure.
tx7jVsCnCb.method: RGA combines learned evidence routing and semantic verification with deterministic evidence qualification and action aggregation. Counterfactual rule-level supervision preserves UNKNOWN conditions without directly supervising the final action.
tx7jVsCnCb.key_idea: Keep unresolved applicability conditions UNKNOWN and aggregate qualified rule evidence into reuse, adaptation, rejection, or deferral decisions.
tx7jVsCnCb.evidence: RGABench evaluates four controlled tracks, with frozen-output qualification replay, matched binary-training ablations, and AppWorld studies.
tx7jVsCnCb.claimed_gains: RGA achieves 84.90% action accuracy and 5.17% Harm versus 44.97% and 45.68%, respectively, for the strongest evaluated mechanism-level control adapted to the same interface.
tx7jVsCnCb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating evidence interpretation from admissibility and the ablations that isolate deterministic qualification.
tx7jVsCnCb.main_concern: Baseline interface restrictions and unequal training budgets prevent clean attribution of the headline gains to structured auditing.

BPJ8mufM9A.one_liner: Computational separations explain why repeated stateful model calls can exceed the representational capacity of distilled fixed-depth students.
BPJ8mufM9A.problem: Training on harness-generated traces may fail to internalize the capabilities supplied by external stateful computation.
BPJ8mufM9A.method: The paper compares harnessed models with students distilled from their traces and constructs a complexity-theoretic separation between repeated lookup composition and fixed-depth forward passes. It varies student size, task difficulty, and chain-of-thought length empirically.
BPJ8mufM9A.key_idea: External stateful composition can compute an NL-complete closure even when each model call performs only an AC0 lookup.
BPJ8mufM9A.evidence: Conditional complexity results accompany Dyck, Sokoban, modular arithmetic, and competition-math experiments, including capacity and chain-of-thought ablations.
BPJ8mufM9A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge clearly stated formal assumptions and empirical evidence of a gap between harnessed models and distilled students.
BPJ8mufM9A.main_concern: The restricted computational and distillation settings leave the broader relevance of the separation to practical harness internalization uncertain.

VqDpqib2hh.one_liner: Operator-predicted refinement fields become conforming meshes that initialize adaptive finite-element solves across parametric PDE instances.
VqDpqib2hh.problem: Adaptive finite-element methods repeat costly sequential mesh-discovery cycles for each new PDE input or parameter setting.
VqDpqib2hh.method: MeshOp learns a map from PDE inputs to AFEM-derived refinement fields. A dedicated score-to-mesh procedure constructs a conforming hierarchical mesh, from which residual-based AFEM can continue for higher accuracy.
VqDpqib2hh.key_idea: Predict cumulative refinement demand from PDE inputs and realize it as a conforming hierarchical mesh before further adaptive solving.
VqDpqib2hh.evidence: Burgers, disk convection-diffusion, and three-dimensional reaction-diffusion benchmarks compare finite-element error and online time against AFEM.
VqDpqib2hh.claimed_gains: Despite $11.4\%$ to $27.4\%$ exact-level disagreement, MeshOp reports comparable finite-element errors and online speedups of $2.34\times$ and $2.10\times$ over reference-error-matched AFEM on Burgers and disk convection-diffusion, and $3.06\times$ over comparable-accuracy fixed-cycle AFEM on three-dimensional reaction-diffusion.
VqDpqib2hh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit combining operator learning with conventional adaptive solvers and evaluating downstream mesh accuracy and cost.
VqDpqib2hh.main_concern: Efficiency depends on substantial offline training within restricted PDE families and fixed geometry or mesh templates.

vs1E2oIHNv.one_liner: Linked debate transcripts and professional adjudication records support Chinese winner, stage-score, and best-debater prediction benchmarks.
vs1E2oIHNv.problem: Chinese full-debate evaluation lacks datasets connecting contextual contributions with detailed professional judgments and outcomes.
vs1E2oIHNv.method: CCDD aligns reviewed competition transcripts with individual judge scores, match decisions, best-debater ballots, commentary, and appeals. It defines winner, stage-score, and best-debater prediction tasks with zero-shot and judge-agreement analyses.
vs1E2oIHNv.key_idea: Link turns and debate stages to original rubric-based professional judgments, preserving individual disagreements and appeal reassessments.
vs1E2oIHNv.evidence: The dataset contains 148 matches, 2,690 stage--side scoring instances, and 20,542 turns, with zero-shot evaluations on three adjudication tasks.
vs1E2oIHNv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the rare, detailed Chinese debate resource and its linked professional adjudication records.
vs1E2oIHNv.main_concern: The benchmark provides limited analysis of model differences and lacks uncertainty estimates needed to interpret close scores.

ZdNepVDpMe.one_liner: Moment-matched surrogate key distributions yield closed-form corrections to merged attention scores and values.
ZdNepVDpMe.problem: Naive KV-cache merging changes attention mass and value selection, degrading retrieval and reasoning accuracy under aggressive compression.
ZdNepVDpMe.method: The paper expresses cluster attention through a cumulant-generating function and an exponentially tilted value mean. A two-atom surrogate matching key-norm moments produces score and value corrections with merge-order-invariant statistics.
ZdNepVDpMe.key_idea: Replace each merged key cluster with a moment-matched two-atom distribution to correct its attention score and query-dependent value.
ZdNepVDpMe.evidence: Theory gives closed-form corrections and conditional exactness and error bounds, with experiments on two 7B–8B models and three tasks including RULER.
ZdNepVDpMe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the principled account of merging errors and training-free score and value corrections.
ZdNepVDpMe.main_concern: Evaluation on only two model sizes and a narrow task and baseline set limits evidence of broader effectiveness.

EKtmR2WnFK.one_liner: Sharp feasible-effect intervals identify when static reward scores determine downstream policy-improvement comparisons.
EKtmR2WnFK.problem: Reward models with identical response rankings and variance can induce opposite policy improvements, making static selection unreliable.
EKtmR2WnFK.method: For norm-bounded linear reward classes, the paper derives the range of initial policy effects consistent with exact score observations. It then gives sufficient conditions for comparisons to remain identified after finite policy changes, including matched KL distance.
EKtmR2WnFK.key_idea: Project score observations onto target-relevant feature directions and bound all policy effects consistent with the remaining reward uncertainty.
EKtmR2WnFK.evidence: Theoretical counterexamples and identification guarantees accompany experiments using pretrained reward-model scores and partial observations.
EKtmR2WnFK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value showing why static reward-model agreement need not determine downstream policy improvement.
EKtmR2WnFK.main_concern: Notation-heavy presentation obscures the intuition, practical construction, and scope of the identification results.

59uNH95GLP.one_liner: Evidence-constrained comparative rewards train visual agents to choose investigations, retrieve context, and explain images.
59uNH95GLP.problem: Images may require contextual investigation even when users cannot specify which visual clues or questions deserve search.
59uNH95GLP.method: Vision-AutonoSearch jointly trains visual autonomous investigation and search-augmented VQA with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. ECCR supplements rubric scores with pairwise preferences granted only when visual or retrieved evidence supports their decisive claims.
59uNH95GLP.key_idea: Reward comparisons between sampled investigations only when evidence substantiates the claims underlying the preference.
59uNH95GLP.evidence: Training uses VAI-SFT-5K and VAI-RL-2K, with evaluation on four investigation and four VQA benchmarks plus controlled training ablations.
59uNH95GLP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the value of agents choosing what to investigate and the motivation for evidence-constrained rewards.
59uNH95GLP.main_concern: Inconsistent tools, prompts, and evaluation protocols prevent fair comparisons with existing search agents and frontier models.

KAHOmLtOMn.one_liner: Marginal requirement-coverage loss per byte governs offloading of persistent 3D scene payloads between robots and cloud storage.
KAHOmLtOMn.problem: Task-relevant scene payloads accumulate over a robot's lifetime, while discarding reusable payloads can require costly reconstruction.
KAHOmLtOMn.method: PORTER keeps lightweight scene anchors onboard and migrates heavy object payloads between edge and cloud. It decomposes tasks into requirements and repeatedly offloads the payload with the smallest marginal Irreplaceable Support Erasure per byte.
KAHOmLtOMn.key_idea: Offload payloads according to lost task-requirement coverage per byte, discounting replaceable information and protecting weakly supported requirements.
KAHOmLtOMn.evidence: Experiments use JITOMA-Bench and apply the approach to four baseline methods for persistent robotic scene memory.
KAHOmLtOMn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value addressing memory across a robot's lifetime and accounting for substitute task support in residency decisions.
KAHOmLtOMn.main_concern: The practical need for cloud residency and its advantage over lightweight local summaries with on-demand retrieval remain insufficiently demonstrated.

t6AXbabKFG.one_liner: A shared diffusion architecture jointly learns time-series captioning and text-conditioned time-series generation.
t6AXbabKFG.problem: Separate captioning and generation models underuse shared text-series structure and face scarce aligned training data across domains.
t6AXbabKFG.method: ISIMUD models text and time series within a shared diffusion architecture for both conditional directions. BOOK-OF-ISIMUD supplies cross-domain text-series pairs with domain-agnostic semantics.
t6AXbabKFG.key_idea: Learn both conditional directions of a shared text-time-series joint distribution within one diffusion architecture.
t6AXbabKFG.evidence: Experiments span in-domain and zero-shot settings, downstream adaptation, and joint-training and prediction ablations, using a dataset covering five domains.
t6AXbabKFG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the motivation for unified modeling, clear presentation, and competitive results on both tasks.
t6AXbabKFG.main_concern: The evaluation does not sufficiently establish that joint training provides meaningful cross-task semantic benefits beyond modest metric gains.

xltpXfyZDL.one_liner: A provenance-graph benchmark tests agents' reconstruction of APT attack chains from long security logs.
xltpXfyZDL.problem: Existing cybersecurity agent benchmarks insufficiently test reconstruction of complete attack campaigns from realistic security logs.
xltpXfyZDL.method: CyberClear requires agents to identify evidence and reconstruct entities, causal relationships, attack techniques, and forensic support as provenance graphs. Its evaluation checks attack behavior, temporal and causal consistency, graph fidelity, and narrative consistency.
xltpXfyZDL.key_idea: Evaluate reconstructed attack graphs for semantic, temporal, causal, and evidence consistency rather than surface text similarity.
xltpXfyZDL.evidence: Experiments cover 450 instances, multiple LLMs and agent frameworks, component ablations, and comparisons with human judgments.
xltpXfyZDL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value attack-chain reconstruction as an underrepresented and practically relevant cybersecurity evaluation task.
xltpXfyZDL.main_concern: Reference-graph construction and limited human validation leave uncertainty about whether scored attack steps are supported by the defender logs.

Dfx9VEydLH.one_liner: Query-aligned spatial support conditions SAR flow generation, with scattering transfer added only from compatible angular evidence.
Dfx9VEydLH.problem: Sparse SAR views leave geometry and view-dependent electromagnetic scattering underdetermined across unseen angles.
Dfx9VEydLH.method: Phi-Flow constructs canonical spatial support from sparse observations and aligns it to the requested view. A flow-matching generator uses that geometry and optionally transfers relative scattering modulation from a compatible reference with denser angular coverage.
Dfx9VEydLH.key_idea: Condition generation on query-aligned coarse geometry and add relative scattering modulation only when a compatible reference supplies reliable angular evidence.
Dfx9VEydLH.evidence: Two SAR datasets test angular sparsity, cross-scene transfer, downstream classification, viewpoint estimation, and geometry and scattering ablations.
Dfx9VEydLH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the geometry-first motivation and spatial-conditioning ablations persuasive.
Dfx9VEydLH.main_concern: The criterion for selecting reliable scattering references is unclear, including whether it requires knowledge of unobserved target views.

v3wKN3dTJP.one_liner: Observation-transition credit assignment and update verification guide test-time policy adaptation for vision-language navigation.
v3wKN3dTJP.problem: Distribution shifts in unseen environments distort local action preferences in vision-language navigation, while existing test-time adaptation signals neither confirm goal-directed progress nor verify whether policy updates should persist.
v3wKN3dTJP.method: Credit-Guided Policy Improvement (CGPI) scores immediate action-induced observation transitions using frozen-feature similarity relative to policy-weighted predictions to estimate local progress credit without privileged feedback. It updates a lightweight action reranker and uses a verify-and-retain test to decide whether candidate policy updates are kept.
v3wKN3dTJP.key_idea: Score action-induced observation transitions with frozen-feature similarity credit and verify candidate updates before retaining lightweight action-reranker changes.
v3wKN3dTJP.evidence: Experiments evaluate online test-time adaptation across multiple vision-language navigation benchmarks, including REVERIE, R2R, and R2R-CE, and across multiple navigation backbones.
v3wKN3dTJP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the identify-propose-verify-retain framework clearly separates policy change from policy improvement and attaches cheaply to frozen navigation policies without privileged test-time information.
v3wKN3dTJP.main_concern: Reviewers question the novelty and reliability of the handcrafted semantic-similarity credit and verification heuristics, noting thin empirical gains and missing counterfactual, matched-budget verifier, and real-world evaluations.

ZT6vGCUEJ8.one_liner: Timestamped multi-hop audio-visual evidence trajectories benchmark long-video reasoning and cross-modal hallucination in OmniLLMs.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.problem: Existing audio-visual benchmarks rely on short clips, isolated modalities, or single-hop perception, failing to test reasoning over sparse, temporally dispersed cross-modal evidence in long videos.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.method: TraceAV-Bench constructs 2,000 validated multiple-choice questions over 578 long videos totaling 339.5 hours across 4 evaluation dimensions and 15 sub-tasks using a three-step pipeline and quality assurance. Each item is annotated with an explicit timestamped, modality-labeled evidence trajectory averaging 3.68 hops across a 15.1-minute span, paired with cross-modal hallucination tasks.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.key_idea: Ground multiple-choice questions over long videos in timestamped, modality-labeled multi-hop evidence trajectories paired with cross-modal hallucination tasks.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.evidence: Evaluations test representative closed- and open-source OmniLLMs across general reasoning and hallucination tasks, supplemented by evidence-masking, text-only shortcut, and human auditing analyses.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.claimed_gains: On general tasks, the strongest closed-source model (Gemini 3.1 Pro) reaches 68.29% and the best open-source model under direct inference (Ming-Flash-Omni-2.0) reaches 51.70%.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicit timestamped and modality-labeled multi-hop evidence trajectories over long audio-visual videos enable more diagnostic analysis than aggregate QA accuracy alone.
ZT6vGCUEJ8.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about dataset quality after spot checks revealed answer-leaking wording and single-hop items, alongside overlap with prior long-video benchmarks and underspecified video input sampling settings.

UXvi1CdXcZ.one_liner: Verbalized Bayesian-network samples test whether continual pretraining preserves conditional probabilities and their relationships.
UXvi1CdXcZ.problem: It remains unclear whether language models learn probabilistic knowledge faithfully rather than only plausible answer rankings.
UXvi1CdXcZ.method: The study generates synthetic Bayesian networks with known distributions, verbalizes sampled data, and continually pretrains language models. It varies network size, documentation policy, scale, and exposure while measuring conditional probabilities and relational compression.
UXvi1CdXcZ.key_idea: Compare model-recovered probabilities and evidence-induced shifts against exact Bayesian-network distributions after training on verbalized samples.
UXvi1CdXcZ.evidence: Controlled OLMo-2 experiments use binary variables and clinic-domain templates with analytic ground truth and variations in documentation and training exposure.
UXvi1CdXcZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled synthetic setup with exact probabilistic ground truth and analysis beyond individual prediction accuracy.
UXvi1CdXcZ.main_concern: A single model family, restricted templates, and one main probability readout limit conclusions about real-world probabilistic knowledge acquisition.

O6wr6yExTY.one_liner: SOLO updates GUI-agent adapters through top-K self-distillation on judged successes and relabeled partial successes from deployment.
O6wr6yExTY.problem: Deployed GUI agents cannot rely on ground truth, retries, or a separate learning phase to update their weights.
O6wr6yExTY.method: SOLO uses a judge to select successful episodes and a proposer-verifier pair to relabel failed prefixes with completed subtasks. Admitted episodes enter a sliding window that drives adapter updates by top-K self-distillation whenever it contains a judged success.
O6wr6yExTY.key_idea: A sliding window of judged successes and relabeled prefixes supplies the agent's own predictions for top-K adapter self-distillation.
O6wr6yExTY.evidence: Experiments use recurring WebArena, VisualWebArena, and MobileWorld streams with UI-TARS-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B and compare against frozen agents and web memory methods.
O6wr6yExTY.claimed_gains: SOLO improves success rate by three to six points over the frozen agent.
O6wr6yExTY.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the explicit deployment setting with no ground truth, one attempt per task, and no pre-deployment training.
O6wr6yExTY.main_concern: Reviewers question the reliability and contribution of judge-based episode selection to adapter updates.

VsQjZFCXQN.one_liner: TRPQuant routes tokens by activation concentration through dense, sparse, or dual quantization branches with selective channel pruning.
VsQjZFCXQN.problem: Modality-level quantization overlooks activation differences among tokens within each modality, reducing accuracy and wasting computation.
VsQjZFCXQN.method: TRPQuant groups tokens as dense, intermediate, or sparse using activation patterns. Dense tokens retain all channels, sparse tokens use a pruned branch, and intermediate tokens combine both branches.
VsQjZFCXQN.key_idea: Channel-energy concentration determines token routing and branch-specific quantization with selective channel pruning.
VsQjZFCXQN.evidence: Experiments evaluate quantization on mainstream VLMs, including Qwen2.5-VL-7B under W3A3.
VsQjZFCXQN.claimed_gains: TRPQuant preserves 94.1% of FP16 performance under W3A3 (69.9 vs. 74.3) on Qwen2.5-VL-7B.
VsQjZFCXQN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate activation-based token grouping and its connection to quantization paths and computational savings.
VsQjZFCXQN.main_concern: Reviewers seek stronger justification of pruning reliability and the stability of selected channels and token groups.

V3zHPj5VgK.one_liner: EvoIn evolves agent decision procedures in a harness, rewrites resulting traces, and fine-tunes models to internalize them.
V3zHPj5VgK.problem: Agent improvement methods conflate tool changes, decision procedures, and model adaptation, obscuring how models learn better decision procedures.
V3zHPj5VgK.method: EvoIn analyzes execution traces to evolve and validate decision procedures in the harness, then generates improved reasoning traces. It rewrites those traces to remove harness references and fine-tunes the model on the resulting self-contained reasoning.
V3zHPj5VgK.key_idea: Rewriting harness-guided traces as self-contained reasoning supplies fine-tuning targets that encode the evolved decision procedures in model weights.
V3zHPj5VgK.evidence: Evaluations cover multiple in-domain task categories and out-of-domain benchmarks, with ablations of harness evolution and trajectory rewriting.
V3zHPj5VgK.claimed_gains: EvoIn raises pass rate by 10.9 points in-domain and by 9.2 points out-of-domain.
V3zHPj5VgK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the procedure-internalization problem and report empirical gains with ablation support for evolution and rewriting.
V3zHPj5VgK.main_concern: Reviewers find insufficient justification for internalizing procedures instead of retaining the evolved harness.

4gec4slkyN.one_liner: DIVER combines local graph diversity and query exposure to select entities for adaptive GraphRAG knowledge extraction.
4gec4slkyN.problem: GraphRAG extraction methods struggle to identify entities that can reveal additional knowledge within limited query budgets.
4gec4slkyN.method: DIVER scores entities using local structural diversity and neighborhood query exposure, then issues targeted relational queries. It changes topics when local extraction opportunities decline.
4gec4slkyN.key_idea: Combining structural diversity with neighborhood query exposure prioritizes unexplored graph regions while discounting redundant local neighborhoods.
4gec4slkyN.evidence: Experiments on Medical, Novel, and Agriculture compare entity and relation recall and F1 against extraction baselines.
4gec4slkyN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the intuition that highly connected but redundant neighborhoods can offer little remaining extraction potential.
4gec4slkyN.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the attack works against ordinary query-only access without cooperative structured disclosure or extra instruction control.

QK3DcTsY3O.one_liner: ZoomSplat aggregates multiview frequency bounds and conditions Gaussian prediction on filter sizes to reduce zoom-in rendering artifacts.
QK3DcTsY3O.problem: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstructions develop erosion and grid artifacts above context-image sampling rates, while existing frequency bounds can oversmooth detail.
QK3DcTsY3O.method: ZoomSplat integrates multiview-aware filtering into Gaussian prediction using an aggregated frequency bound and explicit filter-size conditioning. An opaque-scene prior combines termination-conditioned color normalization with transmittance regularization.
QK3DcTsY3O.key_idea: Aggregated multiview frequency bounds permit finer Gaussian scales where multiple observations support them, with filter-size-conditioned prediction and opacity regularization.
QK3DcTsY3O.evidence: Experiments evaluate DL3DV with six context views across multiple rendering scales, including 139 held-out scenes described by a reviewer.
QK3DcTsY3O.claimed_gains: ZoomSplat improves average 1.4dB PSNR on DL3DV across 1×, 2×, 4×, and 8× rendering.
QK3DcTsY3O.reviewer_consensus: The reviews discussing ZoomSplat recognize its rendering-quality benefits across sampling rates and its practical reconstruction motivation.
QK3DcTsY3O.main_concern: Reviewers question the justification and distinct contribution of multiview frequency aggregation relative to simpler filtering alternatives.

uZzi3DpceG.one_liner: CTR retimes recorded per-arm demonstration segments under task constraints to reduce spurious cross-arm dependencies.
uZzi3DpceG.problem: Bimanual imitation policies can mistake incidental demonstration timing for required coordination and use opposite-arm progress as a shortcut.
uZzi3DpceG.method: Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination augments training data by retiming arm-local sensorimotor segments while respecting task-required cross-arm constraints. The augmented demonstrations train existing policy architectures.
uZzi3DpceG.key_idea: Retiming unchanged arm-local demonstration segments across admissible schedules separates task-required coordination from incidental timing.
uZzi3DpceG.evidence: Experiments train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and π0.5 on four simulated and four real-robot tasks.
uZzi3DpceG.claimed_gains: CTR raises mean success from 42.1% to 74.7% on a simulated task and from 77.8% to 92.3% on a real-robot task, reduces opposite-arm delay after a 4 s pause from 2.56 s to 0.25 s, and yields constraint violations in 0–4% of trials versus 36–98%.
uZzi3DpceG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a training-data approach to cross-arm coupling and empirical evaluation across simulated and real robots.
uZzi3DpceG.main_concern: Reviewers question whether comparisons and ablations sufficiently isolate CTR's contribution from existing constraint-aware recombination and other components.

49qOted6gS.one_liner: ReTrail uses reflection-token probabilities to trigger rollback and biases reflection logits during regeneration.
49qOted6gS.problem: Fixed reflection schedules fail to adapt when reasoning models need either to correct mistakes or stop repetitive reconsideration.
49qOted6gS.method: ReTrail monitors the probability mass of reflection tokens at reasoning-step boundaries and rolls back to an earlier high-hesitation step after a sharp increase. During regeneration, it first raises and then lowers reflection-token logits.
49qOted6gS.key_idea: Sharp increases in reflection-token probability trigger rollback to a hesitant prefix, followed by staged reflection-logit biasing.
49qOted6gS.evidence: Evaluations span four model families, including AIME and LiveCodeBench, with parameters selected on MATH-500 and controlled rollback-location experiments.
49qOted6gS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the training-free, verifier-free method and controlled evidence supporting the choice of rollback location.
49qOted6gS.main_concern: Reviewers find the evidence for hesitation-based triggering and end-to-end gains weaker than the rollback-location evidence, particularly in single-seed ablations.

TMRvp5RVjQ.one_liner: Prior monitor verdicts guide activation edits, whose amplification enables selective evasion of latent-space concept monitors.
TMRvp5RVjQ.problem: Interactive latent monitors expose feedback that may let language models infer and evade their detection rules.
TMRvp5RVjQ.method: The study tests whether models infer monitored concepts from prior verdicts and produce aligned activation edits. Scaling those edits or training a rank-1 LoRA amplifies evasion, with mechanistic analyses tracing dependence on prior context.
TMRvp5RVjQ.key_idea: Infer monitored directions from prior verdicts and amplify aligned activation edits to suppress targeted latent-monitor detections.
TMRvp5RVjQ.evidence: Experiments evaluate held-out concept monitors, standard capability benchmarks, retrained monitors, and mechanistic interventions on contextual feedback.
TMRvp5RVjQ.claimed_gains: Scaling activation edits by a factor of 8 reduces monitor TPR from 100% to 27%, while a rank-1 LoRA reduces it further to 4%.
TMRvp5RVjQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled experiments and mechanistic analyses informative about latent-monitor evasion.
TMRvp5RVjQ.main_concern: The explicit experimental feedback and training setup remain too far from realistic monitoring to support the broad threat-model claims.

WiooOyEhfi.one_liner: An image-description-reconstruction-question-answering loop evaluates whether unified multimodal models preserve task-relevant information across understanding and generation.
WiooOyEhfi.problem: Separate generation and understanding evaluations miss failures in their interaction within unified multimodal models.
WiooOyEhfi.method: Self-Generative-Understanding asks a model to describe an image, reconstruct visual context from that description, and reason over the generated output. It reuses existing VQA answers to score the full loop without new annotations.
WiooOyEhfi.key_idea: Evaluate question-answering after image-to-text-to-image reconstruction to test whether task-relevant information survives the multimodal loop.
WiooOyEhfi.evidence: Experiments across unified models and benchmarks compare original, caption-only, and reconstructed-context reasoning, with component replacements for diagnosis.
WiooOyEhfi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the closed-loop evaluation a useful complement to separate generation and understanding metrics.
WiooOyEhfi.main_concern: Unvalidated caption correctness and evidence sufficiency confound whether loop failures reflect understanding, generation, or generic-description omissions.

NczdGFCwWU.one_liner: Stochastic adapter masking with inverse-survival rescaling regularizes shared LoRA updates across recurrent transformer loops.
NczdGFCwWU.problem: Shared LoRA updates in looped language models favor later loops, while naive adapter omission changes expected training-time update strength.
NczdGFCwWU.method: Loop Dropout randomly masks adapter applications across loops and rescales surviving applications to preserve expected update strength. All backbone loops remain active, and inference uses the adapter at every loop without extra parameters or computation.
NczdGFCwWU.key_idea: Randomly omit shared adapter applications across loops and inverse-scale surviving updates to preserve their expected strength.
NczdGFCwWU.evidence: Experiments examine mathematical reasoning across model sizes, adapter ranks, and training recipes, with instruction-tuning and code-generation evaluations.
NczdGFCwWU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method is simple, efficient, and adds no inference overhead.
NczdGFCwWU.main_concern: The paper does not sufficiently explain why its masking and rescaling improve shared-loop adaptation beyond existing dropout regularization.
