nqNcrLiGRA.one_liner: VAST freezes target-only gene predictors and selectively accepts auxiliary-supervision corrections through per-gene verification.
nqNcrLiGRA.problem: Adding auxiliary-gene supervision can improve average spatial-expression prediction while degrading individual target genes.
nqNcrLiGRA.method: VAST freezes a target-only reference predictor and lets expanded gene supervision propose residual corrections. Per-gene verification controls whether and how much each correction modifies the reference prediction.
nqNcrLiGRA.key_idea: Protect a frozen target-only predictor and gate auxiliary-supervision residual corrections using target-specific evidence.
nqNcrLiGRA.evidence: Evaluation uses 15 datasets from HEST-1k and Stimage, supervision-panel scaling, per-gene transfer analysis, and protect-propose-verify ablations.
nqNcrLiGRA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value analyzing negative transfer at the individual-gene level and safeguarding target predictors against harmful auxiliary supervision.
nqNcrLiGRA.main_concern: The reliability of verification remains uncertain because correction utility is estimated on training slides and sensitivity to cohort size is insufficiently established.

LM5UvBJzjF.one_liner: REBASE matches semantically embedded patient graphs to shared relational bases using Fused Gromov-Wasserstein alignment for heterogeneous tabular prediction.
LM5UvBJzjF.problem: Differences in clinical feature sets, definitions, naming, and units impede transfer across tabular data sources.
LM5UvBJzjF.method: REBASE represents samples as graphs grounded in language-model embeddings and learns reusable relational bases. Fused Gromov-Wasserstein alignment combines semantic and structural correspondence to produce sample-specific coordinates for prediction.
LM5UvBJzjF.key_idea: Align semantically grounded sample graphs to shared relational bases with Fused Gromov-Wasserstein distance and use alignment coordinates for prediction.
LM5UvBJzjF.evidence: Experiments span three clinical benchmarks with 16 domains, including seen-source integration, held-out-domain transfer, and zero-shot and few-shot settings.
LM5UvBJzjF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find heterogeneous clinical transfer practically important and recognize broad evaluation across sources and limited-label settings.
LM5UvBJzjF.main_concern: Reviewers question whether shared relational bases remain meaningful when hospitals differ in outcome definitions, patient populations, and clinical risks.

8JkaqHDQpB.one_liner: RAY-GRPO differentiates ray-based reward-attainment utilities to adapt objective weights in group-relative policy optimization.
8JkaqHDQpB.problem: Fixed multi-objective GRPO weights express preferences without responding to which rewards currently limit joint attainment.
8JkaqHDQpB.method: RAY-GRPO maps preferences to distributions over reference rays and differentiates averaged proportional-attainment utilities at current calibrated reward means. The resulting coefficients weight group-relative contrasts, while endpoint updates alternate with endpoint-preserving residual refinement.
8JkaqHDQpB.key_idea: Differentiate ray-averaged minimum reward-to-proportion utilities at current reward means to weight the objectives limiting attainment.
8JkaqHDQpB.evidence: Alignment experiments cover two, three, and five objectives, reporting mean reward scores and empirical Pareto-front coverage.
8JkaqHDQpB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate interpretable, attainment-adaptive reward coefficients that reuse scored rollouts without extra generation or reward-model calls.
8JkaqHDQpB.main_concern: Reviewers agree that using the same reward models for training and evaluation does not establish broader alignment improvements.

IrJ8dO1ShL.one_liner: HRC-SimBench scripts human roles and interaction constraints to evaluate robot coordination beyond manipulation success.
IrJ8dO1ShL.problem: Existing vision-language-action benchmarks largely omit intent understanding, timing, protocol adherence, and safety during human interaction.
IrJ8dO1ShL.method: HRC-SimBench represents collaboration as executable scripts defining roles, temporal dependencies, coordination constraints, and human behavior distributions. Instructor, Collaborator, and Intruder tasks are evaluated with interaction metrics alongside success.
IrJ8dO1ShL.key_idea: Encode human roles and temporal coordination requirements in executable scenarios and score synchronization, responsiveness, protocol compliance, and safety.
IrJ8dO1ShL.evidence: The benchmark evaluates adapted GR00T, π0.5, and ACT policies on 13 role-conditioned tasks with over 650 episodes.
IrJ8dO1ShL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value making human interaction explicit and measuring failures that final manipulation success misses.
IrJ8dO1ShL.main_concern: Reviewers agree that prerecorded, nonreactive human behavior tests responses to scripts rather than reciprocal collaboration under shared agency.

j2sGXqXLqk.one_liner: Spectral analysis of Gaussian linear diffusion links prediction targets, timestep sampling, and capacity to learned components and generated distributions.
j2sGXqXLqk.problem: The interaction between diffusion prediction targets, timestep distributions, and model capacity lacks a unified theoretical explanation.
j2sGXqXLqk.method: The paper studies Gaussian data with a time-gated linear predictor and constrained capacity. It characterizes how target and sampling choices select spectral components and determine the generated endpoint distribution.
j2sGXqXLqk.key_idea: Analyze target- and timestep-dependent selection of covariance eigendirections under a shared capacity constraint and derive their generated variances.
j2sGXqXLqk.evidence: Theoretical spectral and endpoint-distribution results are tested on synthetic and real data, including CelebA-HQ.
j2sGXqXLqk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value connecting learned spectral components to generated distributions in one tractable framework for coupled diffusion design choices.
j2sGXqXLqk.main_concern: Reviewers find empirical validation of the proposed spectral-selection mechanism insufficient beyond the simplified Gaussian linear setting.

c1q5SbSiJz.one_liner: RELOAD re-encodes coarse future states in a packed second drafting pass for exact speculative diffusion sampling.
c1q5SbSiJz.problem: Sequential diffusion drafting requires repeated neural calls, while parallel anchor-only drafting lacks evolving future source states.
c1q5SbSiJz.method: RELOAD first produces a coarse trajectory, then independently re-encodes its states in a packed neural pass and rebuilds candidates from the same anchor and per-step noise. Role-LoRA adapts this pass, and prefix causality permits unchanged reflection verification under matched-covariance assumptions.
c1q5SbSiJz.key_idea: Re-encode coarse future states independently in a packed second pass, then rebuild causal proposals using the original anchor and per-step noise.
c1q5SbSiJz.evidence: A one-GPU component study and 256 paired ImageNet-256 cases evaluate accepted lengths and latency, with exactness analysis under matched covariances.
c1q5SbSiJz.claimed_gains: At horizon eight, mean accepted length rises from 2.02 to 4.52 and then 4.77 with role adaptation; latency falls 10.0% versus strict FREE (1.111×), while eight-way verification gives 2.286× speedup over one-active-rank TARGET.
c1q5SbSiJz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the missing-future-state problem and evidence that re-encoding improves speculative diffusion proposals.
c1q5SbSiJz.main_concern: Reviewers find generalizability limited by evaluation on one model, dataset, resolution, and fixed stochastic sampler configuration.

X52294nnHl.one_liner: MHG-Mem links entity mentions, evolving states, and source evidence through typed hyperedges for multimodal agent memory.
X52294nnHl.problem: Text abstractions lose fine visual evidence, while raw-observation memories struggle to bind persistent identities and track changes across sessions.
X52294nnHl.method: MHG-Mem groups entity mentions and facts into identity-consistent occurrences, synthesizes aspect-specific evolution states, and links them to provenance. Agentic search chooses entry layers, traverses typed hyperedges, and inspects source observations for verification.
X52294nnHl.key_idea: Connect identity-grouped observations, aspect-specific state histories, and source evidence with typed hyperedges traversed by agentic retrieval.
X52294nnHl.evidence: Experiments span three benchmarks and three backbones, with entity-linking, evolution-tracking, and source-inspection ablations.
X52294nnHl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical combination of visual-evidence preservation and cross-session entity-state tracking, supported by consistent empirical gains.
X52294nnHl.main_concern: Reviewers question the distinct contribution of hypergraph organization beyond combining existing entity, temporal, provenance, and retrieval mechanisms.

ZIRctvE5eQ.one_liner: Conditions discrete-diffusion and flow-matching transcriptome generators on future cellular states predicted by a gene-regulatory stochastic mechanistic model.
ZIRctvE5eQ.problem: Long-horizon single-cell population forecasting from unpaired snapshots struggles when cellular states transition into unseen developmental regimes lacking reliable future biological conditions for generative models.
ZIRctvE5eQ.method: MeCoGen uses a stochastic mechanistic model informed by core regulatory genes and signed gene regulatory network interactions to forecast biologically structured future cellular states. That predicted state conditions a two-part generator that models sparse gene occurrence via discrete diffusion and continuous expression magnitude via conditional flow matching.
ZIRctvE5eQ.key_idea: Predict biologically structured future states with a core-gene stochastic mechanistic model to condition discrete diffusion for gene occurrence and conditional flow matching for expression magnitude.
ZIRctvE5eQ.evidence: Evaluated on three temporal scRNA-seq differentiation and cellular reprogramming datasets (including iPSC-CM) across distributional, marginal, and sparsity metrics alongside fixed-generator conditioning experiments.
ZIRctvE5eQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that combining mechanistic regulatory extrapolation for future state conditioning with separate generative modeling of expression sparsity and magnitude is well motivated and supported across three biological systems.
ZIRctvE5eQ.main_concern: Reviewers point out insufficient documentation of predefined gene regulatory networks, developmental topologies, and cell-state annotations, incomplete isolation of mechanistic dynamics from calibration differences, and unclear metric discrepancies across tables.

wSGSqDEDqh.one_liner: Accelerates diffusion and flow sampling without training via physical-time velocity extrapolation, curvature-aware reuse gating, and error-feedback tolerance calibration.
wSGSqDEDqh.problem: Feature-caching accelerators for diffusion and flow models rely on discrete representation differences rather than continuous physical-time velocity dynamics, allowing approximation errors to accumulate into trajectory deviations.
wSGSqDEDqh.method: Trajectory-Aligned Flow Caching (TAFC) is a training-free caching framework combining Physical-Time Velocity Extrapolation over continuous sampling intervals, Curvature-Aware Reuse Gating from two-anchor changes, and Self-Calibrating Error Feedback that measures approximation errors at refresh steps to adapt reuse tolerances.
wSGSqDEDqh.key_idea: Extrapolate velocity dynamics over continuous physical sampling intervals while gating cache reuse by velocity curvature and adapting reuse tolerances from refresh-step approximation errors.
wSGSqDEDqh.evidence: Evaluated on FLUX.1-dev, HunyuanVideo, and Wan2.1 across multiple speedup regimes using PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics and component ablations.
wSGSqDEDqh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that TAFC is lightweight, training-free, and achieves consistent PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS improvements over compared caching baselines across FLUX.1-dev, HunyuanVideo, and Wan2.1 at matched latency.
wSGSqDEDqh.main_concern: Reviewers argue that despite the physical-velocity framing, the implementation linearly extrapolates transformer residuals like existing caching methods (such as TeaCache, TaylorSeer, FoCa, and AB-Cache), limiting originality while leaving controller settings and related baselines under-documented.

WhnYZYu1Vb.one_liner: Modulates RNN neuronal integration time constants upon rule cues to reproduce primate frontal-cortex sequence working memory reorganization dynamics.
WhnYZYu1Vb.problem: Primate frontal cortex recordings reveal rank-content factorized representations and transient subspaces during sequence working memory reordering, but the underlying recurrent circuit mechanisms remain unclear.
WhnYZYu1Vb.method: The authors train a recurrent neural network with cue-triggered modulation of neuronal integration time constants on rule-guided forward and backward sequence working memory manipulation tasks. Subspace and dynamical analyses compare the emerging ordinal-rank scaffolds and transient buffering subspaces against primate neural recordings and baseline RNN architectures.
WhnYZYu1Vb.key_idea: Apply cue-triggered modulation of neuronal integration time constants in a recurrent network so ordinal-rank memory scaffolds and transient reordering subspaces emerge during sequence manipulation.
WhnYZYu1Vb.evidence: Trained and analyzed on two-item and three-item rule-guided sequence working memory tasks, comparing subspace geometry and dynamics against primate frontal cortex data (Tian et al.) and baseline RNNs and LSTMs.
WhnYZYu1Vb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that focusing on active sequence manipulation in working memory and reproducing experimentally observed rank-reassignment and transient subspaces from primate data addresses an interesting computational neuroscience question.
WhnYZYu1Vb.main_concern: Reviewers find the externally prescribed cue-time constant switch (e.g., from 1 to 4) ad hoc rather than learned, closely related to established gated/variable-timescale RNNs, and insufficiently ablated or mechanistically explained relative to baselines.

4SAERrMgAG.one_liner: Uses software user manuals for retrieval-augmented GUI planning and synthesizes manual-guided task rollouts to train agents without human demonstrations.
4SAERrMgAG.problem: Computer-use GUI agents struggle to generalize to unseen software requiring long-horizon application-specific procedures, while collecting human-annotated tasks and demonstration trajectories is costly.
4SAERrMgAG.method: MAGE (Manual-Augmented computer use AGent Execution and learning) retrieves task-relevant user manual content at inference time so a planner generates explicit procedural guidance for the GUI agent. For training without human demonstrations, MAGE converts user manuals into executable task-plan pairs, guides environment rollouts with those plans, and optimizes the policy (via GRPO) on the resulting trajectories.
4SAERrMgAG.key_idea: Retrieve software user manuals to generate procedural GUI execution plans at inference time and convert manuals into plan-guided environment rollouts for demonstration-free policy training.
4SAERrMgAG.evidence: Evaluated on OSWorld and a Slack environment with component ablations across inference-time manual-guided planning and training-time policy adaptation.
4SAERrMgAG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that leveraging software user manuals as scalable supervision for both inference-time planning and demonstration-free trajectory synthesis is practical and well evaluated on OSWorld and Slack.
4SAERrMgAG.main_concern: Reviewers note that heavy reliance on capable external LLMs/VLMs for planning, task generation, and evaluation—without a same-planner no-manual baseline—makes it unclear how much gain comes from the manuals versus the planner.

T45LUb6lOX.one_liner: Decouples 3D scene-aware human-object interaction synthesis via a motion-affordance interface trained separately on human-scene and human-object datasets.
T45LUb6lOX.problem: Generating realistic human-object interactions in complex 3D scenes requires both environment-feasibility reasoning and detailed object interaction dynamics, yet paired human-object-scene training data are scarce.
T45LUb6lOX.method: MAMHOI factorizes generation through an explicit motion-affordance interface: a scene-conditioned model trained on human-scene data (LINGO) predicts feasible interaction regions and motion affordances, and an affordance-conditioned model trained on human-object data (OMOMO) synthesizes the corresponding 3D human-object motion without paired human-object-scene data.
T45LUb6lOX.key_idea: Factorize scene-aware human-object interaction synthesis through an explicit motion-affordance interface connecting a scene-conditioned feasibility predictor and an affordance-conditioned motion generator trained without paired human-object-scene data.
T45LUb6lOX.evidence: Trained separately on LINGO and OMOMO without paired human-object-scene supervision and evaluated in complex 3D indoor environments on object-scene penetration, motion smoothness, and contact metrics.
T45LUb6lOX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that factorizing scene-aware human-object interaction via motion affordances to learn from separate human-scene and human-object datasets addresses real paired-data scarcity and improves physical plausibility metrics.
T45LUb6lOX.main_concern: Reviewers point out that lifting 2D/vertically pooled affordances loses 3D height constraints (such as overhangs or under-table spaces), oracle training bounding boxes may leak target trajectories and create a train-test gap, and simpler scene-occupancy baselines are missing.

RJFg8cPbL0.one_liner: Uses upper-expectile signed TD errors to regularize learned tasks via dropout and prioritize informative states in hard multi-task RL.
RJFg8cPbL0.problem: In multi-task reinforcement learning with a shared model, hard tasks often stagnate alongside easier tasks due to weak averaged temporal-difference signals and shared-critic over-specialization.
RJFg8cPbL0.method: The authors introduce expectile temporal-difference error (XTD)—an upper expectile of signed TD errors capturing positive value corrections—and build Cross-level Progress Recovery (CPR). CPR combines inter-task dropout, using relative return and declining task-level XTD to regularize sufficiently learned tasks, with intra-task prioritization of high-XTD states within hard tasks without parameter resets.
RJFg8cPbL0.key_idea: Compute upper-expectile signed TD errors (XTD) to apply inter-task dropout on sufficiently learned tasks while prioritizing high-XTD transitions within hard tasks without parameter resets.
RJFg8cPbL0.evidence: Evaluated on Meta-World multi-task RL benchmarks alongside trajectory diagnostics, Q-bias analyses, and ablations of inter-task dropout and intra-task prioritization.
RJFg8cPbL0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that CPR is clearly written, computationally lightweight, and achieves convincing performance improvements on hard Meta-World tasks without parameter resets.
RJFg8cPbL0.main_concern: Reviewers question whether high positive XTD reliably distinguishes under-learned hard tasks from stochastic transition variance or estimation noise, note unresolved inter-task objective conflicts, and request stronger modern scaled/distributional MTRL baselines.

mUNWnAE0Um.one_liner: Lifts 2D image-edited visual goal states into explicit inter-object SE(3) 3D transformations for zero-shot single-view RGB-D robotic manipulation.
mUNWnAE0Um.problem: Learning-based robotic policies struggle to generalize to unseen open-world manipulation tasks, while LLMs and VLMs lack the fine-grained 3D geometric awareness required for precise spatial alignment.
mUNWnAE0Um.method: From single-view RGB-D observations, LAMP uses generative image-editing models to synthesize 2D goal images encoding target spatial relations, then lifts those visual cues—via hierarchical point-cloud filtering and unified scale alignment—into continuous inter-object SE(3) 3D transformations for zero-shot robot execution without task-specific training.
mUNWnAE0Um.key_idea: Generate 2D goal states with image-editing models and lift their spatial cues via filtered, scale-aligned RGB-D registration into continuous inter-object SE(3) transformations for zero-shot manipulation.
mUNWnAE0Um.evidence: Evaluated zero-shot across randomized simulation scenes and 13 real-world manipulation tasks (including insertion, assembly, pouring, ring stacking, and drawer manipulation), with viewpoint and image-editor ablations.
mUNWnAE0Um.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that lifting image-edited visual goals into explicit SE(3) transformations with depth filtering and scale correction performs strongly across diverse zero-shot real-world and simulated precision manipulation tasks.
mUNWnAE0Um.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited methodological distinction from GoalVLA, ablations of filtering and scale alignment restricted to a single ring-stacking task, and unclear per-task selection among image editors and candidate generations.

c0RPjrRfjQ.one_liner: Casts heterogeneous remote-sensing outputs into a shared visual latent space predicted by one flow-matching model with difficulty-adaptive timestep sampling.
c0RPjrRfjQ.problem: Remote-sensing foundation models unify input representations across modalities yet still rely on fragmented task-specific decoders, prediction heads, and training losses.
c0RPjrRfjQ.method: UniFlow-RS casts heterogeneous remote-sensing task outputs into structured visual targets within a common latent space and trains a single shared latent flow-matching predictor with task-dependent input conditioning and a shared LoRA adapter. To balance multi-task joint optimization, Task-Modality Adaptive Timestep Sampling (TMAS) dynamically allocates flow-matching timesteps according to online learning difficulty per task-modality group.
c0RPjrRfjQ.key_idea: Encode heterogeneous remote-sensing task outputs as structured visual targets in a common latent space and optimize one shared flow-matching predictor using difficulty-adaptive task-modality timestep sampling.
c0RPjrRfjQ.evidence: Evaluated with one shared model across six remote-sensing tasks and thirteen multi-modal datasets, including zero-shot referring segmentation and ablations on joint training, target encoding, and TMAS.
c0RPjrRfjQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying six heterogeneous remote-sensing tasks across thirteen multi-modal datasets within a single head-free latent flow-matching predictor is simple, feasible, and thoroughly ablated.
c0RPjrRfjQ.main_concern: Reviewers note incremental originality over prior visual-target generative frameworks (such as Painter and InstructDiffusion), potential geometric precision loss from post-processing visual targets, and mixed performance against task-specific specialists.

sUKY2nMqg2.one_liner: T2Align aligns asynchronous action-chunk tempo and transitions without retraining robot policies.
sUKY2nMqg2.problem: Action-chunked robot policies struggle with time-critical dynamic tasks because task states change during execution and asynchronous chunks can arrive off the current timeline.
sUKY2nMqg2.method: T2Align preserves policy-intended execution tempo under safety constraints and aligns returned chunks to the current execution timeline. Continuity-consistency blending and similarity-gated transition control stabilize chunk transitions in a plug-and-play, training-free system.
sUKY2nMqg2.key_idea: Preserve execution tempo while temporally aligning asynchronously returned chunks and gating blended transitions by continuity and similarity.
sUKY2nMqg2.evidence: Experiments with widely used policies measure success and stability on dynamic manipulation tasks, with real-robot tests and component analyses across multiple policies and platforms.
sUKY2nMqg2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the two-level temporal alignment is clear, practical, and supported by multiple policies, tasks, and real-robot platforms.
sUKY2nMqg2.main_concern: The distinction from existing asynchronous execution and blending methods is insufficiently tested with matched baselines and complex long-horizon tasks.

mA0Q49gygd.one_liner: ICR regularizes Harsanyi interaction complexity during supervised fine-tuning for LLM tool use.
mA0Q49gygd.problem: The mechanisms connecting SFT method, model scale, and data amount to LLM tool-selection and argument-generation performance remain unclear.
mA0Q49gygd.method: The paper decomposes tool-calling output scores into Harsanyi interactions among input words and finds that stronger complex and weaker simple interactions accompany better SFT. Interaction Complexity Regularization adds an auxiliary loss that promotes this pattern during existing SFT-based tool-use training.
mA0Q49gygd.key_idea: Regularize SFT to strengthen many-word Harsanyi interactions and weaken few-word interactions for tool selection and argument generation.
mA0Q49gygd.evidence: Experiments cover five LLM families and three tool-use benchmarks, BFCL, StableToolBench, and τ²-bench, across multiple SFT-based methods and both tool-calling stages.
mA0Q49gygd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that interaction analysis offers a useful explanation of tool-use SFT and that ICR is simple and consistently validated across settings.
mA0Q49gygd.main_concern: Reported gains are modest without multi-seed uncertainty, and grouped interactions do not guarantee the intended word-level complexity changes.

OzBkhsAURH.one_liner: SimHack predicts reward-hacking onset by simulating prompt-level behavior learned from smaller RL runs.
OzBkhsAURH.problem: Reward hacking is usually addressed after detection, although predicting its onset before a full RL run could avoid costly unsafe training recipes.
OzBkhsAURH.method: SimHack models RL as a stochastic prompt-level behavioral process and learns behavior dynamics from a handful of smaller reference runs. It generates counterfactual simulations for unseen target recipes to predict the distribution of reward-hacking onset steps without retraining.
OzBkhsAURH.key_idea: Learn prompt-level stochastic behavior transitions from small reference RL runs and simulate onset timing for unseen training recipes.
OzBkhsAURH.evidence: A released dataset contains 325 coding RL runs across diverse recipes and hacking behaviors, and evaluations test unseen target recipes and transfer settings.
OzBkhsAURH.claimed_gains: SimHack predicts the median training step at which hacking emerges within 11.3% relative error and ranks recipes by onset timing with a Spearman rank correlation of 0.85.
OzBkhsAURH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that forecasting reward hacking is useful and that the large run dataset and behavioral simulator offer a practical proactive approach.
OzBkhsAURH.main_concern: Evidence is limited to two Qwen models, narrow hacking types, and a fixed prompt pool, leaving broader and out-of-pool generalization uncertain.

sFyVgfWahp.one_liner: AMID distills heterogeneous super-resolution teachers through attribution matching and inverse-network alignment.
sFyVgfWahp.problem: Heterogeneous super-resolution architectures lack directly comparable hidden features, while output matching alone does not transfer how teachers use low-resolution evidence.
sFyVgfWahp.method: GAMD matches integrated-gradient maps of guidance-weighted structural responses using teacher outputs and gradients. ISCD passes teacher and student outputs through a frozen student-isomorphic inverse network for multi-layer contrastive alignment, with an inverse reconstruction constraint for degradation consistency.
sFyVgfWahp.key_idea: Match teacher attribution maps and align outputs in a shared inverse-network proxy space without accessing teacher intermediate features.
sFyVgfWahp.evidence: Experiments use five heterogeneous teachers across five benchmarks at 2×, 3×, and 4× scaling, with component analyses separating fidelity and perceptual effects.
sFyVgfWahp.claimed_gains: At 3× with a SwinIR teacher, AMID outperforms all compared baselines across all eight metrics and improves MUSIQ by 1.22 over the strongest competing method.
sFyVgfWahp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the two distillation mechanisms are well motivated and that evaluations across teachers, datasets, and scales support their complementary effects.
sFyVgfWahp.main_concern: The empirical scope centers on RRDB and paired DF2K data, while 5.5x to 9.0x training compute and untested real-camera degradations limit practicality.

eZq8GOZ8KN.one_liner: Balances long-context RL reasoning budgets using length-normalized sequence weights, smooth boundary penalties, and position-aware token credit.
eZq8GOZ8KN.problem: Uniform terminal length penalties in RL can flip positive content advantages into negative updates across early reasoning tokens.
eZq8GOZ8KN.method: LNPO-ATC combines length-normalized sequence weighting, a smooth boundary penalty, and budget-relative positional token allocation while preserving the content advantage at every token.
eZq8GOZ8KN.key_idea: Applies budget-relative positional allocation and smooth boundary penalties on top of length-normalized weighting without erasing early token content advantages.
eZq8GOZ8KN.evidence: Evaluated across six reasoning benchmarks on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and 27B models with five runs and allocation ablations.
eZq8GOZ8KN.claimed_gains: Improves six-task macro-average on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B by 5.53% over GSPO (ATC adds 2.27% over uniform LNPO) with 1.4-1.5% extra wall time.
eZq8GOZ8KN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation is sound and the multi-benchmark experiments on 27B/35B-A3B backbones are extensive and consistent.
eZq8GOZ8KN.main_concern: Reviewers note that positional allocation is confounded with EOS/terminal token weighting and that evaluation mostly uses a fixed 32,768-token budget.

0d7DLdcNit.one_liner: Generates functionally complete 3D indoor scenes feed-forward using a recursive DSL, distilled expert, and execution-grounded RL.
0d7DLdcNit.problem: Agentic 3D scene generators rely on slow test-time generate-evaluate-revise loops and focus on visual plausibility over functional usability.
0d7DLdcNit.method: The authors define Function-Room Generation with a benchmark, design a recursive scene DSL, distill recursive traces into a sequential feed-forward expert executed deterministically without online repair, and refine it with execution-grounded process rewards (ScenePRM).
0d7DLdcNit.key_idea: Distills recursive DSL scene-construction traces into a feed-forward expert trained with execution-grounded process rewards, eliminating test-time repair loops.
0d7DLdcNit.evidence: Evaluated on a 50-prompt human-validated Function-Room benchmark using 17,386 construction trajectories.
0d7DLdcNit.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that targeting functional usability with a recursive DSL and validated 50-prompt benchmark is practically relevant.
0d7DLdcNit.main_concern: Reviewers note ScenePRM gains confound reward granularity with best-of-8 selection, unclear novelty over prior DSL scene agents, and potential VLM/GPT-5.2 evaluation bias.

nD5an32KRp.one_liner: Keeps branching candidate KV states live during scoring and hands off selected histories directly into LLM generation.
nD5an32KRp.problem: Request-scoped LLM serving discards or recomputes candidate KV states produced during scoring once a branch is selected for continuation.
nD5an32KRp.method: CandiKV treats a candidate group as a persistent serving object while selection is pending, using incoming scores to guide compute and KV residency before handing off chosen histories intact to decoding.
nD5an32KRp.key_idea: Maintains candidate-group KV states across selection and uses incoming scores to prioritize residency before zero-recompute handoff to generation.
nD5an32KRp.evidence: Evaluated across six reasoning and retrieval workloads on <=7B models on a single GPU.
nD5an32KRp.claimed_gains: Reduces continuation TTFT by up to 90.7% and cuts wasted GPU KV byte-seconds by 23.7-30.5% vs full retention, with <=0.33% regular-request TTFT change.
nD5an32KRp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that treating candidate groups as persistent serving state between scoring and generation addresses a concrete serving waste.
nD5an32KRp.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons to related workflow KV systems (KVFlow, Continuum, TokenCake), minimal end-to-end JCT improvement (<=0.95%), and unexplained LMCache baseline anomalies.

3rRXGi57Xv.one_liner: Jointly generates pixels and 32 coarse semantic tokens via flow matching to carry evolving context across denoising steps.
3rRXGi57Xv.problem: Pixel-space diffusion models pass only noisy pixels between steps, forcing higher-level semantic context to be re-derived repeatedly.
3rRXGi57Xv.method: SemPix jointly denoises pixel tokens and coarse, locally aggregated semantic tokens from noise via flow matching in a shared Transformer with joint self-attention and separate output heads.
3rRXGi57Xv.key_idea: Co-generates coarse, locally aggregated semantic tokens alongside pixels via joint self-attention to persist evolving semantic context across flow-matching steps.
3rRXGi57Xv.evidence: Evaluated on pixel-space image generation with controlled ablations on token granularity, matched sequence length, and state persistence.
3rRXGi57Xv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the 32-token semantic context formulation is low-overhead and backed by carefully controlled ablations.
3rRXGi57Xv.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty relative to ReDi, REG, Latent Forcing, and Representation Forcing, and flag unfair ImageNet comparisons against non-DINO baselines.

JSZVWAZ55D.one_liner: Replaces CLIP's fixed spectral truncation mask with an image-conditioned MLP router over an offline cross-modal spectral basis.
JSZVWAZ55D.problem: IsoCLIP-style adaptation applies the same manually selected hard truncation mask over the projector spectrum to every input image.
JSZVWAZ55D.method: Dynamic-IsoCLIP constructs a spectral basis offline from frozen image and text projectors and trains a lightweight MLP router with prototype supervision, representation distillation, and spectral sparsity to produce continuous, image-conditioned masks at inference.
JSZVWAZ55D.key_idea: Predict continuous, image-dependent spectral masks using an MLP router over an offline image-text projector basis without online text features.
JSZVWAZ55D.evidence: Experiments on eleven image-to-image retrieval benchmarks, five base-to-new classification datasets, and component ablations support the method.
JSZVWAZ55D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that replacing fixed hard truncation with a lightweight image-conditioned soft mask is practical and yields strong retrieval results.
JSZVWAZ55D.main_concern: All reviewers highlight the missing baseline of a learned global soft mask trained under the same supervised objective, leaving the value of instance-aware routing unproven.

QABVjPgg8S.one_liner: Extends asymptotic directional convergence results for gradient descent from isolated minima to manifolds of non-isolated minima.
QABVjPgg8S.problem: Directional convergence of gradient descent has been characterized near isolated minima, but overparameterized models naturally exhibit non-isolated minima where Hessian eigendirections vary.
QABVjPgg8S.method: Under local regularity assumptions on a regular surface of minima, the authors prove a forward-invariant neighborhood with quantitative descent and characterize when trajectories exhibit a limiting or alternating convergence direction based on step size.
QABVjPgg8S.key_idea: Control tangential drift along a regular minimum manifold within a forward-invariant neighborhood to identify the dominant normal eigendirection and step-size threshold for directional convergence.
QABVjPgg8S.evidence: Theoretical proofs (Theorems 4.1 and 4.2) and illustrative experiments such as 0.5(xy-1)^2 support the analysis.
QABVjPgg8S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending directional convergence of gradient descent from isolated minima to non-isolated minimum manifolds is a natural and meaningful theoretical question.
QABVjPgg8S.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about strong or violated assumptions (such as Hessian rank > 1 excluding the motivating xy=1 example), proof details, and significance beyond existing local convergence theory.

G79QTIFU5P.one_liner: Proves minimax logarithmic regret bounds for unknown matching markets with ties and introduces an adaptive algorithm, ACTL.
G79QTIFU5P.problem: Two-sided matching markets with unknown preferences and exact ties lack sharp regret characterizations and adaptive algorithms that work without knowing the margin or tie pattern.
G79QTIFU5P.method: The authors characterize minimax regret via certificate and preservation margins, prove matching upper and lower bounds, and propose Aggregate Core-Tail Learning (ACTL) to adaptively test core and outside arms.
G79QTIFU5P.key_idea: Separate constant-loss core deviation tests from shortfall-adaptive outside-arm screening using certificate and preservation margins to attain optimal regret without knowing the minimum preference gap.
G79QTIFU5P.evidence: Theoretical matching upper and lower regret bounds and empirical evaluations of an ACTL-Practical variant support the work.
G79QTIFU5P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the matching upper and lower regret bounds separating core and tail exploration in markets with ties as a substantial theoretical result.
G79QTIFU5P.main_concern: Reviewers note poor writing with unexplained terminology, large remainder terms whose practical validity regime is unexplored, and recalibrated constants in the tested practical algorithm.

Lz755URdm1.one_liner: Exposes audit fibers—equivalent states under interface checks that alter downstream behavior—and compiles qualification-preserving FiberRouter attacks.
Lz755URdm1.problem: Model deployment pipelines qualify replaced or converted components only at declared interfaces, missing malicious state differences exploited by downstream consumers.
Lz755URdm1.method: The authors formalize audit fibers as states treated as equivalent by qualification checks, prove composition is unsafe when one fiber induces divergent downstream behavior, and derive FiberRouter, a fixed-weight/representation attack targeting normalized representations and KV-cache handoffs.
Lz755URdm1.key_idea: Exploiting directions in a component's output or KV cache that are ignored by interface qualification checks allows a fixed replacement to steer downstream consumers.
Lz755URdm1.evidence: Theoretical safety criteria and experiments across image/text representations, patched weights, stronger linear-probe checks, and a Qwen KV-cache handoff.
Lz755URdm1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the audit-fiber framing of compositional supply-chain security beyond standard backdoors interesting and well-motivated.
Lz755URdm1.main_concern: Reviewers note that strong targeted attacks assume extensive integrator-private knowledge of the downstream consumer, and question whether real deployment pipelines approve replacements using such narrow checks.

cEVgZFRKzv.one_liner: Learns continuous degradation-query momentum contrastive representations to retrieve and reuse historical restoration tool chains in agentic image restoration.
cEVgZFRKzv.problem: Agentic image restoration methods rely on coarse degradation labels that miss intra-type variations, causing suboptimal tool selection and costly rollbacks.
cEVgZFRKzv.method: LAIR trains a Degradation-Query Momentum Contrastive Encoder (DQ-MCE) using learnable degradation queries, cross-content momentum contrastive learning, and parameter-aware regularization. The agent uses these content-robust degradation embeddings to retrieve, rank, execute, and verify historical restoration tool chains.
cEVgZFRKzv.key_idea: Encodes fine-grained continuous degradation parameters via cross-content momentum contrastive queries to retrieve matching historical restoration tool chains.
cEVgZFRKzv.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic and real-world degraded images, including integration into 4KAgent and comparisons against AgenticIR.
cEVgZFRKzv.claimed_gains: Reduces runtime by up to 58% (from 156.91s to 65.90s per image in synthetic comparison) with fewer tool invocations than AgenticIR.
cEVgZFRKzv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree fine-grained degradation retrieval is practically motivated and delivers substantial runtime and tool-invocation reductions.
cEVgZFRKzv.main_concern: Reviewers find novelty incremental over SEAR/UtilityIR, note narrow retrieval ablations (100 rain-plus-dark images) without transfer-regret metrics, and request clearer online-memory evaluation rules.

WiVd0SKewn.one_liner: Distills students along a continuous spherical trajectory connecting a class-ranking skeleton to normalized teacher logits.
WiVd0SKewn.problem: Standard logit knowledge distillation couples class rankings and response magnitudes in a single target, limiting flexibility in how each is transferred.
WiVd0SKewn.method: RTKD builds a normalized ranking skeleton preserving teacher class order, connects it to the normalized teacher prediction via spherical interpolation, and integrates an adaptive Huber geodesic loss along the trajectory.
WiVd0SKewn.key_idea: Supervises student distillation by integrating geodesic discrepancies along a spherical trajectory between an order-preserving ranking skeleton and normalized teacher logits.
WiVd0SKewn.evidence: Image classification experiments and ablations on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1K.
WiVd0SKewn.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-1K, RTKD improves Top-1 accuracy from 70.49% with standard KD to 73.15% when distilling ResNet50.
WiVd0SKewn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation of separating class ordering from logit magnitudes clear and the spherical trajectory formulation intuitive.
WiVd0SKewn.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablation results show only a small gain for full RTKD (77.48%) over simply using the normalized teacher endpoint (77.00%) or prior mean point (77.14%).

YFX9oHUV5P.one_liner: Evolves diverse item-plus-hypothesis recommendations using a contextual bandit, an LLM proposer, and a quality-diversity archive.
YFX9oHUV5P.problem: High-stakes decision-making benefits from diverse recommendations paired with supporting reasons rather than a single ranked item list.
YFX9oHUV5P.method: QD-Rec selects items via a contextual bandit, uses a foundation model to generate natural-language recommendation hypotheses conditioned on archived examples, and retains entries in a local archive if they are novel or outperform their nearest neighbor.
YFX9oHUV5P.key_idea: Combines contextual-bandit item selection with LLM hypothesis evolution and local nearest-neighbor quality-diversity archive replacement.
YFX9oHUV5P.evidence: Evaluated across M&A, customer targeting, paper recommendation, and Goodreads book recommendation with matched budgets and component ablations.
YFX9oHUV5P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the item-hypothesis quality-diversity formulation creative, interpretable, and simple.
YFX9oHUV5P.main_concern: Reviewers highlight circular evaluation (the same LLM judge guides bandit/archive updates and scores final quality without human validation in most domains) and missing learning baselines.

teyeG0CnPx.one_liner: Discovers metric-induced Gaussian prior anchors, ranks them by first-step denoising velocity, and spherically averages top anchors.
teyeG0CnPx.problem: Existing initial-noise optimization methods for conditional generation are tailored to specific regimes or objectives, limiting cross-task adaptability.
teyeG0CnPx.method: Prior Subspace Recomposition (PSR) distills metric-induced superior Gaussian regions into reusable prior anchors, trains a lightweight local ranker on first-step denoising velocity fields, resolves global anchor orderings via graph optimization at inference, and spherically averages top anchors.
teyeG0CnPx.key_idea: Ranks offline-discovered Gaussian prior anchors via a first-step velocity ranker and graph optimization, then spherically averages top anchors for condition-aware initialization.
teyeG0CnPx.evidence: Evaluated across T2I, T2V, and I2V tasks, multiple generative backbones, and evaluation metrics with selection ablations.
teyeG0CnPx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework clearly written, unified across T2I/T2V/I2V without modifying backbones, and empirically consistent over random initialization.
teyeG0CnPx.main_concern: Reviewers note missing baselines (InitNO, FreeInit, NoiseQuery), lack of a random-anchor-pool control to isolate offline anchor discovery, and extra offline/inference compute cost.

hFRPKRZXeS.one_liner: Builds a training-free image restoration agent using a hierarchical, self-evolving experience pool to guide tool and order selection.
hFRPKRZXeS.problem: Zero-shot MLLM image restoration agents incur heavy trial-and-error tool-call overhead under coupled degradations without prior experience.
hFRPKRZXeS.method: E2IR-Agent organizes tool selection, degradation removal order, and quality preferences into a three-level hierarchical experience pool updated via a self-evolving mechanism driven by image quality assessment metrics.
hFRPKRZXeS.key_idea: Maintains a training-free, three-level hierarchical experience pool updated from accumulated restoration records to guide tool choice and removal order.
hFRPKRZXeS.evidence: Experiments on synthetic and real-world compound image restoration settings measuring full-reference IQA metrics and tool invocation counts.
hFRPKRZXeS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that modeling tool selection, removal order, and quality preferences in a reusable experience pool effectively reduces inference tool calls.
hFRPKRZXeS.main_concern: The paper omits the heavy offline cost of exhaustive trajectory exploration when building the experience pool and relies on overlapping IQA metrics for evolution and evaluation.

aKI9r8b0he.one_liner: Uses a VLM to plan causally ordered keyframes and 2D object trajectories as soft latent guidance for video diffusion.
aKI9r8b0he.problem: Pretrained video diffusion models model local motion well but lack long-horizon physical consistency and causal plausibility.
aKI9r8b0he.method: CausalMotion prompts a VLM to generate intermediate scene keyframes and object-centric 2D trajectories, aligns them temporally via IoU, and injects them as soft latent blending constraints into a frozen video diffusion model at inference.
aKI9r8b0he.key_idea: Decouples physical reasoning via VLM-generated keyframes and 2D object trajectories aligned as soft latent constraints during video diffusion inference.
aKI9r8b0he.evidence: Evaluated on PhyGenBench and VBench with ablations on keyframe and trajectory components.
aKI9r8b0he.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the training-free decoupling of VLM state/trajectory planning from video generation clear, modular, and easy to follow.
aKI9r8b0he.main_concern: Reviewers view the method as an incremental combination of VChain (keyframes) and VLIPP (trajectories), noting small gains (0.05 over VLIPP; 0.01 in ablations) driven mostly by keyframes and limited to 2D boxes.

T3KGhnOUL6.one_liner: Trains a red-teaming controller with reward-weighted SFT and DPO to pair safe text with harmful audio prompts.
T3KGhnOUL6.problem: Text-only red-teaming misses vulnerabilities in large audio-language models where safe text queries combine with audio to trigger harmful compliance.
T3KGhnOUL6.method: ARENA trains a controller via reward-weighted SFT and DPO over closed-loop target feedback, generating safe text queries (checked by Llama Guard 3) and speech/sound variants evaluated by MD-Judge.
T3KGhnOUL6.key_idea: Optimizes an iterative red-teaming controller with reward-weighted SFT and DPO using two-sided text-input and audio-output moderation feedback.
T3KGhnOUL6.evidence: Evaluated on 520 AdvBench objectives across Audio Flamingo 3, Qwen2-Audio, MiMo-Audio, and GPT-Audio, plus cross-model transfer.
T3KGhnOUL6.claimed_gains: Achieves 87.9%, 74.2%, and 68.1% MD-Judge ASR on Audio Flamingo 3, Qwen2-Audio, and MiMo-Audio at 100.0% prompt-pass rate, and 76.5% ASR on GPT-Audio.
T3KGhnOUL6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that audio-grounded attacks paired with safe text expose a realistic, underexplored safety surface across four LALMs.
T3KGhnOUL6.main_concern: Reviewers point out an unfair search-budget comparison (ARENA uses up to 30 iterative attempts and 16 speech variants vs. single-shot static baselines) and insufficient proof that audio drives the jailbreak.

XTp6gxQzmK.one_liner: Freezes low-entropy predictions via selective absorption in uniform discrete flow sampling to prevent destructive token overwrites.
XTp6gxQzmK.problem: Uniform discrete flow permits repeated token revisions that frequently overwrite correct intermediate predictions with later errors.
XTp6gxQzmK.method: LEDFlow introduces selective absorption into uniform discrete flow without retraining, preserving flow velocity at active positions while freezing the lowest-entropy predictions at each step based on an error-decomposition bound.
XTp6gxQzmK.key_idea: Adaptively absorbs lowest-entropy token positions during uniform discrete flow sampling while maintaining velocity updates on remaining positions.
XTp6gxQzmK.evidence: Theoretical error-decomposition analysis and evaluations on Nikoli Sudoku, text-to-image generation, and multimodal understanding.
XTp6gxQzmK.claimed_gains: Attains 0.845 Nikoli Sudoku solve accuracy compared with 0.410 for non-absorbing uniform flow.
XTp6gxQzmK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the motivation to prevent destructive overwrites in uniform discrete flow is clear and empirical results across domains are strong.
XTp6gxQzmK.main_concern: Reviewers cite inconsistent Sudoku baseline numbers across tables, unverified theoretical regularity assumptions, and poor writing clarity.

JeXVn3jwzP.one_liner: Progressively refines spatio-temporal forecasts across scales by decomposing residuals into coarse updates and zero-aggregate detail.
JeXVn3jwzP.problem: Direct spatio-temporal forecasters leave the relationship between coarse future structure and fine-grained detail implicit without explicit revision control.
JeXVn3jwzP.method: ProST defines forecast states across a temporal-spatial scale space and uses a shared scale-conditioned forecaster to decompose corrections into a weighted coarse update and zero-aggregate detail satisfying an exact cross-scale identity. A history-conditioned selector picks the refinement scale sequence upfront.
JeXVn3jwzP.key_idea: Decomposes multi-scale forecast corrections into coarse updates and zero-aggregate detail along a history-selected refinement path.
JeXVn3jwzP.evidence: Evaluated on four traffic and air-quality spatio-temporal forecasting benchmarks with matched retraining interventions.
JeXVn3jwzP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the algebraic coarse-versus-detail decomposition clear and the fixed-sequence forecasting results competitive across benchmarks.
JeXVn3jwzP.main_concern: Reviewers note the history-conditioned scale selector fails to consistently beat random selection, and spatial/joint interventions are missing.

1oYdPNHXF3.one_liner: Solves low-Knudsen BGK kinetic equations using Chapman-Enskog solution ansatze and shock-aligned lifting in separable PINNs.
1oYdPNHXF3.problem: Existing physics-informed neural networks for BGK kinetic equations struggle in low-Knudsen-number regimes due to rapid kinetic relaxation and sharp, evolving shock layers.
1oYdPNHXF3.method: KF-SPINN encodes fast relaxation via a Chapman-Enskog-inspired exponential solution ansatz (CE-ramp), adds multiscale time-modulated lifting features aligned with shock geometry, and trains with conservation and entropy-transport residuals under a self-adaptive Charbonnier penalty.
1oYdPNHXF3.key_idea: Combines a Chapman-Enskog-inspired exponential relaxation ansatz with shock-aligned lifting features and conservation residuals inside a separable PINN.
1oYdPNHXF3.evidence: Experiments evaluate 1D3V shock benchmarks and a radially symmetric 2D Riemann problem over five runs with reference-grid refinement checks and ablations.
1oYdPNHXF3.claimed_gains: KF-SPINN reduces mean macroscopic prediction errors by up to two orders of magnitude on 1D3V shock benchmarks relative to the strongest baseline evaluated.
1oYdPNHXF3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree KF-SPINN achieves strong empirical error reductions in low-Knudsen 1D shock problems and uses physically motivated structure.
1oYdPNHXF3.main_concern: Reviewers view the methodological novelty as incremental combinations of existing techniques, note limited 1D/2D validation, and find that simultaneous engineering changes obscure the source of gains.

tOa7vAROMh.one_liner: Aligns protein language model representations with templated interaction text and residue-level binding geometry via CLIP-style contrastive pretraining.
tOa7vAROMh.problem: Protein language models are ligand-agnostic and fail to capture explicit protein-ligand interaction semantics for 3D complex structure prediction.
tOa7vAROMh.method: The authors build the PLI-TD dataset by translating structured PLIP profiles into natural-language descriptions, then pretrain PLI-CLIP with contrastive alignment and per-residue binding geometry prediction to produce transferable modules for docking models.
tOa7vAROMh.key_idea: Uses CLIP-style contrastive alignment between protein features and templated PLIP interaction text alongside per-residue binding geometry prediction.
tOa7vAROMh.evidence: The transferable module is evaluated on three different docking models with ablations on textual representations and objective components.
tOa7vAROMh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note the framework is straightforward and addresses transferring interaction supervision into docking representations without requiring annotations at inference.
tOa7vAROMh.main_concern: Reviewers question whether converting structured PLIP records into natural language provides any advantage over directly encoding the structured interaction data.

NZsxSFHE0t.one_liner: Encodes multi-view driving images into unified 3D scene tokens via deformable cross-attention for joint reconstruction and occupancy prediction.
NZsxSFHE0t.problem: Existing 2D and monocular visual tokenizers are inefficient and inter-view inconsistent when applied to high-resolution multi-view autonomous driving scenes.
NZsxSFHE0t.method: DriveTok extracts features from vision foundation models and aggregates them into compact 3D scene tokens via 3D deformable cross-attention. A multi-view transformer decoder with Plücker ray embeddings and visibility-guided attention reconstructs RGB, depth, and semantics alongside a direct 3D semantic occupancy head.
NZsxSFHE0t.key_idea: Aggregating multi-view foundation-model features into 3D scene tokens via deformable cross-attention trained jointly on multi-view reconstruction and 3D occupancy.
NZsxSFHE0t.evidence: Experiments on multi-view image reconstruction, semantic segmentation, depth prediction, and 3D semantic occupancy prediction.
NZsxSFHE0t.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying multi-view reconstruction and 3D scene understanding into a shared driving representation is a well-written, appealing direction.
NZsxSFHE0t.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over standard BEV encoders (e.g., BEVFormer deformable attention) and lack of controlled comparisons or compression-efficiency analysis against BEV baselines.

G63Gaaygba.one_liner: Restores dominant-strategy incentive compatibility in auto-bidding meta-games via an end-of-day rebate over an unchanged first-price auction.
G63Gaaygba.problem: In auto-bidding meta-games where advertisers report high-level targets like tCPA, truthful per-impression auctions do not prevent target misreporting.
G63Gaaygba.method: The authors formalize the auto-bidding meta-game as a Myerson single-parameter environment and design a deployable DSIC mechanism using an end-of-day rebate that returns information rent while keeping the first-price auction untouched. For practical deployment, they estimate the allocation curve offline and prove approximate DSIC bounds under uniform estimation error.
G63Gaaygba.key_idea: Applying a Myerson-style end-of-day rebate on top of an unchanged first-price auction using an offline-estimated allocation curve.
G63Gaaygba.evidence: Theoretical proofs (Theorems 1 and 3, Proposition 2), second-price numerical audits, and online A/B and surrogate experiments.
G63Gaaygba.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating per-auction incentives from target-reporting incentives and preserving auction ranking via end-of-day settlements is practically appealing.
G63Gaaygba.main_concern: Reviewers note that the exact mechanism is standard Myerson theory, budget constraints are omitted, and key experiments validate best responses against a proxy objective constructed from the same estimated allocation.

2EB2oSRU0P.one_liner: Constrains cross-view MLLM attention using camera-ray and epipolar geometry supervised by depth-derived soft correspondences.
2EB2oSRU0P.problem: Existing geometry-aware MLLMs enrich individual visual tokens with 3D cues but leave cross-view correspondences to emerge implicitly from appearance-driven attention.
2EB2oSRU0P.method: GeoMLLM equips each visual patch with a camera-ray representation and applies pairwise ray and epipolar cues to constrain which tokens can attend across views. During training, depth-derived soft correspondences supervise cross-view attention to route information between observations of the same physical scene region.
2EB2oSRU0P.key_idea: Constraining cross-view visual attention with pairwise camera-ray epipolar cues and supervising attention maps with depth-derived correspondences.
2EB2oSRU0P.evidence: Built on Qwen3-VL-4B and evaluated on SPAR-Bench and additional multi-image and 3D spatial reasoning benchmarks.
2EB2oSRU0P.claimed_gains: Reaches 83.79 overall on SPAR-Bench, with 83.49 on multi-view tasks (+20.86 points) and 88.13 on Cross-view Perception (+25.12 points).
2EB2oSRU0P.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that explicitly injecting epipolar geometric constraints into cross-view MLLM attention is well-motivated and yields strong empirical performance.
2EB2oSRU0P.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient methodological details and component ablations, plus missing controlled comparisons against prior geometry-aware attention mechanisms under matched training settings.

doLS1jnQG3.one_liner: Decides prompt-customized layer-wise activation sparsity budgets during LLM prefill using an RL controller for zero-overhead static sparse decoding.
doLS1jnQG3.problem: Static activation sparsity hurts complex reasoning, while token-level dynamic routing incurs prohibitive hardware context-switching overhead during autoregressive decoding.
doLS1jnQG3.method: During the compute-bound prefill phase, an RL-trained Macro Controller allocates layer-wise sparsity budgets based on prompt complexity via Dense-Guided Policy Optimization, and a deterministic Micro Router distributes budgets across intra-layer modules. The resulting prompt-customized sparsity configuration becomes a static sparse execution graph during decoding.
doLS1jnQG3.key_idea: Front-loading prompt-conditioned RL sparsity budget allocation into prefill so autoregressive decoding runs as a static sparse graph.
doLS1jnQG3.evidence: Evaluated across LLM families including LLaMA on general and reasoning tasks (e.g., GSM8K) with prompt-free controls and BS=1 speedup measurements.
doLS1jnQG3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that shifting sparsity allocation decisions into the prefill phase addresses a practical decoding-overhead bottleneck.
doLS1jnQG3.main_concern: Reviewers question compatibility with continuous batching beyond batch size 1, note close similarity to WAS without proving RL's advantage over simpler allocators, and observe severe GSM8K degradation at high sparsity.

3scN3irlLE.one_liner: Combines multi-teacher distillation with a three-stage Imitation, Reflection, and Transcendence RL pipeline for LLM machine translation.
3scN3irlLE.problem: Standard knowledge distillation bounds compact machine translation students by the performance ceiling of their larger teacher LLMs.
3scN3irlLE.method: SaKD distills from multiple teacher LLMs and then applies a three-stage pipeline—Imitation, Reflection (preference optimization), and Transcendence (GRPO with a teacher-relative reward formulation)—to enable smaller students to surpass their teachers.
3scN3irlLE.key_idea: Follows multi-teacher distillation with staged Imitation, Reflection preference optimization, and Transcendence GRPO to push translation students past teacher quality.
3scN3irlLE.evidence: Evaluated across four translation directions and two student sizes using automatic metrics (BLEU, COMET) and professional human direct assessment.
3scN3irlLE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem well motivated, the three-stage framework coherent, and the automatic and human evaluation gains over teachers empirically consistent.
3scN3irlLE.main_concern: Reviewers show mathematically that subtracting the constant best-teacher score in Transcendence GRPO cancels out during group advantage normalization, and note an unfair budget comparison against un-tuned teachers.

YrMltsTzZM.one_liner: Encodes 16 fps videos into causal variable-length anchor and incremental frame tokens supervised by multi-truncation reconstruction.
YrMltsTzZM.problem: High-frame-rate video encoding preserves fine motion and identity details but creates heavy token redundancy when every frame is encoded independently at fixed length.
YrMltsTzZM.method: NativeCodec combines complete anchor (I) frames with variable-length incremental (P) frame token suffixes trained via pixel and feature reconstruction at multiple truncation lengths, paired with an offline reconstruction-supervised length predictor and cumulative-length anchor placement; the authors also introduce BallBench.
YrMltsTzZM.key_idea: Concentrates new frame information into variable-length causal token suffixes via multi-truncation reconstruction and uses an offline reconstruction teacher to supervise per-frame token length.
YrMltsTzZM.evidence: Evaluated with a 4B base model on TimeLens-Bench, MomentSeeker, BallBench, and additional video benchmarks across multiple token budgets.
YrMltsTzZM.claimed_gains: With a 4B base model and a fixed suffix ratio, NativeCodec reaches 56.4 mIoU on TimeLens-Bench and 25.0 mIoU on MomentSeeker (plus 26.1% on a metric truncated in the abstract).
YrMltsTzZM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the causal I/P-frame variable-length token design, strong performance under tight token budgets, and the diagnostic BallBench benchmark.
YrMltsTzZM.main_concern: Reviewers note that the learned length predictor degrades performance on five of seven benchmarks compared to a fixed 1/16 suffix ratio, and question whether simple high-fps pooling controls would match the gains.

TyAXKrky6y.one_liner: Adapts SNN online eligibility-trace decay per layer and sample by least-squares projection of the postsynaptic temporal Jacobian.
TyAXKrky6y.problem: BPTT for spiking neural networks incurs memory linear in time steps, while compact online presynaptic eligibility traces use fixed or presynaptic-only decay that mismatches postsynaptic dynamics.
TyAXKrky6y.method: Dynamics-Projected Eligibility Traces (DPET) projects each layer's postsynaptic temporal Jacobian onto a single least-squares scalar decay coefficient per sample, extends to richer neuron states via state-space dynamics, and adds an auxiliary objective using later-step predictions from completed minibatches.
TyAXKrky6y.key_idea: Projects the postsynaptic temporal Jacobian onto one least-squares scalar decay per sample and layer to preserve a single compact presynaptic eligibility trace.
TyAXKrky6y.evidence: Gradient analysis and experiments across image, event-based, point-cloud, and language classification benchmarks comparing accuracy and memory against online SNN methods and BPTT.
TyAXKrky6y.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DPET is a clean, low-memory online SNN training rule with thorough gradient analysis and competitive benchmark accuracy.
TyAXKrky6y.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the lack of genuinely temporal benchmarks (relying mostly on static or static-derived image tasks with few time steps), missing activation-checkpointing BPTT memory baselines, and unweighted Jacobian projection across neurons.

qBs7UNmnAz.one_liner: Benchmarks neural fluid predictors and hybrid receding-horizon controllers for energy-efficient body motion in CFD-simulated channels.
qBs7UNmnAz.problem: Coordinating body motion with coupled fluid-structure forces for energy-efficient control is difficult and lacks unified comparisons across predictors, control modes, and geometries.
qBs7UNmnAz.method: The authors generate a CFD dataset spanning two body shapes, three channel geometries, and sensor-free or sensor-based settings, and compare physical predictors and direct-trajectory or force-and-torque controllers—including hybrid planning combining a learned predictor with a rigid-body fallback—evaluated in OpenFOAM.
qBs7UNmnAz.key_idea: Evaluates neural flow predictors paired with direct-trajectory, force-torque, and hybrid receding-horizon controllers directly inside a CFD solver across geometries and sensing regimes.
qBs7UNmnAz.evidence: CFD-verified experiments in OpenFOAM across two body shapes, three channel geometries, and sensor-free versus sensor-based control settings.
qBs7UNmnAz.claimed_gains: Uses up to 25.7% less work than the best training trajectories for sensor-free circular-body control, and 36.4% (unobstructed), 65.6% (central-obstacle), and 32.3% (two-wall) less work for sensor-based square-body control under hybrid planning.
qBs7UNmnAz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate verifying executed controls directly in CFD and transparently reporting negative results such as complete failure of sensor-free square-body control.
qBs7UNmnAz.main_concern: Reviewers question physical realism (prescribed trajectories or unactuated imposed forces in low-Re 2D flow), confounded hybrid-planning comparisons lacking a constant-load MPC baseline, and selection bias without uncertainty estimates.

E2atTuJMD2.one_liner: Benchmarks biosecurity risks across protein generator architectures and applies NPO and GRPO weight-level unlearning defenses.
E2atTuJMD2.problem: Protein-generative models pose dual-use biosecurity risks, yet risk quantification and weight-level unlearning defenses have not been systematically compared across autoregressive, inverse-folding, and masked-diffusion architectures.
E2atTuJMD2.method: SafeProtein++ evaluates five protein generators (1.66M–1.4B parameters) on a homology-cluster-disjoint panel of 854 proteins under shared masking, folding, and judging protocols, and compares negative preference optimization (NPO) against group relative policy optimization (GRPO) for weight-level unlearning.
E2atTuJMD2.key_idea: Applies unified homology-disjoint red-teaming across three protein-generator families and compares NPO versus GRPO weight-level unlearning on hazardous mask recovery and structural quality.
E2atTuJMD2.evidence: Evaluated five released generators across six mask-by-ratio conditions on 854 proteins plus complementary amylin aggregation tests.
E2atTuJMD2.claimed_gains: NPO reduces the mean hazardous mask-recovery rate to at most 1.7% on every evaluated model, while GRPO better preserves predicted structural quality.
E2atTuJMD2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value unifying red-teaming and unlearning across autoregressive, inverse-folding, and masked-diffusion protein models with homology-disjoint splits.
E2atTuJMD2.main_concern: Reviewers note that RMSD/retrieval hazard proxies miss functional similarity, that open-weight tamper resistance after fine-tuning is untested, and that writing and beam-search attack protocols have flaws.

KeJCdUcpKR.one_liner: Selects problem-specific numerical solvers inside decoupled diffusion iterations to enforce operator-aware measurement consistency with fewer evaluations.
KeJCdUcpKR.problem: Diffusion inverse-problem solvers typically apply a uniform measurement-correction step regardless of differences in forward operators and numerical conditioning.
KeJCdUcpKR.method: DiffOps decouples diffusion prior denoising from measurement consistency and applies classical operator-aware numerical solvers (e.g., CG, DR-to-GD staging) tailored to each inverse problem's operator structure and noise model within diffusion iterations.
KeJCdUcpKR.key_idea: Integrates operator-specific classical numerical solvers directly into decoupled diffusion-prior iterations based on forward-operator structure and noise characteristics.
KeJCdUcpKR.evidence: Evaluated across linear and nonlinear image restoration and scientific imaging inverse problems against competing diffusion solvers.
KeJCdUcpKR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear writing, comprehensive evaluation across diverse linear/nonlinear operators and scientific imaging, and strong phase-retrieval staging.
KeJCdUcpKR.main_concern: Reviewers note heavy overlap with uncited/undiscussed prior optimization-based diffusion solvers (DDfire, DDS, ReSample) and observe that FFHQ results do not consistently beat baselines.

BybP7V7Q8F.one_liner: Calibration-aware 100M encoder building a shared multi-camera geometric memory for dense metric depth and sparse 4D point-motion queries.
BybP7V7Q8F.problem: Autonomous driving stacks require metric scene geometry that downstream planners can query directly without re-running reconstruction or test-time scale alignment.
BybP7V7Q8F.method: GeoAct trains a ~100M-parameter calibration-aware encoder from projected LiDAR and monocular pseudo-labels to build a shared geometric memory from multi-camera histories. A DPT-style head reads dense metric depth/point maps, while a sparse query head predicts where any pixel surface moves at a target timestamp; a frozen encoder feeds a DrivoR planner.
BybP7V7Q8F.key_idea: Builds one calibration-aware multi-camera geometric memory supporting both dense metric depth readout and sparse cross-time surface point queries.
BybP7V7Q8F.evidence: Evaluated on NAVSIM/OpenScene metric depth and frozen-encoder DrivoR planning, plus controlled continuation ablations dropping dense or motion supervision.
BybP7V7Q8F.claimed_gains: Reaches 0.1093 AbsRel on NAVSIM/OpenScene with no test-time scale alignment (beating GeoX even with oracle scale) and 91.78 PDMS with a frozen encoder versus 90.83 for frozen GeoX.
BybP7V7Q8F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clear writing, compact 100M metric-depth performance without test-time alignment, and controlled supervision-dropping ablations.
BybP7V7Q8F.main_concern: Reviewers flag unfair camera/frame input budgets versus GeoX, missing a frozen DINOv3 baseline without geometric pretraining to prove planning benefit, single-seed results, and lack of pose-noise ablations.

MvNsm397vM.one_liner: Benchmarks global workflow orchestration versus step-by-step agents on 650 enterprise SOPs and tests incremental construction, feedback revision, and training.
MvNsm397vM.problem: Generating complete executable workflows upfront (global orchestration) cuts LLM calls relative to step-by-step interaction, but its accuracy gap and remedies are poorly quantified.
MvNsm397vM.method: AgentOrch compares global orchestration and step-by-step interaction under matched tools and environments across 650 enterprise SOPs and 3,220 runtime variants. It evaluates three gap-closing mechanisms: incremental workflow construction, execution-feedback revision of complete workflows, and targeted SFT/training.
MvNsm397vM.key_idea: Compares upfront workflow generation against step-by-step tool use on matched executable enterprise SOPs and evaluates incremental building, feedback revision, and SFT.
MvNsm397vM.evidence: Evaluated across 650 enterprise SOPs and 3,220 runtime variants across early and recent LLMs, including held-out runtime variants and SFT.
MvNsm397vM.claimed_gains: The global-vs-step-by-step gap shrinks ~79% on recent models; incremental construction adds +9.98 pp, execution-feedback revision adds +6.13 pp on held-out variants, and SFT adds +10.29 pp Orchestration Accuracy.
MvNsm397vM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled executable comparison between global and step-by-step protocols on shared enterprise SOPs and diagnostic revision analyses.
MvNsm397vM.main_concern: Reviewers note that Orchestration Accuracy penalizes valid alternative workflows that deviate from reference traces, findings are somewhat intuitive, and evaluation is limited to simulated Workato workflows with fixed schemas.

6IuZfDGv6D.one_liner: Fuses SSL global speech features with local signal artifacts via Hierarchical Adaptive Gating for cross-domain speech deepfake detection.
6IuZfDGv6D.problem: Self-supervised speech deepfake detectors overfit to source domains because they miss fine-grained local spoofing artifacts and use static layer aggregation under OOD layer-importance shifts.
6IuZfDGv6D.method: GLAD combines a Hierarchical Global-Local (HGL) backbone fusing global SSL representations with local CNN signal features and a Hierarchical Adaptive Gating (HAG) mechanism that dynamically recalibrates SSL layer weights per sample, alongside SaniBoost augmentation.
6IuZfDGv6D.key_idea: Fuses global SSL features with local signal branches and applies sample-specific Hierarchical Adaptive Gating to recalibrate SSL layer importance.
6IuZfDGv6D.evidence: Trained on ASVspoof 2019 LA and evaluated across five OOD speech deepfake benchmarks with multi-seed and parameter-matched ablations.
6IuZfDGv6D.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the strong cross-domain detection performance, comprehensive multi-benchmark validation, and controlled parameter-matched/multi-seed ablations.
6IuZfDGv6D.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains over Sensitive Layer Selection (SLS) and SaniBoost augmentation are not cleanly isolated in main comparisons, and causal claims about OOD failure roots exceed experimental proof.

V7eSad5SEy.one_liner: Compiles language failure intents into rule programs, explores safe responses via GRPO, and renders RGB trajectories for VLA driving post-training.
V7eSad5SEy.problem: Rare safety-critical driving interactions are underrepresented in naturalistic logs and hard to collect deliberately as driving policies evolve.
V7eSad5SEy.method: Scenarist compiles natural-language failure-scenario intents into rule programs with deterministic validity checks, connects responsive traffic simulation with GRPO-based safe-response exploration, and synthesizes trajectory-conditioned RGB video. Positive safe responses train VLA policies via SFT while negative responses train RL routing; the benchmark has 16,397 interactions (including rendered Scenarist-2K).
V7eSad5SEy.key_idea: Compiles language intents into validated traffic rule programs, uses GRPO to discover safe responses, and renders action-aligned RGB supervision for VLA post-training.
V7eSad5SEy.evidence: 16,397 interactions across eight vehicle/pedestrian failure intents (2,144 rendered in Scenarist-2K) plus VLA SFT/RL post-training and WOMD validation.
V7eSad5SEy.claimed_gains: Response policy cuts collision rate from 36.70% to 6.23%; VLA post-training cuts collision rate from 24.96% to 1.42% and raises safe rate from 74.77% to 98.58%.
V7eSad5SEy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the end-to-end integration from language-compiled rule primitives to GRPO safe-response discovery and visual VLA supervision.
V7eSad5SEy.main_concern: Reviewers flag lack of implementation details preventing reproducibility of the LLM/GRPO/routing modules, and note that VLA evaluation uses non-reactive logged agents rather than true closed-loop testing.

bQjLCHio4j.one_liner: Organizes multiview 3D geometry into reliability-aware physical groups and fuses question-conditioned local memory with a global spatial prefix.
bQjLCHio4j.problem: Spatial MLLMs struggle to consolidate repeated multiview geometric observations without losing view-specific details or sacrificing either question-relevant detail or global layout.
bQjLCHio4j.method: GS-MLLM groups consistent multiview geometric observations into reliability-aware physical groups retaining source-view evidence, retrieves local detail via question-conditioned semantic memory, and summarizes global layout via an adaptive spatial prefix. Frame-aligned cross-attention injects retrieved geometry into pretrained pixel-token states.
bQjLCHio4j.key_idea: Consolidates multiview geometry into reliability-aware physical groups and injects question-conditioned local retrieval plus a global spatial prefix via frame-aligned cross-attention.
bQjLCHio4j.evidence: Evaluated with Qwen2.5-VL-3B and Qwen3-VL-4B on VSI-Bench and four additional spatial reasoning benchmarks (ViewSpatial, MindCube, etc.) with ablations.
bQjLCHio4j.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-VL-4B, GS-MLLM achieves 54.7 on VSI-Bench (+3.1 points over previous best) and a 2.6-point average gain over GeoThinker across four additional spatial benchmarks.
bQjLCHio4j.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find organizing multiview geometry into cross-view physical groups with local retrieval and global context intuitive and broadly evaluated.
bQjLCHio4j.main_concern: Reviewers flag inaccurate GeoThinker baseline reporting (using a suboptimal rho=0.75 ablation row instead of the main result), limited novelty over SparseVLM/GeoThinker, and uncontrolled token-budget ablations.

PWwYfQ3cuu.one_liner: Robot world model projecting joint trajectories into camera view, carrying action-updated state across chunks, and training with paired branch supervision.
PWwYfQ3cuu.problem: Robot world models often generate visually plausible futures that ignore action differences, failing to reflect physical outcomes needed for reliable policy evaluation.
PWwYfQ3cuu.method: ActionTrace projects robot joint trajectories into the camera view for spatial grounding, carries an action-updated consequence state across video segments, and trains with same-reset paired branch supervision favoring executed controls over alternative actions.
PWwYfQ3cuu.key_idea: Combines camera-projected kinematic grounding, cross-chunk action-updated consequence state, and same-reset paired-action outcome supervision in a robot world model.
PWwYfQ3cuu.evidence: Evaluated on paired action interventions, four trained policies across 50 manipulation tasks, five released policies on WorldArena, and real-world transfer.
PWwYfQ3cuu.claimed_gains: Recovers policy ordering with 0.9805 Pearson correlation across four policies on 50 manipulation tasks and 0.9920 Pearson correlation across five policies on WorldArena.
PWwYfQ3cuu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value targeting faithful action consequences for policy evaluation, strong policy-ranking correlations, and thorough component ablations.
PWwYfQ3cuu.main_concern: Reviewers flag low paired-outcome accuracy (<50% on 24 simple pairs), an unresolved label-consistency issue in recursive paired-branch supervision, and missing kinematic-grounding baselines.
